<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;text-align:justify">Provided that, the Argentine federal government and the Argentine provinces must exercise their rights pursuant to the following principles: (a)&#160;the strategic contribution of YPF S.A. to the achievement of the objectives set forth in the Expropriation Law; (b)&#160;the administration of YPF S.A. pursuant to the industry&#8217;s best practices and corporate governance, safeguarding shareholders&#8217; interests and generating value on their behalf; and (c)&#160;the professional management of YPF S.A. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">You can find a copy of an English translation of the Expropriation Law in the report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">6-K</span> furnished by YPF S.A. to the SEC on May&#160;9, 2012. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, on February&#160;25, 2014, the Argentine Republic and Repsol reached an agreement (&#8220;Repsol Agreement&#8221;) in relation to compensation for the expropriation of 200,589,525 of YPF S.A.&#8217;s Class&#160;D shares pursuant to the Expropriation Law. Under the Repsol Agreement, Repsol accepted US$ 5.0&#160;billion in sovereign bonds from the Argentine Republic and withdrew judicial and arbitral claims it had filed, including claims against YPF S.A., and waived additional claims. YPF S.A. and Repsol also executed a separate agreement (&#8220;Repsol Arrangement&#8221;) on February&#160;27, 2014, pursuant to which YPF S.A. and Repsol each withdrew, subject to certain exclusions, all present and future actions and/or claims based on causes occurring prior to the date of execution of the Repsol Arrangement arising from the expropriation of the YPF S.A. shares owned by Repsol pursuant to the Expropriation Law, including the intervention of YPF S.A. and the temporary occupation for public purposes of 51% of Repsol&#180;s capital stock in YPF S.A. Repsol and YPF S.A. agreed to withdraw reciprocal actions and claims with respect to third parties and/or pursued by them and to grant a series of mutual indemnities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">See &#8220;Item 7. Major shareholders and related party transactions&#8221; for details on our current major shareholders. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Legal nature of YPF S.A. </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">According to the Expropriation Law, YPF S.A. shall continue to operate as a publicly traded corporation pursuant to the Argentine General Corporations Law and its corresponding regulations and shall not be subject to any legislation or regulation applicable to the management or control of companies or entities owned by the Argentine federal government or provincial governments. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">See &#8220;Item 7. Major shareholders and related party transactions&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;The Argentine Republic owns 51% of the shares of YPF S.A.&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We face risks relating to legal proceedings which may cause significant costs and losses&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_14"><span style="font-style:italic">Overview </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF operates mainly in Argentina (see &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;Our business is largely dependent upon economic conditions in Argentina&#8221;) and most of our revenues are primarily derived from the sales in the Argentine domestic market. Additionally, in 2024, our main expenditures were related to investments in unconventional fields with the objective of growing production and reserves, and in the maintenance and/or investment in our downstream business, among others, as well as royalties and taxes related to our operations and the payment of interest related to our financial debt. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_15"><span style="font-style:italic">Business strategy </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our strategy has evolved over the last few years to prioritize the monetization of our vast unconventional hydrocarbon resources. Over the last 10 years, we have invested significantly in the Vaca Muerta formation together with our international and local partners, gaining experience, incorporating technology and adapting processes to become competitive on a global scale. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Having achieved competitive efficiency levels on both capital and operating expenditures, we now have the opportunity to accelerate the development of our shale resources. This has become even more relevant in the current geopolitical context in which the world demands affordable, reliable and sustainable energy, increasing the attractiveness of becoming a net exporter of crude oil and, in the medium term, capitalizing the opportunity to become a relevant LNG exporter. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Therefore, we will continue to focus our efforts on our most profitable business, the Vaca Muerta formation, given its level of recoverable resources. Furthermore, we continue actively managing our portfolio with a capital allocation discipline, reallocating resources from other less profitable businesses. In that sense, we keep on reducing our exposure to conventional mature fields (see &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may fail to execute in whole or in part our disposal plan related to mature fields (&#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221;)&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">While accelerating the growth potential of our shale resources, we also remain focused on maintaining high standards with regards to the health and safety of our people and the communities we work in, reducing our carbon footprint, and remaining focused on securing further efficiencies in all of our operations, including refining/processing of crude oil and natural gas and the distribution and marketing of hydrocarbons and derivative products, which position us as the leading integrated energy company in Argentina. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We intend to strengthen our competitiveness and timely adaptation to the trends that are taking place in the global energy space and that would have a decisive impact in the coming decades, such as decarbonization and electrification, as well as those that aim to increase the efficiency of hydrocarbons production and processing. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Strategic pillars: &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221; </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, we launched our plan named &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221;, which is based on YPF&#8217;s long-term strategy and focuses our efforts in the short and <span style="white-space:nowrap">mid-term</span> on 4 strategic pillars: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">1.</span></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify">Focus on our most profitable business: Vaca Muerta </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Development of our unconventional hydrocarbon acreage with competitive advantages and debottleneck of the crude oil production from the Vaca Muerta formation, through infrastructure projects that will enable future growth and exports. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">3.</span></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify">Maximize upstream and downstream efficiency </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Efficiency in costs and processes in all of our business segments, and particularly in the Vaca Muerta formation, with the aim of ensuring resilience even in low price scenarios; as well as adaptation of our refineries to facilitate greater shale crude oil processing, and to reach the expected quality of fuels demanded by our customers. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221; plan is already ongoing, by which we intend to maximize the value creation for our stakeholders in a sustainable way. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, we continued to focus on implementing our corporate sustainability policy and advancing our commitment to climate and energy-related actions, the reduction of the intensity of the Company&#8217;s CO<sub style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:bottom">2</sub> emissions (focused on upstream operations) as well as the development of renewable energies through our participation in YPF Energ&#237;a El&#233;ctrica S.A. (&#8220;YPF EE&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The investment plan related to our strategy requires the reinvestment of our earnings, our association with strategic partners and the use of debt financing at levels we consider prudent for companies in our industry. The financial viability of these investments and hydrocarbon recovery efforts will depend on numerous factors that YPF does not control or influence, such as the prevailing economic and regulatory conditions in Argentina, the ability to obtain financing in satisfactory amounts at competitive costs, among others. See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8221; and &#8220;Item 5. Operating and financial review and prospects&#8212;Factors affecting our operations&#8221;. Furthermore, we continue to manage our portfolio actively, prioritizing the divestment of matured conventional assets and including the evaluation of new joint ventures to develop our unconventional acreage. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_16"><span style="font-style:italic">Business organization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For a table including the main entities of our organizational structure, and details regarding our principal subsidiaries, see Note 1 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our operations, properties and clients are mainly located in Argentina. However, we also hold participating interest in exploratory areas in Bolivia and sell jet fuel, natural gas, lubricants and derivatives in Chile and lubricants and derivatives in Brazil (see Note 3 &#8220;Sale of equity participation in YPF Brasil&#8221; section to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements). As of December&#160;31, 2024, the Company decided not to renew the contracts related to the commercialization of aerokerosene in Chile in order to focus on operations mainly in Argentina. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December 31, 2024, we conducted our business according to the following organization: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><span style="font-weight:bold">(i)</span></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify">Upstream business segment </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbon fields and production of crude oil and natural gas. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from: (i)&#160;the sale of the crude oil produced to the Downstream business segment; and (ii)&#160;the sale of the natural gas produced and the natural gas retained in plant to the Gas and Power business segment. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On July&#160;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes, which were formerly included in Upstream business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify">Downstream business segment </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Downstream business segment performs activities related to: (i)&#160;crude oil refining and the production of petrochemical products; (ii)&#160;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to the refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&#160;commercialization of refined and petrochemical products obtained from such processes; (iv)&#160;commercialization of crude oil; and (v)&#160;commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their <span style="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of crude oil, refined and petrochemical products, specialties for the agribusiness industry and grains and their <span style="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</span> These operations are performed through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Industries, Transportation, Aviation, Agro, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade and Transportation and Sales to Companies. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of: (i)&#160;crude oil from the Upstream business segment and third parties; (ii)&#160;gasoline and natural gas to be consumed in the refinery and petrochemical industrial complexes from the Gas and Power business segment; and (iii)&#160;propane and butane to be commercialized from the Gas and Power business segment. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

(&#8220;Metrogas&#8221;); and (v)&#160;the storage of the natural gas produced. Also, through our investments in associates and joint ventures, it undertakes activities related to: (i)&#160;separation of NGLs and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and gasoline; (ii)&#160;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&#160;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and the Downstream business segment, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the sale of gasoline, propane and butane to the Downstream business segment and the provision of LNG regasification services. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of natural gas and natural gas retained in plant from the Upstream business segment. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Comparative information for the years ended December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022 has been restated due to changes in certain assets related to the exploration, exploitation and production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Sales between business segments were made at internal transfer prices established by the Company, which approximately reflect domestic market prices. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Operating profit or loss of each business segment has been determined after consolidation adjustments. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For a description of our principal capital expenditures and divestitures see &#8220;Item 5. Operating and financial review and prospects&#8212;Liquidity and capital resources&#8212;Capital investments, expenditures and divestitures&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_17"><span style="font-style:italic">Upstream </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s Upstream business segment seeks to add value to the Company by optimizing the use of deployed capital, achieving levels of operational excellence, thus generating new development opportunities, while delivering profitable growth driven by the increasing incorporation of unconventional projects to its activities where well construction efficiency is a fundamental factor. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The plan of promotion for natural gas production in Argentina, Plan GasAr 2020-2024, launched in November 2020, gave to the Company an opportunity to monetize natural gas reservoirs, ensuring to supply the demand in Argentina for four years at a price that allows for the development of our natural gas projects in certain basins. In the same vein, Plan GasAr 2023-2028, launched in November 2022, allowed the Company to extend this opportunity by ensuring to supply the natural gas demand in Argentina over the following four years. For further information see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business organization&#8212;Gas and Power&#8212;Natural gas activities&#8221; and Note 36.d.1) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, we continued actively managing our portfolio. As of December&#160;31, 2024, we held interests in 111 oil and gas fields in Argentina. According to the IAPG, in 2024, these assets accounted for 36.1% of the total production of crude oil and 28.7% of the total natural gas production of Argentina. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, YPF&#8217;s hydrocarbon production increased by 4.4% compared to 2023. The daily production of crude oil increased by 6.0%, NGLs increased by 0.4%, and natural gas increased by a 3.4% compared to 2023. Additionally, 53% of our total hydrocarbon production is unconventional. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our unconventional hydrocarbon production continued to increase strongly during 2024. The daily production of crude oil increased by 25.9%, NGLs increased by 4.9%, and natural gas increased by 18.6% compared to 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;29, 2024, YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors resolved the disposal of certain groups of assets, mainly mature fields in the Golfo San Jorge, Neuquina, Cuyana and Austral basins. This disposal of assets related to mature fields (&#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221;) is consistent with the Company&#8217;s management plans, which considers that the rationalization of the conventional upstream portfolio is one of the drivers on which the YPF&#8217;s strategy is based, with focus on activities and investments in unconventional fields. The Mature Fields Project is aligned with the second strategic pilar of our &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221; plan, see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business strategy&#8212;Strategic pillars: &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221;&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may fail to execute in whole or in part our disposal plan related to mature fields (&#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221;)&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In this regard, during 2024, YPF signed different assignment agreements for 8 groups of assets (24 areas), subject to the fulfillment of agreed closing conditions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, the agreed closing conditions of the assignment agreements of the &#8220;Escalante - El Tr&#233;bol&#8221; and &#8220;Llancanelo and Llancanelo R&#8221; exploitation concessions were met. In addition, after December&#160;31, 2024, the agreed closing conditions of the assignment agreements of the &#8220;Estaci&#243;n Fern&#225;ndez Oro&#8221;, &#8220;Campamento Central - Ca&#241;ad&#243;n Perdido&#8221;, &#8220;Barrancas&#8221;, &#8220;Vizcacheras&#8221;, &#8220;La Ventana&#8221;, &#8220;Ceferino&#8221;, &#8220;Mesa Verde&#8221; and &#8220;R&#237;o Tunuy&#225;n&#8221; exploitation concessions were met; while the remaining three assignment agreements are subject to the fulfillment of agreed closing conditions for which the Company is taking the necessary steps to close them. For further details see Note 11 &#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8220; section to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements and &#8220;Item 8. Financial information&#8212;Significant changes&#8221;. </p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Relates to Colombia, Bolivia and Uruguay. In Colombia, YPF notified the Colombian National Hydrocarbons Agency (Agencia Nacional de Hidrocarburos or &#8220;ANH&#8221;) of the decision to relinquish the COR 12 and COR 33 blocks; and in July 2022, the ANH began an administrative proceeding claiming the exploration commitments were not performed or paid; as of the date of this annual report the Company has presented its defenses in the administrative process and the ANH is considering the evidence offered. YPF&#8217;s net undeveloped surface acreage totaled 91,553 acres in Bolivia and 4,160,266 acres in Uruguay. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The net exploratory undeveloped acreage in Argentina under the first or second exploration periods, which mature in 2025 and in the period 2026-2028 is 18,325 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> (85.2%) and 3,175 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2 </sup>(14.8%), respectively, of our 21,500 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> net exploratory undeveloped acreage as of December&#160;31, 2024. The net exploratory undeveloped acreage in the Rest of South America is 17,906 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup>, which mature in the period 2025-2027. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The extension of the expiring acreage that the Company would be required to surrender to the relevant enforcement authority will depend on our decision to extend our exploration permit in a given area, provided that the requirements of the Argentine Hydrocarbons Law have been met, including the fulfillment of our obligations under the exploration permit relating to those areas. Therefore, the areas to be relinquished usually consist of acreage where drilling has not been successful and are considered <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-core</span> lease acreage. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, we do not have any material undeveloped acreage related to our exploitation concessions expiring in the near term. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Exploration permits and exploitation concessions in Argentina </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following table sets forth, for the period indicated, information regarding the exploration permits and exploitation concessions we held: </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:0.75pt solid #000000;white-space:nowrap;vertical-align:bottom;background-color:#ebf0f9"><span style="color:#1a4ca3"><span style="font-weight:bold">&#160;</span></span></td>

<td style="BORDER-BOTTOM:0.75pt solid #000000;white-space:nowrap;vertical-align:bottom;background-color:#ebf0f9"><span style="color:#1a4ca3"><span style="font-weight:bold">&#160;</span></span></td></tr>

</table> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Exploration&#160;&amp; Development activity </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold">Argentina </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Exploration activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s <span style="font-weight:bold">onshore exploration portfolio</span> is mainly focused on high-impact projects such as <span style="font-weight:bold">Palermo Aike</span>, believed to be the second shale formation, located in the Austral basin, behind the Vaca Muerta formation in terms of potential, and <span style="font-weight:bold">Vaca Muerta</span>. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The exploration of <span style="font-weight:bold">Palermo Aike</span>, which is being developed jointly with Compa&#241;&#237;a General de Combustibles S.A (&#8220;CGC&#8221;) began in 2023 and continued through 2024. In 2024, the first horizontal well was drilled, completed and tested. This well featured 753 meters stimulated lateral extension with 12 frac stages. Although well productivity was low, the flowback test produced natural gas and condensate, confirming that the well is situated in the natural gas/condensate maturity window. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">Vaca Muerta</span> formation, in 2024, 2 horizontal wells, drilled during 2023, were completed and tested, with 12 and 13 stimulation stages, one in Paso de las Bardas Norte block where we have an exploitation concession and the other one in the CN VII block where we have an exploration permit. Each well featured more than 1,000 meters of horizontal extension, navigating two different levels within the Vaca Muerta formation. Flowback tests of both wells confirmed producing black oil. Encouraged by these results, YPF entered, from August 2024, a second exploratory period in the CN VII block, which was granted to YPF through Administrative Decision No.&#160;30/2024 of the Mendoza Province, where we committed to drill 2 additional horizontal exploratory wells with 2,500 meters of horizontal extension each. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, in <span style="font-weight:bold">Las Tacanas</span> block, 2 wells drilled in 2023 were completed, and, as of the date of this annual report, are producing according to the type-well expectations. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding the activity in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Gas Window Delineation</span>, in the western area of the Neuquina basin, 2 horizontal wells that started drilling in 2023 (1 in <span style="font-weight:bold">Cerro Las Minas</span> block and 1 in <span style="font-weight:bold">Loma del Molle</span> block) were concluded their drilling stage during 2024. No further action was taken since these wells proved to be uneconomical. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The <span style="font-weight:bold">offshore portfolio</span> continues to grow with the acquisition of, in November 2024 from Equinor, the 35% <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> working interest of the <span style="font-weight:bold">AUS 105</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">AUS 106</span> blocks located in the Austral basin. Equinor is the operator of these blocks, with a <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> joint participation of YPF and CGC. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">CAN 100</span> block, between April 2024 and June 2024, the first deepwater well in Argentina (the Argerich well) was drilled without environmental or safety incidents. This well was located 300 km away from the Mar del Plata city&#8217;s port, in the Buenos Aires Province, at a water depth of 1,527 meters, reaching the planned total depth of 4,050 meters. In terms of results, although it proved the geological model, the oil system could not be tested, resulting on a dry well. As of the date of this annual report, a detailed post-drill analysis is being carried out, to assess the remaining exploration potential of the block. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Seismic activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, we carried out four 3D seismic campaigns in offshore blocks in Argentina. Two 3D seismic surveys were acquired for the North Argentina basin, one of 1,500 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> in the CAN 102 block and another one of 2,800 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> in the CAN 114 block. Moreover, one 3D seismic survey was acquired for the Austral basin, a 900 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> survey in the AUS 105 block and a 1,500 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> survey in the AUS 106 block; and a 3,000 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> 3D seismic survey in the MLO 123 block located in the Malvinas basin. As of December&#160;31, 2024, the 3D seismic surveys showed a 40% advance in the MLO 123 block, 93% advance in the CAN 102 block, while in CAN 114, AUS 105 and AUS 106 blocks the surveys were fully completed. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Development activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Unconventional activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024 the hydrocarbon production from our <span style="font-weight:bold">unconventional activities</span> was 208.9 kboe/d (YPF net, from operated areas), representing 39% of YPF&#8217;s total production (YPF net, from operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas). In 2024, YPF, jointly with its partners, continued with its growth plan with more than US$ 2,392&#160;million invested (YPF net, from operated areas), 195 wells were put into production and more than 8,000 frac stages were carried out in blocks operated by YPF. Considering all of the above, YPF expects to continue to lead the unconventional activities development in Argentina. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, YPF&#8217;s was highly active in its drilling operations at the <span style="font-weight:bold">Core Hub blocks</span> (<span style="font-weight:bold">Loma Campana</span>, <span style="font-weight:bold">La Amarga Chica</span>, <span style="font-weight:bold">Bandurria Sur</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada del Cha&#241;ar</span>), with 11 rigs. Operational efficiencies continued to break records, with the drilling of the longest horizontal well in the Vaca Muerta formation with a total length of 8,264 meters (27,113 feet) and a lateral length of 4,948 meters (16,234 feet) in 27 days, using real time data for decision making on drilling and completion activities. The average lateral length drilled in the Core Hub blocks was 2,950 meters (9,678 feet). Additionally, see &#8220;Item 8. Financial information&#8212;Significant changes&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Drilling activities have been gradually increasing at higher levels of the Vaca Muerta formation, showing favorable productivity results, such as the productivity of the wells executed at the &#8220;medium organic&#8221; level in <span style="font-weight:bold">Loma Campana</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Bandurria Sur</span> blocks, and confirming the expectation to increase the drilling activities in the upcoming years. These results allow us to confirm the current inventory of wells expected to be drilled and to incorporate new drilling positions. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Development activities focuses on the lower levels of the Vaca Muerta formation (known as &#8220;Cocina&#8221; and &#8220;Org&#225;nico&#8221;) with proven and profitable results with the application of the High-Density Completion (&#8220;HDC&#8221;) stimulation design. Different strategies are being applied to mitigate parent/child effects from the drilling of nearby wells as development progresses at these lower levels such as well spacing adjustments and stimulation design adjustments. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Throughout 2024, 3 new facilities were put into production in the Core Hub blocks: (i)&#160;the 3N Battery, with a processing capacity of 6,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d; (ii)&#160;a second crude oil treatment plant (&#8220;PTC&#8221;), with a production capacity of 12,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d, both in <span style="font-weight:bold">La Amarga Chica</span> block; and (ii)&#160;the Battery 4 in <span style="font-weight:bold">Bandurria Sur</span> block with a processing capacity of 6,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, a milestone in the development of the Vaca Muerta formation was the acceleration of the <span style="font-weight:bold">South Hub blocks</span> (<span style="font-weight:bold">La Angostura Sur I</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">La Angostura Sur II</span> in Aguada Toledo - Sierra Barrosa exploitation concession), with the drilling of a 9 PADs (groups of between 4 and 6 wells each). As of December&#160;31, 2024, 2 PADs are producing according to the type-well expectations, while the remining 7 PADs are expected to start production during 2025. Also, in December 2024, a production treatment module, with a capacity of 2,500 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d, was put into production. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding the <span style="font-weight:bold">North Hub blocks</span> (<span style="font-weight:bold">Bajo del Toro Norte</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Narambuena</span>), during 2024, activities were focused on <span style="font-weight:bold">Bajo del Toro Norte</span> block with the drilling of 3 PADs on which the delineation stage was completed, and the development stage began. On March&#160;7, 2025, the Neuqu&#233;n Province granted YPF unconventional hydrocarbon exploitation concessions (&#8220;CENCH&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) in Aguada de la Arena, La Angostura Sur I, La Angostura Sur II and Narambuena blocks. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">Gas Hub blocks</span> (<span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada de la Arena</span>, <span style="font-weight:bold">Rinc&#243;n del Mangrullo</span>, <span style="font-weight:bold">La Ribera</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">El Orejano)</span>, the main milestone of 2024 was the startup of the Primary Separation Unit (&#8220;USP&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) in <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada de la Arena</span> block, which expanded the capacity by 4 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d, reaching a total capacity of 7 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Conventional activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold">Sur Region </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the <span style="font-weight:bold">Sur Region</span>&#8217;s hydrocarbon production was 84.5 kboe/d (YPF net, from operated areas), representing 16% of YPF&#8217;s total production (YPF net, from operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas). </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, activity in the Sur Region involved a total investment (YPF net, from operated areas) of US$ 469&#160;million, of which US$ 272&#160;million were related to investments associated with the Mature Fields Project (US$ 248 million of which were investments in the Santa Cruz Province). </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Related to the Mature Fields Project investments, US$ 68 million were related mainly to continuing operational sustainability, taking care of the safety of operations and employees, as well as the environment. The remaining US$ 204 million were investments associated with development projects. The average development cost associated with drilling activity was approximately four times the cost of developing unconventional oil wells. YPF&#8217;s current strategy is based on unconventional fields, in accordance with the first pillar of the &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221;. See &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business strategy&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may fail to execute in whole or in part our disposal plan related to mature fields (&#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221;)&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Related to the Mature Fields Project, in November 2024, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and PECOM Servicios Energ&#237;a S.A.U. (&#8220;PECOM&#8221;), the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in <span style="font-weight:bold">Escalante - El Tr&#233;bol </span>exploitation concession in favor of PECOM was formalized. Additionally, in January 2025, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and PECOM, the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in <span style="font-weight:bold">Campamento Central - Ca&#241;ad&#243;n Perdido</span> exploitation concession in favor of PECOM was formalized. See &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business strategy&#8212;Strategic pillars: &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221;&#8221; and Note 11 &#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8220; section to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In June 2024, the Chubut and Santa Cruz Provinces were affected by a severe snowstorm, affecting the operation of facilities and wells. On average, the production of June 2024 and July 2024 suffered a reduction of 13.8 kbbl/d and 7.1 kbbl/d in the Chubut and Santa Cruz Provinces, respectively, when compared to average daily production of the first quarter of 2024. By the end of 2024, production was normalized. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, activity in the Sur Region was mainly focused on the development of polymer injection projects in <span style="font-weight:bold">Manantiales Behr</span> block, in the Chubut Province. In the <span style="font-weight:bold">Grimbeek Norte II</span> project, a secondary polymer injection pilot, accounting for the 33% of the Sur Region tertiary production in 2024 with 2.5 kbbl/d on average (without previous conventional waterflooding) continues to boost oil production since 2022. Encouraged by the results obtained, the Company plans to begin the massification towards two additional zones in 2025. With the intention to expand the results of Grimbeek Norte II block, a new polymer injection project started in the fourth quarter of 2024 in <span style="font-weight:bold">Grimbeek Central</span> block, whose initial results are expected starting from December 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">El Alba Valle</span> field in the Manantiales Behr block, since 2023, a polymer injection project continues to boost the production with results exceeding expectations. This polymer injection pilot was carried out on the Complejo III formation that had remained untested until now, and emboldened on these results, the Company is analyzing to expand the project towards two additional zones of the El Alba Valle field. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:center">23 </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold">Oeste Region </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the <span style="font-weight:bold">Oeste Region</span>&#8217;s hydrocarbon production was 127.5 kboe/d (YPF net, from operated areas), representing 24% of YPF&#180;s total production (YPF net, from operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas). </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the activity in the Oeste Region involved a total investment (YPF net, from operated areas) of US$ 160&#160;million, of which US$ 80&#160;million were related to investments associated with the Mature Fields Project. These investments in mature fields focused mainly on continuing operational sustainability, taking care of the safety of operations and employees, as well as the environment. See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may fail to execute in whole or in part our disposal plan related to mature fields (&#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221;)&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Related to the Mature Fields Project, in December 2024, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and Petroqu&#237;mica Comodoro Rivadavia S.A. (&#8220;PCR&#8221;), the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in <span style="font-weight:bold">Llancanelo and Llancanelo R</span> exploitation concessions in favor of PCR was formalized. Additionally, in February 2025, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and Quintana E&amp;P Argentina S.R.L., Quintana Energy Investments S.A., and Gas Storage and Midstream Services S.A. (&#8220;Quintana Consortium&#8221;), the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in <span style="font-weight:bold">Estaci&#243;n Fern&#225;ndez Oro</span> exploitation concession in favor of Quintana Consortium was formalized. See &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business strategy&#8212;Strategic pillars: &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221;&#8221; and Note 11 &#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8220; section to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Activity in the Oeste Region is focused on <span style="font-weight:bold">R&#237;o Neuqu&#233;n</span> block where the only YPF&#8217;s operated conventional natural gas production project takes place. During 2024, 1 service well was completed, 8 tight gas wells were drilled, and 10 wells were put into production, which as of the date of this annual report are under evaluation. In 2024, polymer flooding operations in <span style="font-weight:bold">Chachahuen Sur</span> block proceeded as scheduled. Additionally, developments were made on this block in relation to investments in facilities. In 2024, the 16 km oil pipeline and Skimmer Battery 1 were started up. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operated</span> activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the hydrocarbon production of the <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas</span> was 115.3 kboe/d (YPF net, from <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas), representing 21% of YPF&#180;s total production (YPF net, from operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas). </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the <span style="font-weight:bold">conventional activities </span>in the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas involved a total investment (YPF net, from <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas) of US$ 29&#160;million in drilling and completion and US$ 20&#160;million in production facilities and other capital expenditures, of which US$ 10 million were related to investments associated with the Mature Fields Project. These investments in mature fields were focused mainly on continuing operational sustainability, taking care of the safety of operations and employees, as well as the environment. See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may fail to execute in whole or in part our disposal plan related to mature fields (&#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221;)&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the <span style="font-weight:bold">unconventional activities</span> in the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas in the Neuquina basin involved a total investment (YPF net, from <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas) of US$ 409&#160;million in drilling and completion and US$ 367&#160;million in production facilities and other capital expenditures. Shale oil main investments were concentrated in <span style="font-weight:bold">Lindero Atravesado</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Bajada de A&#241;elo</span> blocks, while shale gas investments were focused on <span style="font-weight:bold">La Calera</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada Pichana Oeste</span> blocks. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, in <span style="font-weight:bold">La Calera</span> block, the construction of the Central Production Facility I (&#8220;CPF I&#8221;) project finished its first stage in April 2024, and in October 2024, the <span style="white-space:nowrap">start-up</span> was completed allowing a natural gas treatment capacity of 10 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d and 4,800 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d of condensate. In addition, once the first phase of the construction of the Central Production Facility II (&#8220;CPF II&#8221;) project finishes, the natural gas capacity treatment will increase in 4.5 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d (totaling of 14.5 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d). With the CPF II, La Calera block will have a total treatment capacity of 17 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d and 9,600 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d of natural gas and condensate, respectively, by 2027. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Aguarag&#252;e</span>, <span style="font-weight:bold">La Calera</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada Pichana Oeste</span> blocks are part of the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and Plan GasAr 2023-2028 that aim to boost natural gas production in Argentina by granting competitive prices. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold">Rest of South America </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Exploration activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Throughout 2024 geological studies were carried out to assess the potential of the OFF 5 block, an offshore area in <span style="font-weight:bold">Uruguay</span>, which, as of December&#160;31, 2024, represents 16,836 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> of YPF&#8217;s acreage. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In October 2024, we initiated the drilling of the well committed in the Charagua Block, in <span style="font-weight:bold">Bolivia</span> (in which we hold a 60% interest), which, as of December&#160;31, 2024, is being drilled, with drilling progress of 27%. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The COR 12 and COR 33 blocks located in the Cordillera Oriental basin in <span style="font-weight:bold">Colombia</span>, are operated pursuant to the authorization by the ANH. Our working interest is 60% in the COR 12 block and 55% in the COR 33 block. The combined net area of these blocks is 700 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup>. In 2016, together with our partners, we informed to the ANH of our decision to relinquish both blocks. In July 2022, the ANH began an administrative proceeding claiming the exploration commitments were not performed or paid. As of the date of this annual report, the Company presented its defenses in the administrative process and the ANH is considering the evidence offered. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Oil and gas reserves </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Proved oil and gas reserves are those quantities of oil and gas which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible (from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods and government regulations) prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation. The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project within reasonable time. In some cases, substantial investments in new wells and related facilities may be required to recover proved reserves. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Information on net proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022 was calculated in accordance with the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules. Accordingly, crude oil prices used to determine reserves were calculated for crude oils of different quality produced by the Company. Consequently, to calculate our net proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2024, the Company considered, according to the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules, the unweighted average realized price of crude oils for each month within the <span style="white-space:nowrap">12-month</span> period ended December&#160;31, 2024, which refers to the domestic crude oil prices adjusted by each different quality produced by the Company. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The reported reserves contained in this annual report include only our proved reserves and do not include probable reserves or possible reserves. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, since there are no benchmark market natural gas prices available in Argentina, the Company considered the <span style="white-space:nowrap">12-month</span> period average ended December&#160;31, 2024 of domestic market realized prices according to the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules, and the prices of contracts awarded to YPF under the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 for certain blocks in certain basins, which will be in effect until their corresponding termination dates. See Note 36.d.1) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Notwithstanding the foregoing, commodity prices have fluctuated significantly in recent years. See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our oil and gas reserves and production may decline&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our oil and gas reserves are estimates&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Net reserves are defined as that portion of the gross reserves attributable to the interest of the Company after deducting interests owned by third parties. In determining net reserves, the Company excludes from its reported reserves royalties owed to others, whether payable in cash or in kind, where the royalty owner has a direct interest in the underlying production and is able to make lifting and sales arrangements independently. By contrast, to the extent that royalty payments required to be made to a third-party, whether payable in cash or in kind, are a financial obligation, or are substantially equivalent to a production or severance tax, the related reserves are not excluded from the reported reserves despite the fact that such payments are referred to as royalties under local regulations. The same methodology is followed in reporting our production amounts. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Natural gas reserves exclude the gaseous equivalent of liquids expected to be removed from the natural gas on concessions and leases, at field facilities and at natural gas processing plants. These liquids are included in net proved reserves of NGLs. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Technology used in establishing proved reserves additions </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s estimated proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2024 are based on estimates generated through the integration of available and appropriate data, utilizing well-established technologies that have been demonstrated in the field to yield repeatable and consistent results. Data used in these integrated assessments include information obtained directly from the subsurface via wellbore, such as well logs, reservoir core samples, fluid samples, static and dynamic pressure information, production test data, and surveillance and performance information. The data utilized also include subsurface information obtained through indirect measurements, including high quality <span style="white-space:nowrap">2-D</span> and <span style="white-space:nowrap">3-D</span> seismic data, calibrated with available well control. Where applicable, geological outcrops information was also utilized. The tools used to interpret and integrate all this data included both proprietary and commercial software for reservoir modeling, simulation and data analysis. In some circumstances, where appropriate analog reservoir models are available, reservoir parameters from these analog models were used to increase the reliability of our reserves estimates. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For further information on the estimation process of our proved reserves, see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business organization&#8212;Upstream&#8212;Oil and gas reserves&#8212;Internal controls on reserves and reserves audits&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Net proved developed and undeveloped reserves as of December</span><span style="text-decoration:underline"></span><span style="text-decoration:underline">&#160;31, 2024</span> </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following tables sets forth information, for the period indicated, regarding our estimated net proved developed and undeveloped reserves of crude oil, NGLs and natural gas: </p> <p style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For information regarding changes in our estimated net proved reserves for the year ended December 31, 2024, 2023 and 2022 see &#8220;Supplemental information on oil and gas producing activities (unaudited)&#8221; beginning on page S-1 of this annual report. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Reserves replacement ratio</span> </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The reserves replacement ratio is the net amount of added proved reserves divided by the volumes produced in any given period. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, the reserves replacement ratio was 112% as a result of an addition of 220 Mboe of net proved reserves (107 Mbbl of liquids, and 113 Mboe of natural gas), and considering 196 Mboe produced during the year and the amount of proved reserves at the beginning of 2024. In addition, 11 Mboe of proved reserves were discounted related to sales. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">By excluding the influence of reserves and production volumes associated with the assets within the Mature Fields Project, our reserves replacement ratio yields 146% as of December&#160;31, 2024. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, if the analysis is restricted to unconventional fields only, the reserves replacement ratio reached 192% as of December&#160;31, 2024. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For additional information regarding changes in proved reserves and the reliability of proved reserves estimates, see &#8220;Supplemental information on oil and gas producing activities (unaudited)&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our oil and gas reserves and production may decline&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our oil and gas reserves are estimates&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The table below sets forth, for each of the periods indicated, information regarding reserves replacement ratio: </p> <p style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

In order to meet the high standard of &#8220;reasonable certainty&#8221;, reserves estimates are stated taking into consideration additional guidance as to reservoir economic producibility requirements, acceptable proved area extensions, drive mechanisms and improved recovery methods, marketability under existing economic and operating conditions and project maturity. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Where applicable, the volumetric method is used to determine the original quantities of petroleum in place. Estimates are made by using various types of logs, core analysis and other available data. Formation tops, gross thickness and representative values for net pay thickness, porosity and interstitial fluid saturations are used to prepare structural maps to delineate each reservoir and isopachous maps to determine reservoir volume. Where adequate data is available and where circumstances are justified, material-balance and other engineering methods are used to estimate the original hydrocarbon in place. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Estimates of ultimate recovery in conventional reservoirs are usually reviewed by applying recovery factors to the original quantities of petroleum in place. These factors are based on the drive mechanisms inherent in the reservoir, analysis of the fluid and rock properties, the structural position of the reservoir and its production history. In some instances, comparisons are made with similar production reservoirs in the blocks where more complete data is available. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For unconventional reservoir developments, reserves estimates are focused on performance-based methodologies, where stimulation technique and current technology information are also integrated in the analysis. When applicable, statistical evaluations are implemented considering <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">state-of-the-art</span></span></span> methods. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Where adequate data is available and where circumstances are justified, material-balance and other engineering methods are used to estimate ultimate recovery. In these instances, reservoir performance parameters such as cumulative production, production rate, reservoir pressure, gas to oil ratio behavior and water production are considered in estimating ultimate recovery. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In certain cases where the above methods cannot be used, proved reserves are estimated by analogy to similar reservoirs where more complete data are available. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">To control the quality of reserves booking, a process has been established that is integrated into YPF&#8217;s internal control system. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This process to manage reserves booking is centrally controlled and has the following components: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;text-align:justify">The Reserves Audit department (&#8220;RA&#8221;) is separate and independent from the Upstream business segment. RA&#8217;s activity is overseen by YPF&#8217;s Audit Committee, which is also responsible for supervising the procedures and systems used in the recording of and internal control over the Company&#8217;s hydrocarbon reserves. The primary objectives of the RA are to ensure that YPF&#8217;s proved reserves estimates and disclosure are in compliance with the rules of the SEC, the FASB and the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, and to review annual changes in reserves estimates and the reporting of YPF&#8217;s proved reserves. The RA is responsible for: (i)&#160;preparing the information to be publicly disclosed concerning YPF&#8217;s reported proved reserves of oil, NGLs and natural gas; and (ii)&#160;providing training to personnel involved in the estimation of reserves and reporting process within YPF. The RA is managed by and staffed with individuals that have an average of more than 20 years of technical experience in the petroleum industry, including in the classification and categorization of reserves under the SEC guidelines. The RA staff includes several individuals who hold advanced degrees in either engineering or geology, as well as individuals who hold bachelor&#8217;s degrees in various technical studies. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

The current Reserves Auditor has over 30 years of experience in reservoir engineering, reserves estimates, project development, field operations, economic evaluations and general accounting regulations. Prior to becoming the Reserves Auditor, he worked as Asset Manager and Head of Planning at fields in the Golfo San Jorge and Neuquina basins, and he was Reserves Audit Team Manager in the RA between 2009 and 2022. He holds a degree in Electrical Engineering from the Universidad Nacional de La Plata, a master&#8217;s degree from Escuela Internacional de Negocios, and postgraduate Executive Development Program at IAE Business School. Consistent with our internal control system requirements, the Reserves Auditor&#8217;s compensation is not affected by changes in reported reserves. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

Our QRCs are responsible for reviewing proved reserves estimates. The qualification of each QRC is made on a <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">case-by-case</span></span> basis with reference to the recognition and respect of such QRC&#8217;s peers. YPF would normally consider a QRC to be qualified if such person: (i)&#160;has a minimum of 5 years of practical experience in petroleum engineering or petroleum geology, with at least 3 years of such experience in charge of the estimation and evaluation of reserves; and (ii)&#160;has either obtained, from a college or university of recognized stature, a bachelor&#8217;s or advanced degree in petroleum engineering, geology or other related discipline of engineering or physical science, or received, and is maintaining in good standing, a registered or certified professional engineer&#8217;s license or a registered or certified professional geologist&#8217;s license, or the equivalent thereof, from an appropriate governmental authority or professional organization. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">recently acquired properties not submitted to a third-party reserves audit in the previous cycle and properties with respect to which there is new information which could materially affect prior reserves estimates. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For those blocks submitted to a third-party reserves audit, YPF&#8217;s proved reserves figures have to be within 7% or 10 Mboe of the third-party reserves audit figures for YPF to declare that the volumes have been ratified by a third-party reserves audit. In the event that the difference is greater than the tolerance, YPF will <span style="white-space:nowrap">re-estimate</span> its proved reserves to achieve this tolerance level or should disclose the third-party figures. YPF has adopted the above-mentioned procedure by approving the corresponding internal policy. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, DeGolyer and MacNaughton audited certain YPF operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> blocks in Argentina in the Neuquina, Golfo San Jorge and Cuyana basins. These audits were performed as of December&#160;31, 2024 and the audited blocks contain in aggregate approximately 381 Mboe of proved reserves, which represented approximately 35% of our proved reserves as of such date (166 Mboe were proved undeveloped reserves, which represented approximately 35% of our proved undeveloped reserves as of December&#160;31, 2024). Copies of the related reserves audit reports are filed as an exhibit to this annual report. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, YPF estimates reserves under Petroleum Resources Management System (&#8220;PRMS&#8221;) criteria. As of December&#160;31, 2024, 100% of YPF&#8217;s blocks were externally audited under this criteria, although this should not be interpreted as an external certification or audit of oil and gas reserves under SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules. See Nota 2.c) &#8220;Oil and gas reserves section to the Audited Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We are required, in accordance with Resolutions No.&#160;324/2006 of the former Argentine Subsecretariat of Hydrocarbons and No.&#160;69/2016 of the former Argentine Energy Secretariat, to annually file by March&#160;31 details of our estimates of our oil and gas reserves and resources with the SE, as defined in those resolutions, and certified by an external auditor. The aforementioned certification and external audit only have the meaning established by the aforementioned resolutions and are not to be interpreted as an external certification or audit of oil and gas reserves under SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules. The last report filed was for the year ended December&#160;31, 2023. Estimates of our oil and gas reserves filed with the SE are materially higher than the estimates of our proved oil and gas reserves contained in this annual report, mainly because of: (i)&#160;information filed with the SE includes all properties of which we are operators, irrespective of the level of our ownership interests in such properties; (ii)&#160;information filed with the SE includes other categories of reserves and resources that are not included in this annual report, which are different from estimates of proved reserves consistent with the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules contained in this annual report; and (iii)&#160;the definition of proved reserves under the aforementioned Resolutions is different from the definition of &#8220;proved oil and gas reserves&#8221; established in Rule <span style="white-space:nowrap">4-10(a)</span> of Regulation <span style="white-space:nowrap">S-X.</span> Accordingly, all proved oil and gas reserves estimates included in this annual report reflect only proved oil and gas reserves consistent with the rules and disclosure requirements of the SEC and FASB ASC 932 rules. </p>
