 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Oil and gas production, production costs and sales prices</span> </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following table sets forth, for each of the periods indicated, information regarding our crude oil (including crude oil and condensate), NGLs and natural gas production on an as sold and annual basis. In determining net production, we exclude royalties owed to others, whether payable in cash or in kind, where the royalty owner has a direct interest in such production and is able to make lifting and sales arrangements independently. By contrast, to the extent that royalty payments required to be made to a third-party, whether payable in cash or in kind, are a financial obligation or are substantially equivalent to a production or severance tax, they are not excluded from our net production amounts despite the fact that such payments are referred to as royalties under local regulations. This is the case for our production in Argentina, where royalty expense is accounted for as a production cost. </p> <p style="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="white-space:nowrap;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="white-space:nowrap;vertical-align:bottom;text-align:right">72.0</td>
<td style="white-space:nowrap;vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td></tr>
</table> <p style="margin-top:14pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The <span style="font-weight:bold">La Plata Refinery</span> is the largest refinery in Argentina, located at the port in the La Plata city, in the Buenos Aires Province, 60 km from the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, with a nominal capacity of 198.9 kbbl/d. It is a complex refinery with three distillation units, two vacuum distillation units, two fluid catalytic cracking units, two coking units, a coke naphtha hydrotreater unit, a platforming unit, two diesel hydro finishing units, a gasoline hydrotreater, an isomerization unit, a fluid cracking catalyst (&#8220;FCC&#8221;) naphtha splitter and desulfuration unit, a lubricants complex, and a petrochemical complex that generates methyl tert-butyl ether (&#8220;MTBE&#8221;), tert-amyl methyl ether (&#8220;TAME&#8221;) and aromatics compounds used for blending gasoline and other chemical products. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the revamped Topping D unit was fully operative, allowing the processing of greater volumes of shale oil production. In addition, during 2024, maintenance stoppages were carried out at the FCC and platforming units. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, the crude oil processed at the La Plata Refinery (of which 67.8% was <span style="white-space:nowrap">YPF-produced)</span> was produced mainly from the Neuquina and Golfo San Jorge basins. The La Plata Refinery crude oil supplies come from the Neuquina basin by pipeline and from the Golfo San Jorge basin by vessel, in both cases to Puerto Rosales in the Buenos Aires Province, and then by pipeline from Puerto Rosales to the La Plata Refinery. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The <span style="font-weight:bold">Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery,</span> the second largest in Argentina, located in the Mendoza Province, with a nominal capacity of 113.9 kbbl/d, includes two distillation units, a vacuum distillation unit, two coking units, a fluid catalytic cracking unit, a platforming unit, an ethyl tertiary-butyl ether (&#8220;ETBE&#8221;) unit, an isomerization unit, an alkylation unit, a FCC naphtha splitter, a hydrocracking unit, a FCC naphtha hydrotreater unit and two gasoil hydrotreating units. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Due to its location in the western of the Mendoza Province and its proximity to significant distribution terminals we own, the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery has become the primary facility responsible for refining petroleum products to supply the domestic market of the central and northwest provinces of Argentina. The Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery receives crude oil supplies from the Neuquina and Cuyana basins by pipeline directly into the facility. In 2024, 85.6% of the crude oil processed at the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery was produced by us. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the processing operations of the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery were affected by the maintenance stoppages of the Topping IV, the vacuum distillation, the Coke II and the platforming units. In addition, during 2024 the revamping of the Topping III unit continued, which will allow higher volumes of shale oil to be processed by 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The <span style="font-weight:bold">Plaza Huincul Refinery</span>, located in the Neuqu&#233;n Province, has a nominal capacity of 25.2 kbbl/d. This refinery produces gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, which are sold primarily in nearby areas and in the southern regions of Argentina. Heavier products are transported by pipeline from the Plaza Huincul Refinery to the La Plata Refinery for further processing. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Plaza Huincul Refinery receives its crude oil supplies from the Neuquina basin by pipeline. During 2024, we continued working on a new gasoline stabilization plant and a furnace with completion expected by the first quarter of 2025, which will allow a greater flow of shale oil production. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding investments related to new specifications for sulphur content in fuels (see Note 36.b.2) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements), during 2024, we continued working in the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery to improve the quality of diesel fuel, in a new hydro desulfurization unit II (&#8220;HDS&#8221;), a new hydrogen generator unit II (&#8220;Hydrogen II&#8221;), and the revamping of the HDS I unit. Additionally, in the La Plata Refinery the revamping of the magnaforming unit and the new coke naphtha hydrotreatment plant (&#8220;HTNCB&#8221;) were fully accomplished during 2024, increasing the volume of aromatics allowed for blending. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Biofuels are one of the main supplies for gasoline and diesel production. Law No.&#160;27,640 established the percentages of biofuels that must be added to gasoline and diesel and whose validity was set until December&#160;31, 2030. Gasoline requires a 12.0% blend of ethanol, while the percentage for diesel is 7.5% blend of fatty acid methyl esters (&#8220;FAME&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our refineries are certified under International Organization for Standardization (&#8220;ISO&#8221;) standards. See &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Our environmental, social and governance (&#8220;ESG&#8221;) commitment&#8212;Environmental matters in Argentina&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the renewable energy produced by the Manantiales Behr wind farm (located in the Chubut Province), Los Teros I and II wind farms (located in the Buenos Aires Province) and the Ca&#241;ad&#243;n Le&#243;n wind farm (located in the Santa Cruz Province) represented 36.4% of the electricity consumption of the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery and 0.2% of the La Plata Refinery. See &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business organization&#8212;Gas and Power&#8212;Generation power activities&#8221;. </p>

(&#8220;Oldelval&#8221;), operator of the pipeline. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We also own 3 tanks in the Berisso City, in the Buenos Aires Province, with 90,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> of capacity. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Loma Campana - Lago Pellegrini pipeline allows for the evacuation of conventional and unconventional crude oil from the Vaca Muerta formation. This pipeline is owned by OLCLP, a company owned by YPF (85%) and Tecpetrol (15%), and is operated by a third company, Oldelval. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, we own 33.15% of Terminales Mar&#237;timas Patag&#243;nicas S.A., operator of 2 storage and port facilities: (i)&#160;Caleta C&#243;rdova in the Chubut Province, which has a capacity of 314,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>; and (ii)&#160;Caleta Olivia in the Santa Cruz Province, which has a capacity of 246,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We also have a 30% interest in Oldelval and Oiltanking Ebytem S.A. (&#8220;OTE&#8221;), operator of the maritime terminal in Puerto Rosales, which has a capacity of 480,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We also operate, in Argentina, a network of multiple pipelines for the transportation of refined products with a total length of 1,801 km. We also own 17 storage terminals for distribution of refined products and 7 LPG storage terminals with an aggregate capacity of 1,620,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Three of our storage terminals for distribution are annexed to the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo, La Plata and Plaza Huincul refineries, while 10 have maritime or river connections. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We operate 49 airplane refueling facilities, 40 of which are wholly-owned with a capacity of 22,500 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>, 141 manual fuel dispensers and 13 automatic fuel dispensers. These facilities provide a flexible countrywide distribution system and allow us to facilitate exports. Products are delivered by an exclusive third party tanker truck fleet of 2,400 units. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Midstream Oil division </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Midstream Oil division plays a crucial strategic role in optimizing the development of the Vaca Muerta formation&#8217;s unconventional oil. Aligned with this objective, this division is responsible for ensuring the efficient evacuation of the <span style="white-space:nowrap">ramped-up</span> crude oil production of Argentina, to achieve the required capacity in the shortest time possible, as well as the development of alternative evacuation routes, all aimed at consolidating and supporting YPF&#8217;s strategic plan (see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the&#160;Company&#8212;Business strategy&#8212;Strategic pillars: &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221;&#8221;) and business plans. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF holds an interest of 36% in both parts of the Trans-Andean oil pipeline (Oleoducto Trasandino Argentina S.A. and Oleoducto Trasandino Chile S.A.), which transports crude oil from Argentina to Chile. During 2024, YPF was responsible for shipping more than 5,156 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d of crude oil through this pipeline, which represents 45.7% of the total crude oil transported. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, YPF holds an interest of 75.2% in the transportation concession of the <span style="font-weight:bold">Vaca Muerta Norte oil pipeline (&#8220;VMON&#8221;)</span>, a 151 km pipeline with a capacity of 25,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d, aimed at guaranteeing the supply of the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo refinery and the export of crude oil to Chile. During 2024, VMON led to the transport of 10,258 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d of crude oil, of which 5,895 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d corresponded to YPF. In the third quarter of 2024, the operation of the VMON storage and pumping station &#8220;CABO NOC&#8221; began, with more than 60,000 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> of storage capacity, which represents the first project oriented to ensure storage capacity for the Hub Core. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, progress continues through the <span style="font-weight:bold">Vaca Muerta Sur oil pipeline (&#8220;VMOS&#8221;)</span> aimed to export the production of unconventional crude oil from the Neuquina basin to the Atlantic coast, which will be achieved through the construction of approximately US$ 3&#160;billion and 437 km pipeline connecting towns of Allen and Punta Colorada in the R&#237;o Negro Province, with a maximum design transport capacity of 700 kbbl/d, as well as an onshore terminal with a storage capacity of 3,774 kbbl and an offshore terminal. In the fourth quarter of 2024, YPF together with Pan American Sur S.A. (&#8220;PAS&#8221;), Vista Energy Argentina S.A.U. (&#8220;Vista&#8221;) and Pampa Energ&#237;a S.A. (&#8220;Pampa&#8221;) signed a shareholders&#8217; agreement to create a new company, &#8220;VMOS S.A.&#8221;, whose main purpose is the construction of such oil pipeline (see Note 1 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements). As of the date of this annual report, VMOS pipeline is under construction and is expected to be completed during 2027, alongside the onshore and offshore terminals. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In December 2024, Initial Shipper Transportation Agreements (&#8220;ISTA&#8221;) were signed between VMOS S.A., Shell Western Supply and Trading Limited, and the aforementioned shareholders or their affiliates. Total YPF&#8217;s shipping commitment is for 120 kbbl/d out of total of 450 kbbl/d committed by all the initial shippers. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, VMOS S.A. granted stock options to other companies. As of the date of this annual report, Pluspetrol S.A. (&#8220;Pluspetrol&#8221;), Chevron Argentina S.R.L. (&#8220;Chevron&#8221;), Shell Compa&#241;&#237;a Argentina de Petroleo S.A. (&#8220;Shell&#8221;) and Gas y Petroleo del Neuqu&#233;n S.A. (&#8220;GyP&#8221;) exercised their respective option becoming a shareholder of VMOS S.A., signing their respective ISTA. As of the date of this annual report, YPF&#8217;s shareholding in VMOS S.A. is 26.67%. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March 20, 2025, Resolution No. 302/2025, published in the Official Gazette, on March 21, 2025 approved VMOS S.A.&#8217;s application to the RIGI. The VMOS project, classified as a Long-Term Strategic Export Project in the oil and gas sector, will be developed in R&#237;o Negro with a base capacity of 377,400 bbl/day. The project&#8217;s RIGI adherence date was set as March 6, 2025, under the Bases Law. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In January 2024, the construction of the <span style="font-weight:bold">Vaca Muerta Centro oil pipeline (&#8220;VMOC&#8221;)</span> began, which will connect the Hub Core with the town of Allen in the R&#237;o Negro Province, and which is estimated to be completed in the second quarter of 2025. VMOC will enable evacuation capacity for the oil pipelines of Oldelval and VMOS. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Marketing division </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We market a wide range of refined petroleum and petrochemical products throughout Argentina through an extensive network of sales personnel, <span style="white-space:nowrap">YPF-owned</span> and independent distributors, and a broad retail distribution system. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:center">31 </p>

</div></div>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF sells two types of gasoline: (i) Infinia gasoline, a premium 98 octane gasoline; and (ii) Super gasoline, a regular 95 octane gasoline. In 2024, the premium mix obtained (24.8%) decreased 4.2 percentage points (&#8220;pp&#8221;) compared to the mix obtained in 2023 (29.0%). Additionally, YPF sells two types of diesel: (i) 500 and 800 parts per million (&#8220;ppm&#8221;) of sulphur diesel (&#8220;Low-sulphur diesels&#8221;); and (ii) 10 ppm of sulphur diesel (&#8220;Infinia diesel&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, YPF maintained its leading position in the sale of liquid fuels in Argentina, with a market share of 56.2%. According to information provided by the SE, as of December 31, 2024, our market share of Infinia and Super gasolines was 58.7% and 55.3% respectively, compared to 58.8% and 53.7%, respectively, as of December 31, 2023; and, as of December 31, 2024, our market share of low-sulphur diesels and Infinia diesel was 53.8% and 62.6%, respectively, compared to 56.5% and 62.1%, respectively, as of December 31, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The table below, for each of the periods indicated, provides information about our domestic market liquid fuels sales volumes: </p> <p style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, competitors remained active in communication, promotions, loyalty actions and bank discounts. To enhance brand loyalty, YPF launched campaigns with the aim of positioning itself on the following features: quality, proximity, innovation, avant-garde, trajectory and being an engine of the Argentine economy. Throughout 2024, we showed high presence in all media with campaigns from Infinia, YPF Boxes, YPF&#8217;s convenience store unit (&#8220;Full stores&#8221;) and ServiClub, promoting the quality of products, generating closeness with benefits and improving customer experience. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, YPF consolidated its leadership in digital payments, achieving that almost 4 out of every 10 transactions at its retail service stations were made through the virtual wallet of the YPF App. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The YPF App was a central axis and main driver of this transformation, exceeding 60&#160;million payments during the year, a milestone that reflects the growing and continuous adoption of digital solutions by customers, not only to streamline payments and loyalty but also to improve their experience and personalization. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Focused on the customer and under a vision of continuous improvement and information-based management, the YPF App developed key functionalities such as the renovation of the customers&#8217; home page, the evolution of customers&#8217; money in their account and the interaction with the loyalty program, which allowed it to provide operational efficiencies and competitive advantages. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The expansion of the digital ecosystem and the integration of greater services related to mobility, consolidate the YPF App as an integral tool for YPF&#8217;s relationship with its users. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, Marketing business units were grouped as follows: <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">(i)&#160;Business-to-Customer</span></span> (&#8220;B2C&#8221;) unit; <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">(ii)&#160;Business-to-</span></span> Business (&#8220;B2B&#8221;) unit; (iii)&#160;LPG unit; and (iv)&#160;Chemical unit, focusing on each kind of clients&#8217; requirements<span style="font-style:italic">.</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold">B2C unit </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The B2C unit focuses on delivering the best experience at our retail service stations, based on sustainability, technology, and innovation. Our goal is to provide energy and convenience solutions to our customers in transit. We subdivide the B2C unit into the (i)&#160;Retail unit and (ii)&#160;Convenience Store unit. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our <span style="font-weight:bold">Retail unit</span> sells through the consignment model fuels to the retail service stations. In 2024, we remained as the main fuel retailer in Argentina, with 31.9% of the Argentina&#8217;s retail service stations as of December&#160;31, 2024, according to our estimates. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, the Retail unit&#8217; sales network in Argentina consisted of 1,680 active retail service stations, of which 155 are operated by Operadora de Estaciones de Servicios S.A. (&#8220;OPESSA&#8221;), our wholly-owned subsidiary, 136 are operated by the Autom&#243;vil Club Argentino (&#8220;ACA&#8221;), and the rest are operated by third parties. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, we inaugurated 22 retail service stations, which have impacted 19 districts and 12 Argentine provinces; 68.2% of these retail service stations were new constructions. Among them, the opening of the first service station of the &#8220;proximity station&#8221; (&#8220;ECER&#8221; by its acronym in Spanish) type in the Villa Pehuenia town, in the Neuqu&#233;n Province. In addition, these new service stations include the YPF Xpress model, the first development and implementation in the third-party network, which will have a technology package (consisting of self-service totems on islands and exterior totems for Full stores self-service <span style="white-space:nowrap">pick-up).</span> Additionally, we continued with our infrastructure plan and invested US$ 32&#160;million in image renewal, pumps, tanks, convenience stores (&#8220;Full stores&#8221;), lubrication points, tele measurements and remodeling in retail service stations owned by YPF. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, we continued with the &#8220;Transformation of the Network&#8221; project enabling the installation of a new image on 411 retail service stations (including &#8220;New Full stores image&#8221;) surpassing our annual goal by 19.5%. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Throughout 2024, YPF successfully renewed 94.6% of its expiring contracts with third party retail service station owners, which enabled us to maintain a leading position in the market. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s <span style="font-weight:bold">Convenience Store unit</span> (&#8220;Full stores&#8221;) is a franchise which comprises 1,026 convenience stores. Out of these, we operate 158 through OPESSA, while 868 are operated by third parties. YPF&#8217;s stores franchising model generates income in the form of royalties paid by stores and suppliers, materialized as a percentage of the store&#8217;s sales. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our main strategy for this unit is expansion, and our objective is to transform all the retail service station stores into Full stores franchises. In 2024, our &#8220;CABA Figueroa Alcorta&#8221; Full store (operated by OPESSA) located in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires was granted with the &#8220;Latin American Convenience Retailer of the Year Award&#8221; of the National Association of Convenience Store (&#8220;NACS&#8221;) of the United States. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, we inaugurated 126 new Full stores, increasing the number of stores by 14% compared to 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, we continue working towards achieving operational excellence to deliver the best service and products to our customers. Therefore, concept tests of advanced gastronomic equipment were installed in several stores to support hot&#160;&amp; cold meals categories. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, Full stores sold 217&#160;million units distributed in more than 2,000 stock keeping units (&#8220;SKU&#8217;s&#8221;). The main categories of products sold were coffee, hot&#160;&amp; cold meals, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-alcohol</span> drinks, convenience and kiosk products. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold">B2B unit </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the B2B unit, with focus on the customer, we developed a segment and channel strategy aimed at maximizing value for both YPF and our clients. Our purpose is to promote efficiency in the value chain of our industry segment customers, offering energy solutions, supplies and services. Consequently, by keeping us close to our customers, we developed innovative tailored solutions. We subdivide the B2B unit into (i)&#160;Agriculture unit, (ii)&#160;Industry unit, (iii)&#160;Transport unit, (iv)&#160;Aviation unit, and (v)&#160;Lubricants and Specialties Latam unit. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The <span style="font-weight:bold">Agricultural unit</span> is focused in providing fuel and lubricants to farmers but also small industries and transport companies. As a complement, it provides an extensive portfolio of products and services as fertilizers and crop protection products. At the same time, this unit has been developing and promoting sustainable agronomic practices. Its main goal is to sustain leadership in fuels used in agriculture from initial sowing to final harvesting and maintaining operational excellence throughout its network. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, this strategy was carried out through a network of 100 exclusive dealers, 6 of which are directly operated by YPF. This network is present in 19 Argentine provinces, covering all the agricultural productive areas, offering a complete agro portfolio, which includes fuel, seeds, crop nutrition and crop protection products, lubricants and ensiling bags. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In order to be a point of reference in the industry and stay close to agricultural producers, our business known as &#8220;YPF Agro&#8221; has sustained a constant renewed portfolio of products and commercial conditions for the exchange of grains. Fertilizer and phytosanitary products sales decreased by 24.0% compared to 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, YPF Agro was able to shield its fuels volume with sales 1.8% above those of 2023. Regarding fertilizer sales, as of December&#160;31, 2024, according to our estimates, our fertilizer market share was 11.06% compared to 15.7% in 2023, as our sales decreased by 24% compared to 2023, partly due to a strong policy of reducing working capital aligned to the Company&#8217;s strategy of focusing on its main markets. Regarding crop protection products, we began a thorough change in the business model, halting imports from May 2024, and seeking to enter into a full agreement with a crop protection company to allow them to use YPF Agro dealers in exchange for an annual fee payment. This new business model is expected to enable us to reduce working capital for this product to zero. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, YPF developed crop financing with instruments such as credit cards with local banks. To keep our fuels positioning and volumes we accept several types of grains as payment (bartering operations), mainly soybean, but also corn, rice, wheat, sorghum, sunflower, barley and cotton. This is a widely used form of transaction in the agricultural sector in Argentina </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The <span style="font-weight:bold">Industry unit</span> supplies the entire industry sectors in Argentina, which requires a broad portfolio of products and services to meet customer needs. We supply products such as fuels (diesel, gasoline, jet fuel and fuel oil), lubricants, coal, asphalts, and derivatives (sulphur, CO<sub style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:bottom">2</sub>, decanted oil and aromatic extract), either directly from our refineries to the point of consumption through our own ground and waterway network, or through a network of 16 industrial distributors with national coverage (mining, oil and gas and asphalts). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our purpose is to promote efficiency in the value chain of our Industry unit&#8217;s customers, offering energy solutions, supplies and services. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, we supplied the fuels that third-parties DAPSA and GULF sell at their 252 retail service stations, representing 3.6% of the total market. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our <span style="font-weight:bold">Transport unit</span> provides fuels (diesel and gasoline), lubricants and automotive urea, either directly from our refineries to the point of consumption, or through our network of retail service stations for those clients members of our business known as &#8220;YPF Ruta&#8221;, an integral solution for the management of all types and sizes of fleets of any activity. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, the YPF Ruta App (launched in 2022) achieved a penetration of 7%, with around 1&#160;million transactions per month. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our <span style="font-weight:bold">Aviation unit</span> provides jet fuels, such as jet <span style="white-space:nowrap">A-1</span> fuel in 48 airports and AvGas in 38 airports across Argentina. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, our sales in the aviation unit decreased by 0.9% compared to 2023, and our market share for jet fuel was 54.4%. Specifically, our sales for international flights increased 7.9% compared to 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, the Company decided to leave the operations in the aviation unit in Paraguay and Chile, to focus exclusively on operations in Argentina. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">Lubricants and Specialties Latam unit</span>, we manufacture a wide range of products including motor oil, heavy duty and industrial lubricants for commercialization in retail, wholesale and industrial markets through a grid of dealers and distributors. We have developed our lubricants network in Argentina, known as YPF Boxes, with 426 sales points throughout the country. In the La Plata refinery, we operate a manufacturing facility where we produce lubricants for the domestic and export markets. Our line of automotive lubricants, including mineral and synthetic oils, has been approved by leading global automotive and engine manufacturers, including Ford, GM, Porsche, Scania, Mercedes Benz, Volkswagen, Renault, PSA, Audi, Deutz, Cummins, Volvo, Toyota, MAN Truck, Subaru, Suzuki, Metalfor, Detroit Diesel, ZF, Allison and MTU. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, we launched R&#214;D, a new line of lubricants for motorcycles, with the aim of repositioning YPF within the motorcycling market. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, our lubricants and specialties market share was 34.4%, a decrease of 2.2 pp compared to December&#160;31, 2023, according to the information provided by the SE. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, compared to 2023, sales of our mainstream products (&#8220;PCMO&#8221;) line, ELAION, in the domestic market reached 9,834 m<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>, decreasing by 16%; sales volumes of our heavy-duty motor oil (&#8220;HDMO&#8221;) line, Extravida, decreased by 21.6%; and sales volumes of Azul 32, a product used in vehicles that complies with the emission standard Euro 5 to reduce gas emissions, decreased by 6.7%. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our quality controls ensure that the product reaches the customer in optimal conditions and complies with strict standards. In this sense, we achieved the following certifications: (i)&#160;for lubricants and specialties, ISO 9001: 2015, ISO 14001: 2015, ISO 45001: 2018, IATF 16949-First Edition; and (ii)&#160;for Azul 32, ISO 2224. Additionally, we obtained for Azul 32 a certification as part of the American Petroleum Institute (&#8220;API&#8221;)&#8217;s Diesel Exhaust Fluid Certification Program and German Association of the Automotive Industry (&#8220;VDA&#8221;) renewal agreement to use the AdBlue brand. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify">LPG unit </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Through our <span style="font-weight:bold">LPG unit</span>, we are engaged in the LPG wholesale business, which encompasses LPG storage, logistics and commercialization to domestic and export markets. We obtain LPG from natural gas processing plants and refineries, as well as from third parties. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the domestic market, we sell LPG mainly through distributors that supply the retail market. The LPG unit does not directly supply the retail market, which is supplied by our associate, YPF Gas S.A. (&#8220;YPF Gas&#8221;). During 2024, we sold 22.9% of our LPG production to YPF Gas. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, LPG sales reached 760.3 ktn, compared to 608.9 ktn in 2023. In 2024, 384.1 ktn of total sales were sold in the domestic market, compared to 362.6 ktn in 2023. Our main clients in the domestic market are companies that sell LPG in cylinders or bulk packing to <span style="white-space:nowrap">end-consumers,</span> also providing LPG to households in some regions. Additionally, exports in 2024 reached 376.2 ktn, compared to 246.3 ktn in 2023. The main destinations of these exports were Chile, Paraguay, Uruguay and Brazil. Transportation of LPG to overseas customers is carried out by truck, pipelines and barges. </p>

</div></div>

The use of natural gas as a raw material allows us to monetize reserves, demonstrating the integration between the Chemical unit and the Upstream business segment, while raw materials for petrochemical production in the CIE, including virgin naphtha, propane, butane and kerosene, are supplied mainly by the La Plata refinery. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, 61.3% of our petrochemical sales (including propylene) were made in the domestic market, while we exported the remainder to Mercosur countries, the rest of Latin America, Europe and the United States. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The La Plata petrochemical plant in the CIE and the methanol plant in the Plaza Huincul refinery are certified under ISO standards, see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Our environmental, social and governance (&#8220;ESG&#8221;) commitment&#8212;Environmental matters in Argentina&#8221;. The ISO certifications for each plant cover the following processes: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, the La Plata petrochemical plant in the CIE has been certified under the program &#8220;Responsible Care for the Environment&#8221; by the Argentine Chamber of Chemical and Petrochemical Industry for six consecutive years (2019-2024). Responsible Care for the Environment is a voluntary program that promotes continuous improvement in areas of safety, occupational health and the environment in the chemical industry. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, the production of methanol was affected by the maintenance stoppage of the unit located in the Plaza Huincul refinery. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Trading division </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our Trading division sells refined products and crude oil to international and domestic customers. We also purchase crude oil from domestic oil companies and refined products from international suppliers to meet the requirements of our own industrial system. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, we strengthened the export of Medanito crude oil to Chile using the Trans-Andean oil pipeline, and in 2024, revenue from this operation amounted to US$ 913.6&#160;million. Additionally, we continued with our exports of other varieties of crude oil to different destinations. As a result, in 2024, YPF became Argentina&#8217;s top oil exporter. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, we developed different marketing actions to open new markets for the Vaca Muerta formation&#8217;s crude oil production, ending the year with the conference &#8220;Medanito Roadmap to Global Markets&#8221;, with the objective to promote Medanito crude oil in the international market and position YPF and Argentina as relevant crude oil exporters. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, we export petroleum coke mostly to Brazil and China. We also sustained the supply of butane, MTBE and base oils to a variety of destinations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following table sets forth, for each of the periods indicated, volumes of export sales: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, imports of <span style="white-space:nowrap">low-sulphur</span> diesel, gasoline, AvGas, among others, totaled 2.0 Mbbl, a 81.6% decrease compared to 2023. United States, United Arab Emirates and Italy were the main origin countries of these imports, which we purchased for the resale in the domestic market. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, imports of fertilizers and agrochemicals totaled 0.12&#160;million tn, a 78.3% decrease compared to 2023. China and North Africa were the main destinations of origin of these imports, which we purchased for the resale in the domestic market. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_19"><span style="font-style:italic">Gas and Power </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Natural gas activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, our <span style="font-weight:bold">natural gas activities</span> included the natural gas transportation and commercialization, the storage of produced natural gas, the transportation, conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation of gasoline, propane and butane, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminal in Escobar, the separation of NGLs and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and gasoline through our jointly controlled company Compa&#241;&#237;a Mega S.A. (&#8220;Mega&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, we kept our position as the largest producer of natural gas in Argentina with total natural gas sales of 13,502 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>, which accounted for 28% of the market share (calculated through December 2024, as provided by Ente Nacional Regulador del Gas (&#8220;ENARGAS&#8221;)), with operations in all productive basins: Noroeste, Cuyana, Neuquina, Golfo San Jorge and Austral. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, 87% of our natural gas sales were produced in the Neuquina basin. We believe that natural gas from the Neuquina basin has a competitive advantage compared to natural gas from other regions, since it is strategically located in relation to the principal market of the Buenos Aires Province and is supported by sufficient capacity during most of the year. Our production of natural gas from the Neuquina basin accounted, as of December&#160;31, 2024, for 25% of the market as provided by the IAPG. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Due to the growing development of the Neuquina basin and the continuous decline in other basins, the capacity of the natural gas trunk pipelines connected to the Neuquina basin has become a relevant issue, since most of the pipelines reached full capacity between 2021 and 2022. Such bottlenecks hindered the evacuation of the natural gas produced in the Neuquina basin, mostly during the winter period. In this context, in 2022, the Argentine government through Decree No.&#160;76/2022 granted a transportation concession on the Presidente N&#233;stor Kirchner gas pipeline (&#8220;GPNK&#8221;), later renamed to Gasoducto Perito Francisco Pascasio Moreno (&#8220;GPM&#8221;), to Integraci&#243;n Energ&#233;tica Argentina S.A. (&#8220;IEASA&#8221;, or &#8220;Energ&#237;a Argentina S.A.&#8221;, &#8220;ENARSA&#8221; since August&#160;1, 2022), to contribute to the natural gas production growth and increase our natural gas supply. With the first section of the GPM inaugurated in 2023, in July 2024 the compressor plant at the head of the gas pipeline was put into operation, and in October 2024 another compressor plant was inaugurated. The GPM gas pipeline expanded the natural gas evacuation capacity in the Neuquina basin by 21 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d, contributing to the YPF&#8217;s evacuation of the natural gas production under Plan GasAr stimulus programs. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In December 2024, the Argentine government declared of National Public Interest the initiative of Transportadora Gas del Sur S.A. (&#8220;TGS&#8221;) to expand the GPM gas pipeline and increase natural gas evacuation from the Neuquina basin, which, if implemented, is expected to add 14 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d to the existing 21 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d, bringing the total transportation capacity to 35 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:center">35 </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, we sold 23% of our natural gas volume to local residential distribution companies, 9% to compressed natural gas (&#8220;CNG&#8221;) <span style="white-space:nowrap">end-users,</span> 30% to industrial users (including our affiliates Mega and Profertil S.A. (&#8220;Profertil&#8221;)), 23% to power generation plants (including our jointly controlled company YPF EE), 9% to the Downstream business segment and the remaining 5% was exported. In the CNG market segment, as of December&#160;31, 2024, YPF had a market share of 57%, compared to a market share of 60% as of December&#160;31, 2023, as provided by the ENARGAS. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As part of its <span style="font-weight:bold">natural gas commercialization</span> activities, YPF markets natural gas through long-term and short-term contracts and spot market sales, supplying residential distribution companies, power generation plants, CNG clients, and industrial and commercial clients. The commitments with the residential and power generation segments are within the framework of the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and Plan GasAr 2023-2028. Under such framework, YPF has been awarded base volume contracts of 21.9 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d at an average price of 3.66 US$/MBtu, and peak volumes of 3.25 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d at a price of 6.35 US$/MBtu. Moreover, YPF was awarded an incremental contract for volumes of natural gas from the Noroeste basin according to a maximum incremental production curve at a price of 9.8 US$/MBtu from October 2023 to December 2026 and 6.0 US$/MBtu from January 2027 to December 2028. If the maximum volumes of the incremental natural gas production curve are not obtained, regardless of the cause, and/or there are deviations of the incremental natural gas production curve from the maximum daily amount of natural gas, these events do not constitute a breach of the commitment. For further information see Note 36.d.1) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">natural gas distribution</span> activities, we distribute natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, in which we hold a 70% stake, a natural gas distribution company located in the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires and southern suburbs of the Buenos Aires Province, and one of the main natural gas distributors in Argentina. During 2024, Metrogas distributed 6,657 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> (or 235 bcf) of natural gas to 2.3&#160;million customers. Tariffs that regulate the natural gas distribution market are determined by a complex and regulated framework. For additional information regarding YPF&#8217;s shareholding in Metrogas and Metrogas&#8217; tariff scheme, see Note 36.c.3) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">LNG regasification</span> activities, since 2011, YPF is the operator of UT Escobar (a joint venture with ENARSA), which operates a LNG regasification terminal (&#8220;LNG Escobar&#8221;) located in Escobar, in the Buenos Aires Province. In 2024, through the conversion of LNG into natural gas, LNG Escobar terminal injected 1.6 bm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> (or 55.7 bcf) of natural gas into the Argentine distribution network. Additionally, in 2024, the Company approved an addendum to the contract of the LNG Escobar terminal to extend its validity until January&#160;31, 2027. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">LNG liquefaction</span> activities, in December 2024, in line with the Company&#8217;s forth pillar of its &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221; plan (see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business strategy&#8212;Strategic pillars: &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221;&#8221;), YPF and Shell Argentina S. A. (&#8220;Shell&#8221;) signed a Project Development Agreement for the evaluation and later execution of basic engineering for the Argentina LNG project. The scope of the agreement is to jointly develop a liquefaction capacity of 10&#160;million tn/y. YPF and Shell expect to award front end engineering designs in 2025. The onboarding of this new partner concludes the previously Join Study and Development Agreement signed with Petronas in September 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the <span style="font-weight:bold">natural gas transportation</span> activities, natural gas is delivered by us through our own gathering systems and through the midstream companies such as Gasoducto del Pac&#237;fico (Argentina) S.A. (&#8220;GPA&#8221;) (in which we have a 10% equity stake) and Transportadora de Gas del Sur S.A. (&#8220;TGS&#8221;) from each of the major basins to the TGS and TGN trunk pipelines. Additionally, YPF provides midstream services, such as natural gas transportation and processing, through its own facilities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding <span style="font-weight:bold">natural gas storage</span> capacity, we utilize natural underground structures located close to consuming markets as underground natural gas storage facilities, storing limited volumes of natural gas during periods of low demand and prices and selling the stored natural gas during periods of high demand and prices, with the purpose of getting the seasonal price differential. In 2024, we extracted 109.3 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> of natural gas from Diadema, our principal natural gas storage facility located in the Patagonia region, near the Comodoro Rivadavia City in the Chubut Province, and sold it to our clients. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We carry out <span style="font-weight:bold">NGLs</span> activities through several plants for the processing of NGLs that we own and operate, such as the Turboexpander Loma La Lata (&#8220;Tex LLL&#8221;) plant, the El Porton plant, the Turboexpander Loma Negra (&#8220;Tex Loma Negra&#8221;) plant, and through Mega, a company in which we have a 38% equity stake and we jointly control with Petrobras (34%) and Dow Chemical (28%), which operates a NGLs separation plant located in the Loma La Lata block, in the Neuqu&#233;n Province; a NGLs fractioning plant, which produces ethane, propane, butane and gasoline located in the Bah&#237;a Blanca City, in the Buenos Aires Province; a pipeline that transports the NGLs produced in the Loma La Lata block to the Bah&#237;a Blanca City; and transportation, storage and port facilities in the NGLs fractioning plant, with an aggregate maximum annual production capacity of 1.6&#160;million tons of gasoline, LPG and ethane and with YPF being Mega&#8217;s main supplier of natural gas for the development of these activities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During the second quarter of 2024, the revamping of the Tex LLL plant was finalized and the full operation mode of the plant (LPG and gasolines recovery) began, which increased the processing capacity of the Neuquina basin by 6 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d and over 600 tn/d of NGLs, allowing the natural gas to be conditioned in order to improve the flow in the evacuation network. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As part of the construction of the <span style="white-space:nowrap">two-phase</span> network for the evacuation of the associated natural gas from the northern area of the Vaca Muerta formation, during the third quarter of 2024, the construction of a 75 km and <span style="white-space:nowrap">16-inch</span> gas pipeline with a capacity of 4.5 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d to the El Port&#243;n industrial complex (&#8220;CIEP&#8221;) began, which will allow the processing of such associated natural gas in the CIEP, where there are several cryogenic and compression power plants for its treatment. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the construction of 17 km and <span style="white-space:nowrap">8-inch</span> for the Las Tacanas gas pipeline was finalized, which allows the evacuation of 0.7 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d of natural gas from Aguada Villanueva, Meseta Buena Esperanza and Las Tacanas blocks to the facilities of the southern region of the Vaca Muerta formation where the Tex Loma Negra plant with LPG recovery can treat this rich natural gas. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of this annual report, Mega&#8217;s project for the construction of a new fractioning module in the NGLs fractioning plant in the Bah&#237;a Blanca City is being executed, expecting start up by the first quarter of 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Generation power activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, our <span style="font-weight:bold">generation power activities</span> included the generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy through our jointly controlled company YPF EE (commercially known as &#8220;YPF Luz&#8221;) including its subsidiary Central Dock Sud S.A. (&#8220;CDS&#8221;), and our jointly controlled company CT Barrag&#225;n S.A. (&#8220;CTB&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, we participated directly and, indirectly through YPF EE and CTB, in 16 power generation plants, with an aggregate installed capacity of 4,240 MW. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, YPF EE kept its position as one of the strongest competitors in the electrical generation market in Argentina, being the biggest player in the private market (Mercado a T&#233;rmino de Energ&#237;as Renovables or &#8220;MATER&#8221;) with 25.8% of the market share and holding the second place in renewable energy generation with 9.4% of the market share, as provided by Compa&#241;&#237;a Administradora del Mercado Mayorista El&#233;ctrico S.A. (&#8220;CAMMESA&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, YPF EE generated 13,236 GWh through its power plants located in Tucum&#225;n, San Juan, C&#243;rdoba, Buenos Aires, Neuqu&#233;n, Santa Cruz and Chubut, presenting an increase in power generation of 14.0% as compared to 2023. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:center">36 </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The average electricity cost was 71.4 US$/MWh, a 0.3% decrease compared to 2023 (the average cost in Argentine pesos was 66,174 Ps./MWh, an 216.6% increase compared to 2023). For additional information regarding remuneration of power generation units not committed under contracts, see Note 36.c.5) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;5, 2023, the SE through Resolution No.&#160;59/2023 authorized CAMMESA to enter into contracts with electric power generating companies whose combined cycles power plants were under the spot remuneration scheme, with the goal of encouraging the necessary investments to the execution of programmed maintenance, and thus improving the thermal electric power availability of the Ministry of Energy and Mining (&#8220;MINEM&#8221;). YPF EE and CDS signed contracts with CAMESSA under the mentioned Resolution. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding the <span style="font-weight:bold">renewable energy market</span>, the Manantiales Behr, Los Teros I, Los Teros II, Ca&#241;ad&#243;n Le&#243;n and General Levalle wind farms and the Zonda solar farm, all wholly-owned by YPF EE, represented 9.4% of renewable power generation in Argentina in 2024 and 9.8% of renewable electric power installed capacity as of December&#160;31, 2024, as provided by CAMMESA. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In May 2024, the construction of the fifth wind farm, Parque E&#243;lico CASA, to be located in the Olavarr&#237;a City in the Buenos Aires Province commenced, with an estimated investment of US$ 80&#160;million, which will have a total installed capacity of 63 MW, from which 28 MW will be allocated to the self-generating power of Cementos Avellaneda S.A. and the rest to supply the industrial demand within the MATER. This wind farm is projected to be completed and commissioned by the first quarter of 2026. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In October 2024, the construction of the second solar farm for electricity generation, El Quemado, to be located in the Mendoza Province commenced, with an estimated investment of US$ 210&#160;million, which will have an installed capacity of 305 MW. This solar farm is projected to be completed and commissioned by the first half of 2026. Additionally, in October 2024, it was approved by the YPF EE&#8217;s board of directors the application for adherence to the Large Investment Incentive Regime (&#8220;RIGI&#8221;) submitted by Luz del Campo S.A., a wholly-owned subsidiary of YPF EE. Such adherence was approved by the Ministry of Economy in January 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In August 2024, General Levalle wind farm, located in the C&#243;rdoba Province, started its commercial operations in stages reaching a total installed capacity of 155 MW by December 2024. The energy produced in this wind farm is delivered to private off takers under several Power Purchase Agreements in the MATER. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For additional information on related regulations, see Note 36.c.5) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Fertilizers activities</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, our activities in the fertilizer market included the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through our jointly controlled company Profertil, one of the market leaders of fertilizers in the Southern Cone. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, Profertil produced 1.3&#160;million tons of urea and 0.8&#160;million tons of ammonia through its production facility in the Bah&#237;a Blanca City. Additionally, Profertil marketed other nutrients and special blends of prepared land to optimize soil performance. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="font-style:italic">Natural gas delivery commitments and supply contracts </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We are committed to providing fixed and determinable quantities of natural gas in the near future under a variety of contractual arrangements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, we were contractually committed to deliver 73,020 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> (or 2,575 bcf) of natural gas in the future (without considering interruptible export supply contracts), of which 25,816 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup> (or 910 bcf) will have to be delivered from 2025 through 2026. The aforementioned figures contain the commitments within the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and Plan GasAr 2023-2028 stimulus programs (see Note 36.d.1) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements). According to our estimations, as of December&#160;31, 2024, our contractual delivery commitments for the next two years could be met with our own production and, if necessary, with purchases from third parties. For further information regarding our hydrocarbons production see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business organization&#8212;Upstream&#8212;Oil and gas reserves&#8212;Oil and gas production, production costs and sales prices&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Since 2004 the Argentine government has established regulations for both the international and domestic natural gas markets, which have affected the ability of Argentine producers to export natural gas. Consequently, in the past, because of actions taken by the Argentine government, we have been forced in many instances to partially or fully suspend natural gas export deliveries that are contemplated by our contracts with export customers. Thus, we could not meet our export commitments and were forced to declare force majeure under our natural gas export sales agreements, although certain counterparties have rejected our position. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The current regulatory framework allows firm and interruptible exports, subject to the relevant authorization from the SE. In 2024, the SE allowed for the request of export firm permits on a multi-year basis subject to certain limits and conditions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January&#160;5, 1995, March&#160;11, 1997, and November&#160;13, 2001 (&#8220;GSA 2001&#8221;) we committed to supply natural gas to the Methanex S.A. (&#8220;Methanex&#8221;)&#8217;s plant in Cabo Negro, Punta Arenas, in Chile, under agreements, of which only GSA 2001 for 1.1 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d is currently in force. Pursuant to the Argentine government intervention, deliveries have been interrupted since 2007. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As a result of negotiations with Methanex, YPF entered into various agreements that involved investments by YPF in hydrocarbon exploration in Chile, tolling agreements and, as of 2019, firm and interruptible natural gas supply contracts, in order to replace the commitments under the original agreements in accordance with the natural gas export regulations in force in Argentina, which include an agreement between the parties for the recovery of volumes not delivered for regulatory reasons. In August 2024, YPF entered into a muti-year term firm agreement with Methanex that allows the supply of the remaining natural gas volumes originally committed under the GSA 2001 until December 2025 and the natural gas volumes agreed to be recovered with Methanex until November 2027. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In April 2023, the Argentine government called for the submission of export sales agreements in order to allow firm natural gas exports through Gasoducto Gas Andes Argentina S.A. (&#8220;Gas Andes&#8221;) from October 2023 to April 2024 (the volume assigned to YPF was 0.8 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d), and from GPA from October 2023 to December 2024 (the volume assigned to YPF was 0.3 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d). In September 2023, the Argentine government authorized YPF to export natural gas from May 2024 to September 2024 and from October 2024 to December 2024 for 1.5 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, the Argentine government called for the submission of export sales agreements in order to evaluate firm natural gas exports authorizations on a yearly basis. Maximum firm potential volumes to be contracted and applied to be granted for a firm export authorization for 2025 were, in the case of YPF, up to 2.1 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from January to April, 1.6 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from May to September and 2.1 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from October to December. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, the Argentine government allowed for the request of firm export authorizations on a multi-year basis, from 2026 to 2028. The potential contractual volumes allowed to be requested for firm export permits to YPF were 50% of those allocated in 2025 (1.0 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from January to April, 0.8 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from May to September and 1.0 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from October to December). The Argentine government also allowed the possibility for non-Plan GasAr 2023-2028 participants to request for multi yearly export permits for a total of up to: (i)&#160;from de Neuquina basin (from January to December), 2025: 1.5 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d and 2026-2028: 0,8 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d; and (ii)&#160;from the Austral basin (for the summer period, from October to December and from January to April), 2025: 1.0 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d and 2026-2028: 0.5 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d. As of the date of this annual report, YPF has applied for: (i)&#160;from the Neuquina basin: 1.5 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from January to April 2025, 1.6 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from May to September 2025, 1.2 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from October to December 2025, 0.3 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from January to April 2026, 0.4 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from May to September 2026 and 0.3 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from October to December 2026; and (ii)&#160;from de Austral basin: 1.1 Mm<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">3</sup>/d from September 2024 to November 2027. </p>
