 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Safety of people </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In recent years, we have made significant progress both in the implementation of technical occupational safety measures (all our facilities have physical barriers to prevent accidents) and in our regulatory and management systems. A core objective is to continue strengthening a proactive safety and self-care culture embedded in everything we do, based on the 10 Golden Rules for Saving Lives, leadership, long-term commitment, continuous learning and monitoring and safety indicators. During 2024, we implemented specific programs focused on the most critical risks in terms of potential impact, aligned with best practices. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For those facilities that are subject to structural and procedural modifications, it is necessary to analyze beforehand the scope and consequences of potential accidents through studies concerning specific risks. When our personnel and contractors must perform <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-routine</span> tasks, in situ methodologies known as <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">permits-to-work</span></span> are set in place. All occupational accidents are registered in the Integral Management System for Operational Excellence, including not only the accident-related data, but also the root causes and the improvement actions that arise from the analysis of each accident. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Occupational safety training </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Basic training starts with a general safety induction as well as specific training focused on the function, which all employees receive directly and through contractors. Simultaneously, safety content for the entire organization is continuously fostered through actions on corporate online platforms to raise awareness and inform. Each Vice Presidency also conducts specific actions according to its needs and focuses on each contractor. These actions are communicated to the contracting company, through the contract inspectors, which act as a link between YPF and the contracting company. In 2024, we continued to reinforce awareness of our 10 Golden Rules for Saving Lives, with a special focus on those in operational roles. Each business unit continued to train its own personnel and contractors focused on the most important risks of their activities. In addition, a review of the complete regulatory framework of each 10 Golden Rules for Saving Lives was carried out. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We also continued the safe driving program, implemented in previous years, in order to reinforce the reduction in the accident frequency rate of vehicle accidents in recent years. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Emergency response </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company has an Emergency and Crisis Management system, which focuses on prevention and strengthening the Company&#8217;s resilience to unforeseen events. This system aligns prevention, preparedness, response and recovery activities including incident response management, business continuity management and crisis management. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Safety incident occurrence </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, the frequency index of safety incidents decreased compared to 2023. Incident investigation, recording and analysis have been essential to achieving these results as they allowed us to develop and implement improvement actions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The identification of risk is based on an analysis of risks with potential impact on workers, communities, the environment, assets and the business. We use different inputs as reports from reinsurers, accident investigations, audits, contractors and environmental monitoring, among others. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In case of an undesired event, the action protocols are applied, which include organizational and operative aspects to carry out containment, evaluation and control actions. In all cases, the priority is people care. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">After the response and containment of the event, the necessary actions are taken to return to operational conditions or to recondition the affected areas, if it is required. In addition, the pertinent records are made and subsequently the investigation of the case is carried out. The lessons learned are used to adapt the emergency and crisis management system. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_26"><span style="font-style:italic">Insurance </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The scope and coverage of the insurance policies and indemnification obligations discussed below are subject to change, and such policies are subject to cancellation in certain circumstances. In addition, the indemnification provisions of certain of our drilling, maintenance and other service contracts may be subject to different interpretations, and enforcement of those provisions may be limited by public policy and other considerations. We may also be subject to potential liabilities for which we are not insured or in excess of our insurance coverage, including liabilities discussed in &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may not have sufficient insurance to cover all the operating hazards to which we are subject&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Oil and gas activities are subject to significant economic, social, environmental and operational risks&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may incur significant costs and liabilities related to environmental, health and safety matters&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We insure our operations against inherent risks in the oil and gas industry, including loss of or damage to property and our equipment, <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">control-of-well</span></span> incidents, loss of production, business interruption, removal of debris, sudden and accidental pollution, damage and clean up and third-party claims, including personal injury and loss of life, among other business risks. Our insurance policies are typically renewable annually and generally contain limits, exclusions and deductibles determined by (i)&#160;risk management assessment surveys conducted by international companies, (ii)&#160;terms offered by insurance and reinsurance markets, and (iii)&#160;the risk retention policy defined by the Company. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our liability insurance policy covering our operations provides third-party liability coverage up to US$ 400&#160;million per event. Certain types of incidents, such as intentional and/or <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-sudden</span> and/or <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-accidental</span> pollution are excluded from the insurance policy&#8217;s coverage. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our material damage and business interruption insurance policy provides coverage for physical loss or damage in respect of, but not limited to, onshore and offshore property of any kind and description, up to US$ 1.5&#160;billion and up to US$ 800&#160;million for each and every incident for downstream and upstream operations, respectively, but up to US$ 1.5&#160;billion for each and every incident combined for both types of operations, with different deductible amounts depending on the type of coverage. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Furthermore, we maintain life insurance for employees, automobile, cargo and transportation, as well as insurance against construction risks on a <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">case-by-case</span></span> basis, and minor works or assemblies for assets in operation. We do not currently maintain insurance coverage for cybersecurity incidents, see &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may suffer information technology system failures, network disruptions and breaches in data security&#8221; and &#8220;Item 16K. Cybersecurity&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our insurance policies are subject to deductibles, limits, exclusions and limitations, and there is no assurance that such coverage will adequately protect us against liability from all possible consequences and damages associated with our activities. </p>

Operating and financial review and prospects&#8212;Statements of comprehensive income breakdown&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our business is inherently volatile due to the influence of external factors, such as those listed above. Consequently, our past financial condition, results of operations and the trends indicated by such results and financial condition may not be indicative of the financial conditions, results of operations or trends in future periods. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_34"><span style="font-style:italic">Macroeconomic conditions </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Overview </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Substantially all of our revenues are derived from our operations in Argentina and, therefore, are subject to prevailing macroeconomic conditions in Argentina. Consequently, changes in economic, political and regulatory conditions in Argentina have had and are expected to continue to have a significant impact on our business, financial position and results of operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In recent years, the Argentine economy experienced significant volatility characterized by periods of low or negative growth, macroeconomic instability, currency devaluations and high variable levels of inflation. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">According to the &#8220;Estimador Mensual de Actividad Econ&#243;mica&#8221; report (an activity level progress report in Argentina) published in February 2025 by the Instituto Nacional de Estad&#237;stica y Censos (&#8220;INDEC&#8221;), the economic activity in Argentina in December 2024 showed a positive variation of 5.5% compared to December 2023, while the cumulative variation for 2024 recorded a decrease of 1.8% compared to 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In terms of inflation, Argentina has recently confronted an acceleration of inflation indexes, which significantly increased during the last months of 2023 and through February 2024, when a slowdown in inflation rates was observed. During 2024, the consumer price index (&#8220;CPI&#8221;) published by the INDEC presented a cumulative increase of 117.8%, while the wholesale internal price index (&#8220;WPI&#8221;), also published by the INDEC, presented a cumulative increase of 67.1%. During 2023, the CPI presented a cumulative increase of 211.4%, while the WPI presented a cumulative increase of 276.4%. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In terms of trade balance, according to the data published by the INDEC in the Argentine Commercial Trade Report, the surplus in Argentina&#8217;s balance of trade account totaled US$ 18.9&#160;billion during 2024, while a deficit of US$ 6.9&#160;billion was recorded in 2023, explained by a decrease in imports of 17.5% and an increase of exports of 19.4%, compared to 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With respect to local market exchange rate conditions, the Ps./US$ exchange rate stood at 1,030.50 Ps./US$ as of December&#160;31, 2024, having increased 27.7% from its value of 806.95 Ps./US$ as of December&#160;31, 2023, according to the Banco de la Naci&#243;n Argentina (&#8220;BNA&#8221;). The average exchange rate for 2024 amounted to 914.67 Ps./US$ and was 210.1% higher than the average recorded during 2023 of 294.95 Ps./US$. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:center">48 </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In January 2024, the IMF modified the targets of the agreement under the Extended Fund Facility Program with Argentina based on the stabilization plans of the new administration of the Argentine government, approving the extension of the program through December&#160;31, 2024 and adjusting the disbursement schedule under the program. In June 2024, the IMF concluded the eighth quarterly review and indicated that the targets had been overachieved, enabling a disbursement of US$ 0.8&#160;billion. Subsequently, on March&#160;11, 2025, DNU No.&#160;179/2025 was published by which the Argentine Executive Branch approved to enter into a new <span style="white-space:nowrap">10-year</span> EFF with the IMF, the purpose of which will be mainly to refinance liabilities, including <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-transferable</span> treasury bills and the amounts pending amortization under the current EFF. On March 19, 2025, the Chamber of Deputies of the Argentine Congress approved the DNU No. 179/2025. As of the date of this annual report, this EFF has not been executed. For more information, see &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;Argentina&#8217;s ability to obtain financing from international capital markets could be limited, which may have an impact on our ability to access those markets&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Increased interest rates, uncertainty and illiquidity in credit and capital markets may impair our ability to obtain credit and financing, or obtain them on acceptable terms&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding the local macroeconomic context, there are relevant challenges to be solved related to the macroeconomic imbalances of the Argentine economy, such as reducing the inflation rate, maintaining a trade and fiscal surplus, accumulating reserves, managing the public debt and improving the competitiveness of the local industry. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In this sense, the measures adopted by the Argentine government focus on the deregulation of the Argentine economy and on the reduction of public spending and monetary issuance, which have been implemented through Decree No.&#160;70/2023 (see Note 36.i) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements) and the Law of Bases and Starting Points for the Freedom of Argentines No.&#160;27,742 (&#8221;Bases Law&#8221;), published in the Official Gazette on July&#160;8, 2024 (see Note 36.j) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Hydrocarbon market </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our pricing policy for fuels considers several factors such as international and local crude oil prices, international prices of refined products, processing and distribution costs, biofuel prices, exchange rate volatility, local demand and supply, competition, inventories, export duties, local taxation, domestic margins for our products, among others. Our expectation is to align our local prices to those of international markets over time, while seeking to maintain a reasonable relationship between local crude oil and fuel prices, without considering short-term fluctuations, however, we cannot assure you that some critical factors that are considered in our pricing policy (including, but not limited to, changes in the exchange rates, or in international prices or potential legal or regulatory or other limitations that affect the ability of the market to face changes in products prices), will not have an adverse impact on our ability to maintain such relations, considering that volatility and uncertainty in the international prices of crude oil and derivatives and the fluctuations in the value of the Argentine peso will probably continue in the near future. For more information, see &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;Our business is largely dependent upon economic conditions in Argentina&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Pricing of our products in Argentina and fluctuations in international prices of oil and refined products may adversely affect our results of operations&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, local crude oil was negotiated between producers and refiners. Brent crude oil price trading at an average of 79.8 US$/bbl in 2024 (a 2.9% decrease compared to 2023). As for the local Medanito and Escalante crude oils, the average prices were 68.9 US$/bbl and 72.7 US$/bbl, respectively for 2024, compared to the average prices of 60.8 US$/bbl and 68.7 US$/bbl, respectively for 2023. See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Pricing of our products in Argentina and fluctuations in international prices of oil and refined products may adversely affect our results of operations&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2023, we started to export crude oil to Chile. With respect to this export destination, during 2024, we exported 11,870&#160;thousand barrels (US$ 914 million), while during 2023 we exported 3,786&#160;thousand barrels (US$ 310 million). In the fourth quarter of 2024 there was a 106.7% increase in our exported volume with respect to the fourth quarter of 2023 driven by the <span style="white-space:nowrap">start-up</span> of the VMON in November 2023. During the fourth quarter of 2024, we exported 3,581&#160;thousand barrels (US$ 257 million), compared to 1,732&#160;thousand barrels (US$ 141 million) in the fourth quarter of 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As for natural gas market, the Argentine government has established domestic market natural gas production incentive programs, which remain in force as of the date of this annual report. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_35"><span style="font-style:italic">Statements of comprehensive income breakdown </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The information below should be read in conjunction with the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements included in this annual report. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Summarized of consolidated statement of comprehensive </span><span style="text-decoration:underline">income</span> </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

On July&#160;1, 2024, certain assets related to the exploration, exploitation and production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes, which were formerly included in Upstream business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. Consequently, the comparative information for fiscal years ended December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022 has been restated. Nonetheless, we consider these changes immaterial. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF explains its net profit or loss through the operating profit or loss, which is managed through its business segments, and its net financial results and income tax charge, which are managed on a consolidated basis. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For information about our business segments see &#8220;Item 4. Likewise, the daily production of NGLs increased by 0.4% in 2024 compared to 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the operating profit of the Upstream business segment was US$ 515&#160;million, compared to the operating loss of US$ 1,915&#160;million during 2023. This represents an increase in operating profit of US$ 2,430&#160;million mainly explained by: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Consolidation adjustments </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The main transactions between business segments are generated by: (i)&#160;the sales of crude oil and natural gas produced by the Upstream business segment to the Downstream and Gas and Power business segments, respectively, and (ii)&#160;the sales of gasoline, propane and butane produced by the Gas and Power business segment to the Downstream business segment. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Consolidation adjustments during 2023, which correspond to the elimination of operating profit or loss results between the different business segments that have not involved third parties, had a positive amount of US$ 56&#160;million compared to a negative amount of US$ 36&#160;million in 2022. In 2023 and 2022, changes in transfer prices reflect market price variations. See Note 5 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_37"><span style="font-style:italic">Liquidity and capital resources </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Liquidity </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company closely monitors liquidity levels in order to meet its cash needs from business operational and financial obligations. We have a conservative approach to the management of our liquidity which consists mainly of: (i)&#160;cash and cash equivalents (cash in hand, demand deposits with banks and other short-term highly liquid investments with original maturities of up to 3 months); (ii) investments in financial assets (bills and bonds issued by the BCRA and the Argentine Government, corporate bonds and promissory notes); and iii) daily account overdrafts and/or other short-term financing agreements with banks and settlement and clearing agents (&#8220;ALyC&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish). Based on the discussion below, we consider that our working capital is reasonable for the Company&#8217;s present liquidity requirements. Our management believes that our cash balances and available credit facilities are sufficient to meet our present liquidity requirements. If we determine that our cash requirements exceed the amount of cash and cash equivalents we have on hand at the time, we may seek to issue debt securities or obtain credit facilities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In order to fulfill our financial needs, the access to bank credit facilities together with local and international debt capital markets, provide a material source of funding in the short-term and long-term. The Company issued several series of negotiable obligations (&#8220;NO&#8221;) in the local and international markets at different currencies, interest rates and tenors under the Medium-Term Notes (&#8220;MTN&#8221;) Programs and the Frequent Issuer Regime. All such securities are authorized to be traded on the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange (&#8220;BYMA&#8221;) and/or the A3 Mercados S.A. (former Mercado Abierto Electr&#243;nico S.A.) (&#8220;A3 Mercados&#8221;) in Argentina, while international issues are authorized for trading on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange. For additional information about the outstanding notes of the Company as of December&#160;31, 2024, see Notes 4, 22 and 39 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Based on the level of our outstanding loans and our dependence on capital to maintain a significant investment program, we have a recurrent need for debt funding to refinance maturing debt and finance our capital investments. We are therefore affected by the local and global macroeconomic environments as well as local and global financial market conditions. This exposes us to certain risks, including, among others, market risk (exchange rate risk, interest rate risk and price risk), liquidity risk and credit risk. For information related to financial risk management see Note 4 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;Our business is largely dependent upon economic conditions in Argentina&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;Argentina&#8217;s ability to obtain financing from international capital markets could be limited, which may have an impact on our ability to access those markets&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Given the restrictions imposed by the BCRA on access to the foreign exchange market (see Note 36.h) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements and &#8220;Item 10. Additional information&#8212;Exchange regulations&#8221;) and the potential loosening of such restrictions, the Company may be affected in the event of exchange rate fluctuations, which has motivated, in the past years, an active strategy in the Company&#8217;s liquidity management. As of December&#160;31, 2024, liquidity of YPF, considering cash and cash equivalents and investments in financial assets current, was comprised 40.2% in Argentine pesos (approximately 9% hedged in U.S. dollars) and 59.8% in other hard currencies (mainly U.S. dollars). See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;We may be exposed to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates&#8221;. </p>

We may, from time to time, make additional repurchases of, or effect other transactions relating to, our publicly traded bonds if, in our own judgment, the market conditions are attractive. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;28, 2018, YPF S.A. registered as &#8220;Frequent Issuer No.&#160;4&#8221;, under the simplified Regime for Frequent Capital Markets&#8217; Issuers (&#8220;R&#233;gimen Simplificado para Emisores Frecuentes&#8221;) created by the CNV in June 2018. This Regime seeks to speed up internal authorization processes within the CNV to promote the development of the local capital markets, while also generating more efficient controls. Also, this Regime allows frequent issuers such as YPF S.A. to significantly reduce the timeline of the offering process, which in turn provides flexibility to take advantage of favorable market conditions in local and international markets. On January&#160;7, 2021, the Board of Directors authorized an increase of the issuance of NO for up to an additional outstanding amount of US$ 6,500&#160;million which was subsequently approved by the CNV through Resolution No.&#160;20,939 dated January 27, 2021. On March&#160;6, 2025 the Board of Directors authorized to ratify the frequent issuer condition for an amount of up to US$ 382&#160;million available to be used for future issuances (which can be further increased). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following table sets forth information regarding the expected maturity dates of our loans (principal amount plus accrued interest): </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January&#160;2, 2025, YPF S.A. announced an offer to purchase the Class&#160;XXXIX NO due July 2025 issued under the 2008 MTN Program for a total principal amount of US$ 757&#160;million at a price equal to the principal plus a premium and unpaid accrued interest. Having received and accepted purchase orders for US$ 315&#160;million, on January&#160;17, 2025, 42% of the amount of such NO was fully paid. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January&#160;17, 2025, YPF S.A. issued in the international market the Class&#160;XXXIV NO due 2034 for a nominal amount of US$ 1,100&#160;million at a rate of 8.25%. The principal amount will be amortized in three consecutive annual installments of 30% in January 2032 and 2033 and 40% in January 2034. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January&#160;18, 2025, YPF S.A. announced the repurchase of the remaining Class&#160;XXXIX NO at a price equal to the principal amount plus a premium and unpaid accrued interest. The repurchase became effective on February&#160;18, 2025, and thus, YPF S.A. cancelled all of the Class&#160;XXXIX NO. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;27, 2025, YPF S.A. issued in the local market the Class&#160;XXXV and Class&#160;XXXVI NO for US$ 140&#160;million maturing on February&#160;27, 2027, and US$ 59&#160;million maturing on August&#160;27, 2025, respectively. The Class&#160;XXXV NO accrue interest quarterly at a fixed annual rate of 6.25% and the Class&#160;XXXVI NO accrue and pay interest at maturity at a fixed rate of 3.50%. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For details on the interest rates on our loans, including our NO, see Note 22 to the Audited Financial Consolidated Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For a description of our exposure to market risk, see &#8220;Item 11. Quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk&#8221; and Notes 4 and 22 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Covenants in our indebtedness</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Most of the Company&#8217;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial covenants mainly consisting in the limitation of incurrence on additional debt when exceeding the Company&#8217;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of default triggered by materially adverse judgments (see Notes 17, 33 and 34 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements), among others. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under the terms of the financial loan agreements and NO, if the Company breaches a covenant and does not remedy such breach within the stipulated cure period, the Company would be in default, which could result in the acceleration of amounts due and would affect the Company&#8217;s liquidity. In addition, given that the majority of the Company&#8217;s loans contain cross-default provisions, a default could result in the acceleration of its obligations under other facilities. </p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Net cash flows from operating activities in 2024 amounted to US$ 5,869&#160;million compared to US$ 5,913&#160;million in 2023; this decrease of US$ 44&#160;million is primarily due to lower dividends received in 2024. Net cash flows from operating activities in 2023 amounted to US$ 5,913&#160;million compared to US$ 5,693&#160;million in 2022; this increase of US$ 220&#160;million or 3.9% is primarily due to higher dividends received in 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Net cash flows used in investing activities in 2024 amounted to US$ 5,511&#160;million compared to US$ 5,332&#160;million in 2023; this increase of US$ 179&#160;million was primarily due to lower proceeds from sales of financial assets, net for US$ 323&#160;million (proceeds from sales of financial assets and interests received from financial assets, net of payments from purchase of financial assets), and higher proceeds from concessions, assignment agreements and sales of assets for US$ 127&#160;million. Net cash flows used in investing activities in 2023 amounted to US$ 5,332&#160;million compared to US$ 4,016&#160;million in 2022; this increase of US$ 1,316&#160;million was primarily due to higher acquisitions of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets for US$ 1,667&#160;million, partially offset by lower payments from purchase of financial assets, net for US$ 329&#160;million (payments from purchase of financial assets, net of proceeds from sales of financial assets and interests received from financial assets). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Net cash flows used in financing activities in 2024 amounted to US$ 293&#160;million mainly due to payments of interest for US$ 707&#160;million, payments of leases for US$ 400&#160;million, and repayments of account overdrafts, net for US$ 48&#160;million, partially offset by proceeds from loans net of debt repayments of US$ 865&#160;million (proceeds from loans net of payments of loans). Net cash flows from financing activities in 2023 amounted to US$ 278&#160;million mainly due to proceeds from loans net of debt repayments of US$ 1,271&#160;million (proceeds from loans net of payments of loans), partially offset by payments of interest for US$ 623&#160;million, and payments of leases for US$ 359&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Material cash requirements</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following paragraphs set forth our main material commitments under commercial contracts as of December&#160;31, 2024: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;text-align:justify">Purchases of goods and services: Purchase obligations are obligations under contractual agreements to purchase goods or services, including investments projects. These obligations enforceable and legally binding on the Company and specify all significant terms, including fixed or minimum quantities to be purchased; fixed, minimum, or variable price provisions; and the timing of the transaction. For obligations with cancellation provisions, we considered the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cancellable</span> portion of the agreement or the minimum cancellation fee. In addition, purchase commitments under commercial agreements that do not provide for a total fixed amount have been determined using our best estimates. Accordingly, our actual purchase obligations may differ from the estimated amounts as of December 31, 2024. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, the Company was committed to purchase goods and services for approximately US$ 6,490&#160;million, of which US$ 1,235&#160;million correspond to purchases maturing in less than one year. Our analysis was focused on quantitatively and/or qualitatively significant contracts (the contracts not analyzed are not quantitatively and/or qualitatively material to our business as a whole). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The expected timing for payments under these purchase obligations is estimated based on current information. Timing of payments and actual amounts paid may be different, depending on the time of receipt of goods or services, or changes to agreed-upon amounts. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

This disposal of assets related to mature fields (&#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221;) is consistent with the Company&#8217;s management plans, which considers that the rationalization of the conventional Upstream portfolio is one of the drivers on which the YPF&#8217;s strategy is based, with focus on activities and investments in unconventional fields, with the objective of maximizing value for the Company, its shareholders and investors. As of December&#160;31, 2024, based on the evaluation of the changes in the fair value of the assets held for sale, the Company recognized a loss due to changes in the fair value of assets held for sale by US$ 260&#160;million in the &#8220;Other net operating results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income, mainly generated by the more pronounced decline of the fields and the lower production than expected due to their performance. The carrying amount of the assets held for sale may be adjusted in future periods depending on the results of the disposal process and the economic consideration to be agreed with third parties for such assets. See Notes 8 and 11 &#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221; section to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, the Company signed different assignment agreements for 8 groups of assets (24 areas), subject to the fulfillment of agreed closing conditions, including applicable regulatory and provincial approvals. As of the date of this annual report, the remaining groups of assets, mainly conventional areas of Santa Cruz and Neuqu&#233;n, are in negotiations with third parties for their disposal or reversion. The recoverable amount of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">right-of-use</span></span> assets analysis is performed on the <span style="white-space:nowrap">year-end</span> date or whenever there is any indication of impairment of the recoverable value. It is difficult to predict with reasonable certainty the amount of expected future impairment losses given the many factors impacting the assets and the cash flows used in the impairment test calculation. These factors include, but are not limited to, oil and natural gas future selling prices, volumes of reserves, the distribution over time of production levels associated with such reserves, future investments, production costs, field depletion rates, the supply and demand in local and international markets, the current legislation and contractual conditions. According to the foregoing, and in connection with the estimation of impairment of property, plant and equipment as of December&#160;31, 2024, if our future crude oil and natural gas prices were reduced by 5 US$/bbl and 0.5 US$/MBtu, respectively, for all years of the future discounted cash flows, and assuming all other factors remain constant, our provision for impairment of property, plant and equipment comprising the Upstream business segment CGUs would increase by approximately US$ 2.1&#160;billion before income tax effects. Actual cash flows may be materially affected by other factors and there are numerous uncertainties inherent in the present value estimate of future cash flows, so this hypothetical calculation should not be construed as indicative of our development plans or future results of operations. In addition, for information regarding impairment charges see Note 8 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements, and for information regarding our estimates of oil and gas reserves, see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business organization&#8212;Upstream&#8212;Oil and gas reserves&#8221; and &#8220;Supplemental information on oil and gas producing activities (unaudited)&#8221;. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Outside business interests and experiences of the members of the Board of Directors </span></span></p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="max-width:100%;margin-left:0%; margin-right:0%;border:solid 1px;background-color:;padding-top:2pt;padding-bottom:3pt"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-top:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Horacio Daniel Mar&#237;n </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Current position:</span> Director and Chairman of the Board, and Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) of YPF S.A. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Other directorships:</span> None. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Experience:</span> Over the course of his <span style="white-space:nowrap">36-year</span> career, he worked in the development and strategy of the oil and gas industry in several countries besides Argentina, including the United States, Mexico, Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia, holding different positions in operations, development, exploration and strategy. He was responsible for the development of both the surface and the infrastructure in the Fort&#237;n de Piedra block in the Vaca Muerta formation, developed in record time. He served at Tecpetrol S.A. as Corporate Reservoir Manager, among other positions, and in November 2008 he was appointed Exploration&#160;&amp; Production President of Tecpetrol S.A., a position he held until December 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Education:</span> He is a Chemical Engineer graduated from Universidad Nacional de La Plata. He holds a Master&#8217;s degree in Petroleum Engineering from University of Texas at Austin. In 2009 he attended the Executive Program at the Graduate School of Business at Stanford University. </p></div> <p style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="max-width:100%;margin-left:0%; margin-right:0%;border:solid 1px;background-color:;padding-top:2pt;padding-bottom:3pt"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-top:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Carlos Manuel Bastos </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Current position:</span> Director of the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Other directorships: </span>Director of the board of Metrogas, Vice President of Andina Electricidad S.A. and Trancura Energ&#237;a S.A. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Experience:</span> In 1970 he joined Empresa Provincial de Energ&#237;a de C&#243;rdoba (&#8220;EPEC&#8221;) where he worked as a technician and then as an engineer. He held the following positions until 1996: Undersecretary of Energy (1991), Secretary of Energy (1992-1995), Secretary of Energy and Communications (1995), Secretary of Energy and Transportation (1995)&#160;and Secretary of Public Works and Services (1996). Between July 1999 and December 1999, he was Chairman of EPEC. Between March 2001 and December 2001, he was the Minister of Infrastructure of Argentina. Between March 2016 and December 2017, he was appointed &#8220;vocal primero&#8221; of the Ente Nacional Regulador de la Electricidad (&#8220;ENRE&#8221;). He was a consultant in the energy industry. He has been a member of the Advisory Experts team of Trench Energy Consulting S.A., and he has been an independent consultant in hydrocarbons and electric energy. He acted as arbitrator and expert witness in many arbitration cases on regulatory issues in Argentina and other Latin American countries related to the energy distribution and transport. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Education:</span> He holds a degree in Electronic Engineer from Universidad Nacional de C&#243;rdoba, Facultad de Ciencias Exactas with a postgraduate degree in Energy Economics from Fundaci&#243;n Bariloche. </p></div> <p style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="max-width:100%;margin-left:0%; margin-right:0%;border:solid 1px;background-color:;padding-top:2pt;padding-bottom:3pt"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-top:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Jos&#233; Rolandi </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Current position: </span>Director of the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Other directorships: </span>None. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Experience: </span>He worked as a senior consultant at Imagina Management&#160;&amp; IT S.A. advising on projects in the oil, petrochemical and mass consumption industries between 2007 and 2011. He worked as project manager of the Carape I and II Wind Farm and the Aconcagua <span style="white-space:nowrap">Bi-oceanic</span> Corridor in Corporaci&#243;n Am&#233;rica S.A. between 2011 and 2014. Between 2014 and 2018 he was Strategic Planning and Commercial Manager at CGC being responsible for the commercialization of crude oil, natural gas and LNG. He also has experience in IT, having <span style="white-space:nowrap">co-founded</span> companies related to artificial intelligence, augmented reality and development of solutions based on facial biometrics. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Education: </span>He holds an Industrial Engineer degree from Instituto Tecnol&#243;gico de Buenos Aires (&#8220;ITBA&#8221;). </p></div> <p style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="max-width:100%;margin-left:0%; margin-right:0%;border:solid 1px;background-color:;padding-top:2pt;padding-bottom:3pt"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-top:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Eduardo Alberto Ottino </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Current position: </span>Director of the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Other directorships: </span>None. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Experience: </span>He has 42 years of experience having held various positions in the areas of management control, economic and financial planning, tax, internal audit, administration, reporting and finance. He played key roles in the acquisitions of large and <span style="white-space:nowrap">medium-sized</span> industrial companies acquired by the Techint Group in Argentina (Sociedad Mixta Siderurgia Argentina -today Ternium S.A.-, Comesi and Armco), as well as in the United States (Maverick and Hydril), Venezuela Sider&#250;rgica del Orinoco SIDOR S.A. and Europe (Silcotube). He was Administrative Director of Siderar between 1992 and 1999, and Director of Administration and Finance of Techint Ingenier&#237;a y Construcci&#243;n and Techint Engineering Company between 2000 and 2002. Between 2003 and 2007 he was Chief Administrative Officer of Tenaris S.A. and between 2008 and 2016 he was Chief Administrative Officer of the Techint Group. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Education: </span>He is a Certified Public Accountant graduated from the School of Economics from Universidad Nacional de La Plata. Since December 2023, he is the Minister of Economy, Production and Industry of the Neuqu&#233;n Province. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Education:</span> He is a Certified Public Accountant from Universidad Nacional del Comahue. </p></div> <p style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="max-width:100%;margin-left:0%; margin-right:0%;border:solid 1px;background-color:;padding-top:2pt;padding-bottom:3pt"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-top:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Carla Antonela Matarese </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Current position:</span> Alternate Director of the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Other directorships:</span> None. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Experience:</span> Between 2005 and 2007, she worked at the Ministry of Production of the Chubut Province, as Advisor in the Management of Financial Programs and Special Projects and as Director of Development Promotion.  <div style="max-width:100%;margin-left:0%; margin-right:0%;border:solid 1px;background-color:;padding-top:2pt;padding-bottom:3pt"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-top:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Hugo Eduardo Rodr&#237;guez </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Current position: </span>Alternate<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>Director of the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Other directorships:</span> None. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Experience: </span>He has experience in the oil and gas industry, having managed national and international oil services companies. She has completed a specialization in Legal and Economic Structure of Energy Regulation and an interdisciplinary master&#8217;s degree in Energy (thesis currently pending), both at the Center for the Study of Energy Regulatory Activity, School of Law of Universidad de Buenos Aires. </p></div> <p style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div style="max-width:100%;margin-left:0%; margin-right:0%;border:solid 1px;background-color:;padding-top:2pt;padding-bottom:3pt"> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-top:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Julio Alejandro Schiantarelli </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Current position:</span> Alternate Director of the Board. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Other directorships:</span> None. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Experience:</span> He joined YPF S.A. in 1977 at the Reservoir Engineering area. He also served at the Training and Development Area. He was appointed General Secretary of SUPeH Florencio Varela in 1984, reelected until 1992. He held different positions in SUPeH. Currently, he serves as Deputy Secretary of SUPeH. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; padding-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; margin-right:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-weight:bold">Education:</span> He holds a degree in Industrial Relations from UADE. </p></div> <p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">To the knowledge of the Company, none of the Directors and Alternate Directors have family relationships with members of senior management or other members of the Board of Directors. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Board of Directors&#8217; practices </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The information provided below describes the responsibilities of our Board of Directors<span style="font-style:italic">.</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In accordance with the Argentine General Corporations Law, directors have an obligation to perform their duties with loyalty and with the diligence of a prudent businessperson. Directors are jointly and severally liable to YPF S.A., its shareholders and to third parties for the improper performance of their duties, for violating the law, our bylaws or other regulations, and for any damage caused by willful misconduct, abuse of authority or gross negligence. Specific duties may be assigned to a director by the bylaws, applicable regulations, or by shareholders resolution. In such cases, a director&#8217;s liability will be determined by reference to the performance of those specific duties so long as the director&#8217;s appointment and assignment of duties was approved at a shareholders&#8217; meeting and was registered with the Superintendence of Legal Entities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Only shareholders, through a shareholders&#8217; meeting, may authorize directors to engage in activities in competition with YPF S.A. Transactions or contracts between directors and us in connection with our activities are permitted to the extent they are performed under fair market conditions. Transactions that do not comply with the above mentioned requirements may only be carried out with prior approval of the Board of Directors or, in the absence of a quorum at a Board of Directors meeting, of the Supervisory Committee. In addition, these transactions must be subsequently approved by our shareholders at a general meeting. In case the shareholders meeting does not approve the relevant transaction, the directors or members of the Supervisory Committee who approved the transaction, as the case may be, shall be held jointly and severally liable for any damages caused to us and the agreement shall be void. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Any director whose personal interests conflicts with those of YPF S.A. on any matter shall notify the Board of Directors and the Supervisory Committee and abstain from participating and voting on the matter. Otherwise, such director may be held jointly and severally liable to YPF S.A. for the damages caused by his acts and omissions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">A director will not be liable if, notwithstanding his presence at the meeting at which a resolution is adopted or his knowledge of such resolution, a written record exists of his opposition to such resolution and he reports his opposition to the Supervisory Committee before any complaint against him is brought before the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Committee, the shareholders&#8217; meeting, the appropriate governmental agency or judicial action is brought to the courts. Any liability of a director to YPF S.A. terminates upon approval of the director&#8217;s performance, or by express waiver or settlement by the shareholders at a general meeting, provided that shareholders representing at least 5% of our capital stock do not object and provided further that such liability does not result from a violation of the law, our bylaws or other regulations. The termination of liability of a director to YPF S.A. will not be effective in case of an involuntary liquidation or bankruptcy process. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As part of its continuing process of improving the corporate governance of YPF S.A., the Board of Directors implements an annual self-assessment that covers aspects related to the functioning of the Board of Directors in general, its committees and its members individually. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With this process, the functioning and effectiveness of the Board of Directors can be monitored regularly, according to the best corporate governance practices. This is also a requirement of the BYMA Corporate Governance Panel, of which YPF S.A. is a party, and a recommendation of the CNV regulations, and is aligned with the NYSE Listing Regulations. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Board of Directors can also entrust the Corporate Secretary with the preparation and implementation of improvement proposals, based on the results obtained under the YPF S.A.&#8217;s Corporate Governance continuous improvement plan. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For information regarding to the Board of Directors roles in cybersecurity see &#8220;Item 16K. Cybersecurity&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Compensation of members of our Board of Directors </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Argentine General Corporations Law provides that the aggregate annual compensation for any concept paid to the members of the Board of Directors (including those directors acting in an executive capacity) and of the members of the Shareholders&#8217; Surveillance Committee (&#8220;Consejo de Vigilancia&#8221;), if applicable, including salary and other remuneration for the performance of technical-administrative functions of a permanent nature, with respect to a fiscal year may not exceed 5% of the net income for such year if YPF S.A. is not paying dividends in respect of such net income. If YPF S.A. pays dividends, that percentage is increased proportionally up to 25% of the net income, based on the amount of such dividends. The annual compensation of YPF S.A.&#8217;s directors shall be determined in accordance with the prevailing market practice and shall be proposed by the Board of Directors to the ordinary general shareholders&#8217; meeting, for its approval. When one or more directors exercise special commissions or technical administrative functions in a fiscal year where there are reduced profits or no profits, and there is a need to exceed the abovementioned limits, such compensations may only be paid in excess of those limits if expressly agreed by the shareholders&#8217; meeting, for which purpose the matter should be included as a special item on the agenda of such meeting. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Shareholders&#8217; Surveillance Committee is a control corporate body regulated by the Argentine General Corporations Law, composed of shareholders of a corporation. As of the date of this annual report, YPF S.A. does not have a Shareholders&#8217; Surveillance Committee, since the Argentine General Corporations Law requires us to have a Supervisory Committee, composed of statutory auditors. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For the year ended December&#160;31, 2024, the aggregate compensation accrued by the members of the Board of Directors and YPF&#8217;s executive officers for services in all capacities was Ps. 58.606&#160;million (US$ 59 million), excluding social security payments made by YPF S.A. as required by law, but including Ps. 30.306&#160;million (US$ 31 million) in the form of equity compensation plans, pensions, retirement or similar benefits that YPF S.A. provides to its Board of Directors and executive officers. All compensations are determined in the currency of legal tender, which is the Argentine peso. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, as indicated above, some of the members of our Board of Directors may also be employees of YPF S.A. Thus, we include a brief description of our current employee benefit plans and programs. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s performance-based compensation programs include performance bonus programs which are intended to motivate and reward individuals for the annual achievement of business objectives. The Company has short-term benefit cash payment programs applicable to certain employees. These programs are mainly based on the fulfillment of vice presidencies and unit objectives and may be increased based on individual performance. They are calculated considering the remuneration of each employee, the number of salaries assigned per salary category and certain key factors related to the fulfillment of these objectives. As of 2024, a new variable compensation program based on the Company&#8217;s results (&#8220;CVR&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) was implemented, to be paid whenever these results are positive. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Since 2013, YPF S.A. has implemented a share-based benefit plan, which: (i)&#160;encourages key personnel to align their performance with the objectives of YPF S.A.&#8217;s strategic plan; (ii)&#160;generates a clear and direct link between the creation of shareholder value and compensation of key personnel, rewarding them for achieving long-term results reflected in the share price; and (iii)&#160;assists in the retention of key personnel within YPF S.A. In addition, in April 2024, the Company adopted the &#8220;Value Generation Plan&#8221;, which is a long-term remuneration program for eligible members of management of YPF with the objective of incentivizing extraordinary results in the long term and retaining key employees. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For additional information see Notes 2.b.11) and 38 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements and &#8220;Item 16E. Purchases of equity securities by the issuer and affiliated purchasers&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Executive officers who also perform as members of the Board of Directors can also be entitled to the aforementioned programs (with certain exceptions), which shall be subject to the limitations set forth hereinabove in this section. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">None of the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-employee</span> members of YPF S.A.&#8217;s Board of Directors is party to any service contract with us or any our subsidiaries providing for benefits upon termination of their term in office. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_45"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Board of Directors&#8217; Committees </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors has established the following committees: Audit Committee, Legal and Institutional Affairs Committee, Risk and Sustainability Committee, Strategy and Transformation Committee, the Compensation and Nomination Committee and the Disclosure Committee. These committees periodically report its activities to the Board of Directors. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following table sets forth a summary of the composition of the committees composed of Directors as of the date of this annual report: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The activities and responsibilities of the committees are further described below. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Audit Committee </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Capital Markets Law, described in &#8220;Item 9. The offer and listing&#8221;, and the Article 15, Sections V, Chapter III, Title II of the CNV Rules require publicly traded corporations to appoint an Audit Committee composed of at least 3 members of the Board of Directors and which majority of its members must be independent directors. The Audit Committee&#8217;s regulations set forth the composition and provisions for the performance of the Audit Committee, according to the applicable law. Executive directors of YPF S.A. are not permitted to sit on the Audit Committee. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">See &#8220;Item 6. Directors, Senior Management and Employees&#8212;Independence of the members of our Board of Directors and Audit Committee&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Activities of the Audit Committee </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our Audit Committee supports the Board of Directors in its oversight duties, such as: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;text-align:justify">Periodically supervises the functioning of the internal control over financial reporting system and the administrative-accounting system, as well as the reliability of the latter, and of the financial information, hydrocarbon reserves information and other relevant information communicated to the CNV and the markets in compliance with the applicable information regime. </p></td></tr></table>
