<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;text-align:justify">Ensures that our Code of Ethics complies with the legal requirements and is adequate for YPF S.A. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Meetings </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Audit Committee, pursuant to its regulations, must meet as many times as needed and at least once every quarter. From May&#160;8, 2024 to March&#160;28, 2025, the Audit Committee held 11 formal meetings. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Economic and financial information </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Using the assessment of the Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;) and the work performed by our external and internal auditors, the Audit Committee analyzes the consolidated annual and quarterly financial statements (for statutory, legal and regulatory purposes filed with CNV) before they are submitted to the Board of Directors. The Audit Committee reviewed our Consolidated Financial Statements as of and for the year ended December&#160;31, 2024 and comparative information included in this annual report and our report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">6-K</span> furnished to the SEC on March&#160;14, 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Oversight of the internal control system </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our internal control over financial reporting system is aligned with the requirements established by Section&#160;404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. These regulations provide, among other requirements that, along with the annual audit, a report must be presented by our management relating to the design, maintenance and periodic evaluation of the internal control over financial reporting system and be accompanied by a report from our external auditor. Several of our departments are involved in this activity, including the internal audit department. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Relations with the internal auditor </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Audit Committee oversees the progress of our annual internal audit, which is aimed at identifying critical risks, to supervise our internal control over financial reporting system and ensure that they are sufficient, appropriate and efficient. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Throughout the year, the Audit Committee is kept informed by our internal auditor of the most relevant facts and recommendations arising out of its work and the status of the recommendations issued. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Relations with the external auditor </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Audit Committee interacts closely with the external auditor, allowing them to make a detailed analysis of the relevant aspects of the audit of our Consolidated Financial Statements and to obtain detailed information on the planning and progress of the work. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Audit Committee also evaluates the services provided by our external auditor, determines whether the conditions for independence of the external auditor, as required by applicable law, are met and monitors the performance of the external auditor to ensure that it is satisfactory. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of this annual report, and pursuant to the evaluation process described in the above paragraph, the Audit Committee had no objections to the designation of Deloitte&#160;&amp; Co. S.A. as our external auditor of the Consolidated Financial Statements for the year ended December&#160;31, 2025. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Legal and Institutional Affairs Committee </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Among its main functions, the Legal and Institutional Affairs Committee is responsible for the supervision of management and analysis of the litigation strategy of the main <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-trial,</span> arbitral and judicial disputes where YPF S.A. is a party, among other matters. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Risk and Sustainability Committee </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Risk and Sustainability Committee main functions are to establish comprehensive management policies for business risks and to monitor their adequate implementation; to identify and evaluate risk factors that are specific to YPF S.A. and/or its activity; and to monitor risks and implement corresponding mitigation actions, among other functions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Strategy and Transformation Committee </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Strategy and Transformation Committee main functions, among others, are to discuss issues related to YPF S.A.&#8217;s medium and long-term strategy and to act as liaison between the Board of Directors and the Executive Management Committee (the Senior Management herein), in order to facilitate and expedite the internal treatment of YPF S.A.&#8217;s business development overall strategies; to resolve, in the event of unforeseen or emergency situations when it would not be possible to convene a Board of Directors meeting, the approval of YPF S.A.&#8217;s operations and/or necessary management, subject to the ratification of the Board of Directors. </p>

<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(1)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This organizational structure was approved by the Board of Directors, at its meeting held on December&#160;5, 2024. All the members of senior management report to the CEO. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:7pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(2)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Indicates when the person has been appointed, as applicable, for the first time continuously. No expiration date of position specified when appointed. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_47"><span style="font-style:italic">Independence of the members of our Board of Directors and Audit Committee </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following description of the CNV regulations were considered in order to assess each director&#8217;s independence. In that sense, a director is considered independent if the main material relationship of such director with YPF S.A. is being a member of its Board of Directors. A director is not considered independent when such director: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(i)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Holds a position as director in the board of directors of the issuer&#8217;s controlling shareholder or any other entity in the issuer&#8217;s corporate group at the time of the director&#8217;s appointment or if he held such position during the immediately preceding three years. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(ii)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Has an affiliation with the issuer or with any of its shareholders who have directly or indirectly a &#8220;significant participation&#8221; (as defined below) in the issuer at the time of the director&#8217;s appointment or in the companies in which they also have a direct or indirect &#8220;significant participation&#8221;, or if he had such affiliation with them by an employment relationship during the immediately preceding three years. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(iii)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Has a professional relationship with, or is a member of a company or professional association that maintains habitual professional relationships of relevant nature and volume with, or receives remuneration or fees (other than those received in consideration of his performance as a director) from the issuer or any of its shareholders who has a direct or indirect &#8220;significant participation&#8221; in the issuer, or with a company in which they have a direct or indirect &#8220;significant participation&#8221;. This prohibition extends through the preceding three-year period to the director&#8217;s appointment. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(iv)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Directly or indirectly owns at least 5% voting shares and/or capital stock in the issuer or in any other entity which holds a &#8220;significant participation&#8221; in the issuer. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(v)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Directly or indirectly habitually sells or provides goods or services (other than those set forth in (iii)&#160;above) of relevant nature and volume to the issuer or to any of its shareholders who has a direct or indirect &#8220;significant participation&#8221; in the issuer for an amount substantially exceeding his remuneration as a member of the board of directors (this prohibition extends through the preceding three-year period to the director&#8217;s appointment). </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(vi)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Has been a director, manager or executive officer of <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-profit</span> organizations which have received contributions in excess of those set forth in Article 12, item l) of the UIF Resolution No.&#160;30/2011 (as amended) from the issuer, its controlling shareholder, and any other member of the issuer&#8217;s corporate group or from the executive officers of any of them. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(vii)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Receives any payments, including those derived from the director&#8217;s participation in stock option plans, from the issuer or any company of its corporate group (other than those received in consideration of his performance as a director, with the exception of dividends perceived pursuant to item (iv)&#160;or payments pursuant to item (v)&#160;above). </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(viii)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Has been a director of the issuer, its controlling shareholder or any other member of the issuer&#8217;s corporate group for more than 10 years, provided that the director will be deemed independent following a three-year period after he ceased to hold any such position. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(ix)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Is the spouse or legally recognized partner or family member (up to second grade of affinity or up to third grade of consanguinity) of persons who, if they were members of the board of directors, would not be deemed independent. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In case that, following the director&#8217;s appointment, such director became subject to any of the restrictions in items (i)&#160;through (ix) above, such director shall be required to disclose this circumstance to the issuer immediately, who in turn shall be required to disclose it to the CNV and to the stock exchanges on which the issuer&#8217;s stock is listed, immediately after its occurrence or after being noticed. The directors and members of the Supervisory Committee appointed by the government are deemed independent. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The term &#8220;significant participation&#8221; shall be deemed to refer to such persons that hold an interest of at least 5% of the capital stock and/or votes, or a lesser amount when they allow the appointment of one or more class directors or that have together with other shareholders, agreements related to the government and administration of the relevant company or its controlling shareholder. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The term &#8220;economic group&#8221; shall mean controlling companies, controlled companies and those affiliated in which there is a relevant influence in the decisions. Direct and/or indirect interests through companies or individuals are considered. </p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of this annual report, Directors Guillermo Alberto Francos, Eduardo Alberto Ottino, Omar Guti&#233;rrez, C&#233;sar Rodolfo Biffi and Ignacio Ezequiel Bruera, and Alternate Directors Guillermo Gustavo Koenig, Carla Antonela Matarese and Hugo Eduardo Rodr&#237;guez, qualified as independent members of our Board of Directors under the criteria described above. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_48"><span style="font-style:italic">Compliance with the NYSE Listing Standards on Corporate Governance </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Independence of the members of the Audit Committee </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In accordance with the NYSE corporate governance rules, all members of the Audit Committee are required to be independent. Independence is determined in accordance with highly detailed rules promulgated by the NYSE and SEC. Each of the members of our Audit Committee was determined to be independent in accordance with the applicable NYSE and SEC rules. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Significant differences between our corporate governance practices and those required by NYSE listing standards </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-U.S.</span> NYSE listed companies may, in general, follow their home country corporate governance practices in lieu of most of the NYSE corporate governance requirements. The NYSE rules, however, require that <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-U.S.</span> companies disclose any significant ways in which their specific corporate governance practices differ from those of U.S. companies under the NYSE listing standards. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following is a summary of the significant differences between our corporate governance practices and those applicable to U.S. companies under the NYSE listing standards: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman">&#9679;</span></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Independence of the members of the Board of Directors</span>: In accordance with the NYSE corporate governance rules, a majority of the board of directors of U.S. companies listed on the NYSE must be composed of independent directors, whose independence is determined in accordance with highly detailed rules promulgated by the NYSE. The relevant Argentine rules for determining director independence are described under &#8220;Item 6. Directors, Senior Management and Employees&#8212;Independence of the members of our Board of Directors and Audit Committee&#8221;. The independence of the members of our Board of Directors is determined according to the CNV regulations. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman">&#9679;</span></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Compensation and Nomination Committee</span>: In accordance with the NYSE corporate governance rules, all U.S. companies listed on the NYSE must have a compensation committee and a nomination committee, and all members of such committees must be independent in accordance with highly detailed rules promulgated by the NYSE. Under Argentine law, these committees are not mandatory but are recommended by the CNV General Resolution No.&#160;622/2013. YPF S.A. follows the CNV&#8217;s recommendation and has a Compensation and Nomination Committee established by our Board of Directors under the option provided in Article 17 clause (xii)&#160;of YPF S.A.&#8217;s bylaws. The Committee is integrated by 3 members and the President is independent. Also, the NYSE rules require that, with limited exemptions, all equity compensation plans be subject to a shareholder vote. Under Argentine law, the approval of equity compensation plans is within the authority of the Board of Directors. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman">&#9679;</span></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Separate meetings for <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-management</span> directors</span>: In accordance with the NYSE corporate governance rules, independent directors must meet periodically outside of the presence of its executive directors. Under Argentine law, this practice is not required and as such, the independent directors of our Board of Directors do not meet outside of the presence of the other directors, except for the meetings of the Audit Committee, which is comprised of independent directors. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_49"><span style="font-style:italic">Supervisory Committee </span></p> <p style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Supervisory Committee is responsible for overseeing compliance by the management and the Board of Directors with Argentine General Corporations Law, the bylaws and regulations (if any), and shareholders&#8217; resolutions. The functions of the Supervisory Committee include, among others, attending all meetings of the Board of Directors, preparing a report of the financial statements for our shareholders, attending shareholders&#8217; meetings and providing information upon request to holders of at least 2% of our capital stock. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The bylaws provide for a Supervisory Committee composed of three to five members and three to five alternate members, as determined by the shareholders&#8217; meeting, that are elected for <span style="white-space:nowrap">one-fiscal</span> year term. The Class&#160;A shares are entitled to elect one member and one alternate member of the Supervisory Committee so long as one share of such class remains outstanding. The holders of Class&#160;D shares may elect up to four members and up to four alternates members. Under the bylaws, meetings of the Supervisory Committee may be called by any member. The meetings require the presence of all members and a majority vote of the members in order to make a decision. The members and alternate members of the Supervisory Committee are not members of our Board of Directors. The role of our Supervisory Committee is different from that of the Audit Committee. See &#8220;Item 6. Directors, Senior Management and Employees&#8212;Management of the Company&#8212;Board of Directors&#8217; Committees&#8212;Audit Committee&#8221;. In 2024, the aggregate compensation paid to the members of the Supervisory Committee was Ps. 357.2&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of this annual report, the Supervisory Committee is composed of the following members: </p> <p style="font-size:4pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_50"><span style="font-style:italic">Our people </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Attraction, retention and development </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, we continued with our leadership development, which consisted of training programs for leaders at different levels: supervisors, heads, managers, and new leaders, in which a total of 1,673 leaders participated. Additionally, more than 200 executives and key people participated in a management program along with the IAE Business School. We also performed open spaces with Senior Management to talk about expected culture and leadership in order to foster the strategy execution. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We also worked to accompany business units along the Company in their specific business transformation with different leadership trainings, and continued with &#8220;LIFE&#8221;, our female leadership program implemented in 2020, in which 198 talented women of YPF participated to take on roles of greater responsibility. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The 360&#176; Feedback Evaluation was carried out once again, in which more than 2,200 leaders were evaluated, obtaining different perspectives regarding their role and leadership style. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We held Talent Review sessions to assess the profile and potential of our staff, identifying individuals with high technical value, high potential, and successors for key roles, and defining tailored development plans based on this. Additionally, special monitoring was carried out on a group identified as Critical Talent, a subgroup within the high potentials identified by each Vice Presidency, in order to ensure appropriate retention and development actions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As one of people management goals is the retention of key people, we continuously monitor the voluntary rotation, which keeps levels below 3%, below market reference. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We focused on developing actions to ensure critical business capabilities, prioritizing cross skills such as agility, data, innovation, and project management. Nowadays, the digitization and virtualization of content is key. In 2024, 74.59% of the training proposal was carried out remotely, 47.23% by <span style="white-space:nowrap">e-learning</span> and 27.36% virtually. We managed 452,555 hours of training for our staff, with an average of 25.25 hours of training per person. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In terms of attraction, we used &#8220;job posting&#8221; as a resource to cover vacancies with internal staff, a practice that continued to consolidate. As a result, 64.8% of the vacant positions in 2024 were filled by internal candidates. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In terms of young employment, we also carried out our Young Trainees Program where we incorporated 25 professionals coming from different universities and locations around Argentina. As part of the training process, these professionals rotate through different areas during a nine-month period. Then, they are assigned to a specific position to continue their professional development in the Company. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In order to continue strengthening our position as an employer of choice, we continue fortifying our employer brand strategy which included various actions aimed at positioning and consolidating the Company in the talent market, carrying out initiatives such as presentations and talks at university fairs, conferences and events, sponsorships in different technical spaces, among others. In 2024, we improved our positioning in rankings and awards on human resources practices and young talent. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Compensation and benefits </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As part of its compensation management, YPF monitors reference markets with the aim of ensuring the competitiveness of its compensation and the internal equity of salaries, so that employees receive the same salary levels for the same position, seniority, experience and performance. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition to the salary, employees receive a variable performance bonus, which is a monetary incentive linked to the achievement of annual objectives, which are calculated based on goals and indicators set at the vice presidency and unit levels. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, a new bonus related to the Company&#8217;s results, the CVR, applicable to certain employees, was incorporated, and the &#8220;Value Generation Plan&#8221;, which is a long-term remuneration program for eligible members of YPF&#8217;s management, was adopted. For further information see &#8220;Item 6. Directors, Senior Management and Employees&#8212;Board of Directors&#8212;Compensation of members of our Board of Directors&#8221; and Note 38 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF also has a Long-Term Variable Compensation Program, which promotes the retention of executives and key personnel through the granting of Company&#8217;s shares. In 2024, 6.3% of the eligible employees had a long-term assignment. For more information see &#8220;Item 6. Directors, Senior Management and Employees&#8212;Management of the Company&#8212;Board of Directors&#8212;Compensation of members of our Board of Directors&#8221; and Note 38 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, YPF has the YMile Recognition Program, launched in 2022, which seeks to identify and recognize those employees who in their daily activity have contributed in an extraordinary way to creating value and strengthening the culture. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In terms of benefits, the Company has set out to improve the wellness of its workers, through benefits such as medical plan, longer leaves for pregnant and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-pregnant</span> caregivers, a savings and pension plan with <span style="white-space:nowrap">co-participation</span> of the Company, fuel discounts, <span style="white-space:nowrap">co-financing</span> graduate studies, among others. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Diversity and integration </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">We know diversity not only contributes to create a more representative workforce but also to build a more innovative, successful, and profitable company. We believe that YPF has to be a place where people with different stories and experiences contribute their talent and are part of a diverse team. We are on the way to that place, committed to creating it. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Since 2017, we have a Diversity Committee sponsored by five of the Company&#8217;s Vice Presidents, which was created to ensure transparency and representation of diverse&#160;voices and opinions in order to promote a comprehensive focus. We also extend our best practices to supplier companies, contractors and unions with the aim of developing joint actions to promote diversity, equity and integration. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Diversity and inclusion perspective is integrated into the processes of recruitment, development, promotion, hiring of young professionals and internship admissions, talent review, succession plans and salary gap reviews. We annually define participation goals for women in leadership positions, hiring new professionals and implementing internships. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With the aim of accelerating integration in our Company, we have the Women&#8217;s Network and Young Professionals Network, which is composed of employees from different business areas who promote initiatives and goals aligned with our Company&#8217;s integration strategy and act as a facilitator to create a favorable context for inclusion. We support the Women&#8217;s Empowerment Principles (&#8220;WEPs&#8221;) from the UN Women (a United Nations&#8217; organization for women) and the United Nations Global Compact. As adherents to the WEPs, we applied the WEP assessment, in which we obtained a rating of 82%, which recognizes us as a leading company in gender practices. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:center">72 </p>

</div></div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Includes 9,436, 8,799 and 7,568 employees of AESA as of December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, the most significant variations are explained by: (i)&#160;an increase of 649 employees at AESA, due to new engineering projects as part of its construction business unit, (ii)&#160;a decrease of 341 due to the Mature Fields Project, and (iii)&#160;a decrease of 317 due to rightsizing in service stations, structures, refineries and corporate functions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2019, YPF began a process of incorporating contracted personnel with functions inherent to its operations into its own workforce in order to reduce costs and improve productivity, increasing the number of employees but reducing more than 50% the number of contracted personnel and associated costs. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following table provides, for each of the periods indicated, a breakdown of our employees by geographic location: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_51"><span style="font-style:italic">Labor relations </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, 67.2% of our employees were unionized, 33.2% of which were represented by the SUPeH Federation that negotiates labor agreements and salaries applicable to YPF S.A. and OPESSA unionized employees. The SUPeH is in continuous negotiations with us, and we maintain a good level of communication. In general, requests of labor unions in connection with the oil and gas industry were consistent with general wage increases given by the General Unions Confederation. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, labor conditions and salaries of third-party employees are mainly represented by 16 other unions. As of December&#160;31, 2024, 59.7% of third-party employees (mostly in the Upstream business segment) were represented by ten unions with whom we negotiate directly labor agreements and salaries. These unions are clustered into four groups: (i)&#160;Petroleros Privados, which consists mainly of five unions; (ii)&#160;Personal Jer&#225;rquico, which consists of three unions; (iii)&#160;SUPeH; and (iv) UOCRA Petroleros. The remaining 40.3% of third-party employees are represented by unions with whom we have indirect relations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During 2024, within the framework of the Mature Fields Project, we reached agreements with labor unions from the Mendoza, Neuqu&#233;n, Chubut, and Santa Cruz Provinces to initiate the <span style="white-space:nowrap">stand-by</span> of equipment and the reduction of activity levels, which resulted in the orderly transfer of areas in the Chubut and Mendoza Provinces. Additionally, we successfully extended the term of <span style="white-space:nowrap">stand-by</span> agreements in the Mendoza and Santa Cruz Provinces until January&#160;31, 2025, and until February&#160;28, 2025, respectively. Additionally, and in relation to the Mature Fields Project, in December 2024, the Company has committed to an optimization plan that involves operating efficiency measures related to the reduction of third party employees directly or indirectly affected to the operation of areas in the Santa Cruz Province (see &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;We may fail to execute in whole or in part our disposal plan related to mature fields (&#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8221;)&#8221;, &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business Strategy&#8212;Strategic pillars: &#8220;4x4 challenge&#8221;&#8221;, &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;Business organization&#8212;Upstream&#8221;, and Note 11 &#8220;Mature Fields Project&#8220; section to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements). </p>

<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(3)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:7pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Participated Ownership Program (&#8220;Programa de Propiedad Participada&#8221; or &#8220;PPP&#8221;) established by the Argentine government in the privatization process in 1991. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_53"><span style="font-style:italic">Related party transactions </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">All material transactions and balances with related parties as of December&#160;31, 2024, are set forth in Note 37 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The main related party transactions were sales of products to certain joint ventures and associates, and purchases of services and products that we do not produce ourselves from certain joint ventures and associates. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, the Argentine Republic owns 51% of the shares of YPF S.A. (see &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;History and development of YPF S.A.&#8221;). Consequently, and in addition to transactions mentioned in the paragraph above, we also inform the agreements with the Argentine federal government as well as with certain agencies, institutions or companies with state participation. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, see Note 2.b.11) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements regarding our long-term share compensation plans and other plans offered to certain personnel. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For a table including the main entities of our organizational structure, including details on our interests in our principal affiliates, see Note 1 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_54"><span style="font-style:italic">Argentine law concerning related party transactions </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Articles 72 and 73 of the Capital Markets Law provide that before a company whose shares are listed in Argentina (&#8220;Issuer&#8221;) may enter into an act or contract involving a &#8220;significant amount&#8221; with a &#8220;related party&#8221; or &#8220;related parties&#8221;, the Issuer must obtain approval from its board of directors, and obtain an opinion, prior to such board approval, from its audit committee or from two independent valuation firms that states that the terms of the transaction may reasonably be deemed consistent with those that could be obtained on an <span style="white-space:nowrap">arm&#8217;s-length</span> basis. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For the purpose of Article 72 of the Capital Markets Law and the CNV Regulations, &#8220;significant amount&#8221; means an amount that exceeds 1% of the Issuer&#8217;s shareholders equity as reflected in the latest approved financial statements. For purposes of Articles 72 and 73 of the Capital Markets Law, &#8220;related party&#8221; means, in relation to the Issuer, (i)&#160;its directors, members of the supervisory committee or of the surveillance committee, as well as its general or special managers appointed in accordance with Article 270 of the Argentine General Corporations Law; (ii)&#160;the persons or entities that control or hold a &#8220;significant participation&#8221; (as regulated by the CNV) in the Issuer or in its controlling shareholder; (iii)&#160;any other company under common control of the same controlling company; (iv)&#160;ascendants, descendants, spouses or siblings of the persons mentioned in (i)&#160;and (ii); or (v)&#160;companies in which the persons referred to in (i)&#160;to (iv) hold directly or indirectly &#8220;significant participations&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As long as it is not included in items (i)&#160;to (v) above, a company controlled by the Issuer shall not be considered a &#8220;related party&#8221; with regards to Article 72 of the Capital Markets Law. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For the purposes of Article 72 of the Capital Markets Law, and pursuant to the CNV Regulations the term &#8220;significant participation&#8221; shall be deemed to refer to such persons that hold an interest of at least 15% of the capital stock, or a lesser amount when they have the right to appoint one or more directors by class of shares or that have together with other shareholders, agreements related to the Argentine government and administration of the relevant company or its controlling shareholder. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The acts or contracts referred to above, immediately after being approved by the board of directors, shall be disclosed to the CNV, making express indication of the audit committee and/or independent valuation firms&#8217; opinions, as the case may be. Additionally, on the business day following the day the transaction was approved by the board of directors, the audit committee or the independent valuation firms&#8217; opinions, as the case may be, shall be made available to the shareholders at the Issuer&#8217;s principal executive offices. This shall also be informed to the shareholders by a publication in the market&#8217;s bulletin. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">If the Audit Committee and/or the two independent valuation firms do not consider that the transaction is on <span style="white-space:nowrap">arm&#8217;s-length</span> terms, approval must be obtained at YPF S.A.&#8217;s shareholders&#8217; meeting, prior to the transaction. </p>

YPF S.A. and CGC will have a 51% and 49% interest, respectively, in the joint venture, with YPF S.A. being the operator of the block. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The transaction was carried out for the sum of US$ 75 million and, in addition, CGC will pay, on behalf and at the request of YPF S.A., 80.40% of the investments attributable to YPF S.A.&#8217;s working interest in the block for a period of four years, subject to certain maximum annual and monthly amounts. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Mature Fields Project</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January 29, 2025, Resolution No. 16/2025 was published in the Official Gazette of the Province of Mendoza, which authorized the transfer of 100% of YPF&#8217;s rights and obligations in &#8220;Barrancas&#8221;, &#8220;Vizcacheras&#8221;, &#8220;La Ventana&#8221;, &#8220;Ceferino&#8221;, &#8220;Mesa Verde&#8221; and &#8220;R&#237;o Tunuy&#225;n&#8221; exploitation concessions in favor of Petroleos Sudamericanos S.A. (&#8220;PS&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March 27, 2025, after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions by YPF and PS, the transfer of 100% of the rights and obligations of YPF in such exploitation concessions in favor of PS was formalized. </p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Argentine Securities Market</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The principal market for the Company&#8217;s ordinary shares, listed under the trading symbol &#8220;YPFD&#8221;, is BYMA. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Historically, Argentina&#180;s securities market comprised five stock exchanges, located in the Buenos Aires, C&#243;rdoba, Mendoza, Rosario and Santa Fe cities, which were authorized to quote publicly offered securities. With the enactment and enforcement of the Capital Markets Law and its regulatory Decree No.&#160;471/2018, along with the CNV Regulations, mandated that securities could only be listed and traded on stock markets authorized by the CNV. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Buenos Aires Stock Exchange (the &#8220;BASE&#8221;), established in 1854, was the principal stock exchange in Argentina, being the primary market where the Company&#180;s ordinary shares were first listed under the trading symbol &#8220;YPFD&#8221;. Its exchange functions were absorbed by the S&amp;P MERVAL, a stock market authorized by the CNV. An agreement between S&amp;P MERVAL and BASE, approved by the CNV, delegated certain functions to BASE, including listing authorization, arbitration courts and public information bulletins. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;29, 2016, the CNV approved the creation of BYMA as a new stock market. BYMA emerged from the <span style="white-space:nowrap">spin-off</span> of the S&amp;P MERVAL and the capital contribution of the BASE. Also, the BASE and the S&amp;P MERVAL decided to transfer their entire shareholding in the Stock Exchange Incorporated (Caja de Valores S.A.) to BYMA. Consequently, BYMA became the major shareholder of the Stock Exchange Incorporated, an internationally recognized central securities depository. As of the date of this annual report and as a result of the beforementioned, the Company&#180;s ordinary shares are currently listed in BYMA under the trading symbol &#8220;YPFD&#8221;. The Argentine securities market is regulated by the CNV under the Capital Markets Law, which oversees securities exchanges, stockbroker transactions, market operations, public offerings, corporate governance of public companies and trading of futures and options. Separate government agencies regulate Argentine institutional investors and insurance companies, while financial institutions are primarily regulated by the BCRA. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In Argentina, debt and equity securities traded on an exchange or <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">over-the-counter</span></span> market must be deposited with Stock Exchange Incorporated (Caja de Valores S.A.), a corporation owned 99.96% by BYMA. Stock Exchange Incorporated is the central securities depositary of Argentina, providing central depositary facilities clearinghouse services, and acting as a transfer and paying agent for securities transactions. It also, handles the settlement of securities transactions carried out by BYMA and operates through Millennium. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Capital Markets Law includes several key provisions defining negotiable securities, corporate governance requirements (including audit committees composed of three or more members of the board of directors, the majority of whom must be independent members under CNV Regulations; regulations for market stabilization; insider trading; market manipulation, securities fraud; going-private transactions; and acquisitions of voting shares). It also includes provisions regarding the demutualization of stock exchanges, new regulatory powers and resources for the CNV, a mandatory tender offer system, and new requirements for brokers/dealers and other market participants. These provisions are regulated by CNV General Resolution No.&#160;622/2013, as amended. Before offering securities to the public in Argentina, issuers must meet CNV requirements regarding assets, operating history, and management. Only securities approved for a public offering by the CNV may be listed on authorized markets. CNV approval does not certify the quality of securities or issuer solvency, although issuers must file unaudited quarterly financial statements, audited annual financial statements in accordance with IFRS, and various periodic reports to the CNV and the authorized market. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:1%; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Admission to BYMA&#8217;s Corporate Governance Plus Panel </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF S.A. is a member of BYMA&#180;s &#8220;Corporate Governance Plus Panel&#8221; (&#8220;CG+Panel&#8221;) created in December 2018. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The CG+Panel includes companies that voluntarily adhere to higher standards of corporate governance and transparency than those required by Argentine regulations. These standards align with the OECD&#180;s corporate governance principles, adopted by the G20, and companies commit to periodic monitoring of these standards. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_62"><span style="font-style:italic">Anti-money laundering and counter terrorism financing regulations </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Law No.&#160;25,246, as amended, the Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing Regime (&#8220;AML/CFT Regime&#8221;), categorizes money laundering as an autonomous crime against the economic and financial order, separate from the crime of concealment, which is an offense against the public administration, and allowed for sanctions for money laundering that are not necessarily linked to the participation in the crime that originated the funds subject to such money laundering. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;15, 2024, Law No.&#160;27,739 was published in the Official Gazette, introducing amendments to the Criminal Code and reforming the system for the prevention of money laundering, financing of terrorism and proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. These amendments broaden the criminal classification of money laundering to include activities such as converting, transferring, administering, selling, encumbering, acquiring, dissimulating or otherwise circulating goods or other assets derived from criminal offenses. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Financial Information Unit (&#8220;UIF&#8221;) is the designated authority to enforce the AML/CFT Regime and a decentralized agency that operates with autonomy and financial independency under the Ministry of Economy. The UIF is empowered to receive and request reports, documents, background and any other information deemed useful to fulfill its duties from any public entity, whether federal, provincial or municipal, and from individuals or public or private entities, all of which entities must furnish such information in accordance with AML/CFT Regime. Whenever the information furnished, or analyses performed by the UIF show the existence of sufficient evidence to suspect that a money laundering or terrorist financing crime has been committed, the UIF shall transmit such evidence to the Government Attorney&#8217;s Office (&#8220;Ministerio P&#250;blico Fiscal&#8221;) so that it may start the relevant criminal action, and the UIF may appear as an accusing party to such proceedings. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The AML/CFT Regime, in line with international AML/CFT standards, not only designates the UIF as the agency in charge of preventing money laundering and terrorism financing, but also establishes certain obligations to various public and private sector entities and individuals, which are designated as Reporting Subjects (&#8220;Sujetos Obligados&#8221;), which are legally bound to inform and collaborate with the UIF. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Decree No.&#160;360/2016, as amended, the Argentine government created the National Coordination Program for Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing within the purview of the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights. Its purpose is to rearrange, coordinate and strengthen the <span style="white-space:nowrap">anti-money</span> laundering and <span style="white-space:nowrap">anti-terrorist</span> financing system at the national level, in light of the actual risks that could impact Argentine territory and the global requirements to be met under the scope of the obligations and international recommendations of the United Nations and FATF standards. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The voluntary system of declaration under the Argentine Tax Amnesty Law No.&#160;27,260 and its Regulatory Decree No.&#160;895/2016 (jointly the &#8220;Tax Amnesty Framework&#8221;) established that the information voluntarily submitted under the Tax Amnesty Framework may be used for the investigation and punishment of the crimes of money laundering and financing of terrorism. For such purpose, the UIF has the power to communicate information to other public intelligence or investigation agencies, based on a previous resolution of the UIF&#8217;s President and provided that there are serious, precise and concordant indications of the commission of money laundering and/or terrorism financing crimes. Furthermore, the Argentine tax administration (<span style="font-style:italic">Agencia de Recaudaci&#243;n y Control Aduanero</span> or &#8220;ARCA&#8221;) (formerly, &#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">Administraci&#243;n Federal de Ingresos P&#250;blicos</span>&#8221; or &#8220;AFIP&#8221;) remains obliged to report to the UIF suspicious operations detected within the Tax Amnesty Framework and to provide it with all information required by it, not being able to oppose fiscal secrecy. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Law No.&#160;27,739 provides that the ARCA will centralize, as enforcement authority, in a Public Registry of Beneficial Owners, the adequate, accurate and updated information regarding those individuals who qualify as &#8220;beneficial owners&#8221; (as defined below) according to the AML/CFT Regime. All companies, legal entities, or other contractual entities or legal structures, incorporated in Argentina or of foreign origin that carry out activities in the country and/or own goods and/or assets located and/or placed in the country, must inform their beneficial owner/s, for inclusion in such Public Registry. This disclosure must adhere to the terms and conditions established by the enforcement authority, within the terms set forth in the law and in the regulatory rules, within 60 days as from the entry into force of such law. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The UIF Resolution No.&#160;112/2021 defines &#8220;beneficial owner&#8221; as the human person(s) who owns at least 10% of the capital or voting rights of a legal person, a trust, an investment fund, an affectation patrimony and/or any other legal structure; and/or the human person/s who by other means exercises the final control of the company. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The UIF Resolution No.&#160;35/2023 updates the regulation regarding the list of people who should be considered politically exposed persons in Argentina, considering the functions they perform or have performed, as well as its closeness or affinity relationship with third parties that perform or have performed in such functions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The UIF Resolution No.&#160;78/2023, as amended, applicable to Reporting Subjects within the capital markets framework, was issued with the main purpose of setting minimum requirements related to identifying, evaluating, monitoring, administrating and mitigating money laundering and terrorism financing risk. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_63"><span style="font-style:italic">Law No.&#160;27,401 on corporate criminal liability </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On November&#160;8, 2017, the Argentine Congress enacted legislation establishing the criminal liability regime applicable to private legal entities, state-owned or not (&#8220;Corporate Criminal Liability Law&#8221;). The Corporate Criminal Liability Law applies to private legal entities for the crimes of national and transnational bribery and influence peddling, transactions that are incompatible with the exercise of public offices, and illegal exaction committed by public officials, among others. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Entities are liable for those crimes carried out directly or indirectly, with their intervention or in their name, interest or benefit. An entity is also liable for the acts of others if a third-party, without any capacity, acted in the benefit or interest of such entity, provided that the entity has ratified the acts of the third party, even implicitly. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the event of transformation, merger, absorption, <span style="white-space:nowrap">spin-off</span> or any other corporate restructuring, an entity&#8217;s responsibility will be transferred to the resulting or absorbing entity. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Corporate Criminal Liability Law also provides that an entity may be convicted even if the individual involved could not be identified or judged, provided that the circumstances of the case confirm that the crime could not have been committed without the acquiescence of such entity. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The penalties that could be applicable to entities include fines, total or partial suspension of business activities of up to ten years, suspension from participating in public bids or tenders for the execution of public works or services, dissolution and winding up of the legal entity under certain circumstances, loss or suspension of government benefits, among others. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Penalties can be graduated by judges, who will contemplate compliance with internal rules and procedures, the number and hierarchy of the officials, employees and collaborators involved, the lack of surveillance, the extent of damage caused, the amount of money involved, the willingness to reduce or repair the damage and recidivism. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">An entity will be exempted from penalties and administrative liability if it has: (i)&#160;self-reported an offense under the Corporate Criminal Liability Law; (ii)&#160;implemented, prior to the fact under prosecution, an adequate monitoring and supervision system, pursuant to the risks of its activity, dimension and economic capacity (a compliance program); and (iii)&#160;returned the undue benefit obtained. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Public Prosecutor&#8217;s Office and the relevant entity may enter into an effective collaboration agreement, whereby the latter undertakes to cooperate by disclosing data or information for the clarification of the facts, the identification of the participants and/or the recovery of the assets or profits proceeding from the crime, as well as to comply with the other conditions established by the Corporate Criminal Liability Law. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Corporate Criminal Liability Law establishes the desirable content of a compliance program, providing the mandatory requirements for those entities entering into certain agreements with the Argentine government. Compliance programs shall include a set of internal actions, mechanisms and procedures to promote integrity, supervision and control aimed at preventing, detecting and correcting irregularities and unlawful acts under this law. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:right"><span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">YPF</span> <span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> Form 20-F <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="font-family:ARIAL;color:#1a4ca3">|</span></span> 2024 </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL" id="txa866694_64"><span style="color:#1a4ca3"><span style="font-weight:bold">ITEM&#8201;10. Additional information </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_65"><span style="font-style:italic">Capital stock </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our capital stock consists of Ps. 3,933,127,930, divided into 3,764 Class&#160;A shares, 7,624 Class&#160;B shares, 40,422 Class&#160;C shares and 393,260,983 Class&#160;D shares, each fully subscribed, <span style="white-space:nowrap">paid-in</span> and authorized for stock exchange listing, with a par value of Ps. 10 per share and the right to one vote per share. Our total capital stock has not changed since December&#160;31, 2004. No preferred shares have been issued by YPF S.A. as the date of this annual report. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Class</span><span style="text-decoration:underline"></span><span style="text-decoration:underline">&#160;C shares</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As a result of the transactions carried out according to the Privatization Law, the Argentine government&#8217;s ownership percentage of our capital stock was reduced from 100% to 30%, including shares that had been set aside to be offered to our employees upon establishment of the terms and conditions by the Argentine government in accordance with Argentine law. The shares set aside to be offered to employees represented 10% of our outstanding capital stock. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In July 1997, the Class&#160;C shares set aside for the benefit of our employees in conjunction with the Privatization Law, excluding 1.5&#160;million Class&#160;C shares set aside as a reserve against potential claims, were sold through a global public offering, increasing the percentage of our outstanding shares of capital stock held by the public to 75%. Proceeds from the transactions were used to cancel debt related to the PPP, with the remainder distributed to participants in such plan. Additionally, Resolution No.&#160;1,023/2006 of the Ministry of Economy effected the transfer to the employees covered by the PPP of 1,117,717 Class&#160;C shares, corresponding to the Class&#160;C shares set aside as a reserve against potential claims, and reserving 357,987 Class&#160;C shares until a decision was reached in a pending lawsuit. Subsequently, with a final decision having been reached in the lawsuit, and consistent with the mechanism of conversion of Class&#160;C shares into Class&#160;D shares established by Decree No.&#160;628/1997 and its accompanying rules, as of December&#160;31, 2009, 1,447,983 Class&#160;C shares had been converted into Class&#160;D shares. Through Law No.&#160;25,471, the Argentine government assumed sole responsibility for any compensation to be received by YPF S.A.&#8217;s former employees who were excluded from the PPP. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">See Note 31 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements and &#8220;Item 4. Information on the Company&#8212;History and development of YPF S.A.&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_66"><span style="font-style:italic">Memorandum and articles of association </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF S.A.&#8217;s bylaws were registered on February&#160;5, 1991, under No.&#160;404 of the Book of Corporations 108, volume &#8220;A&#8221; of the Public Registry of Commerce of the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, in charge of the IGJ; and which amended bylaws were approved by National Executive Decree No.&#160;1,106/1993, and approved by YPF S.A.&#8217;s shareholders&#8217; meeting held on June&#160;11, 1993, and notarized by public deed No.&#160;175, dated June&#160;15, 1993, at the National Notary Public Office, sheet 801 of the National Registry and registered at the Public Registry of Commerce of the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, in charge of the IGJ on June&#160;15, 1993, under No.&#160;5,109 of the Book of Corporations 113, volume &#8220;A&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">At the shareholders&#8217; meeting held on January&#160;26, 2024, YPF S.A.&#8217;s shareholders approved an amendment to YPF S.A.&#8217;s bylaws, unifying the functions of the Chair of the Board of Directors and the CEO. On March&#160;15, 2024, this amendment was registered in the Public Registry of Autonomous City of Buenos Aires in charge of the IGJ. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Corporate purpose</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Section&#160;4 of our bylaws, the corporate purpose of YPF S.A. is to perform, on its own, through or in association with third parties, the survey, exploration and exploitation of liquid and/or gaseous hydrocarbon fields and other minerals; the industrialization, transportation and commercialization of these products and their direct or indirect <span style="white-space:nowrap">by-products,</span> including petrochemical products, chemical products, whether derived from hydrocarbons or not, and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-fossil</span> fuels, biofuels and their components; the generation of electrical energy through the use of hydrocarbons; among others. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For this purpose, YPF S.A. shall be entitled to manufacture, use, purchase, sell, exchange, import and export the said products and/or <span style="white-space:nowrap">by-products</span> and to carry out any other activity complementary to its industrial and commercial business or any activity which may be necessary to attain its corporate purpose. To better achieve these purposes, YPF S.A. may set up, become associated with or have an interest in any public or private entity domiciled in Argentina or abroad, within the limits set forth in our bylaws. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">For a detailed description of YPF S.A.&#8217;s corporate purpose, see &#8220;Legal information&#8212;Main business of the Company&#8221; section to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;font-weight:bold" id="txa866694_67"><span style="font-style:italic">Directors </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Our business and affairs are managed by the Board of Directors in accordance with our bylaws and the Argentine General Corporations Law. Our bylaws provide for a Board of Directors of 11 to 21 regular members (&#8220;directors&#8221;), and up to an equal number of alternate directors (&#8220;alternates&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Alternates are elected by the shareholders to replace directors appointed by the same class of shares who are absent from meetings or who are unable to exercise their duties, prior acceptance by the Board of Directors of the cause of absence or inability when they are transitory. Alternates have the responsibilities, duties and powers of directors only if and to the extent they are called upon to attend board meetings and as long as they perform duties of a director. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">According to our bylaws and the Argentine General Corporations Law, shareholders elect the directors by majority vote by class of actions in shareholders meetings. In accordance with our bylaws, the Argentine government, as sole holder of Class&#160;A shares, is entitled to elect one director and one alternate. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Supervisory Committee may elect directors in case of vacancies, in accordance with our bylaws and the Argentine General Corporations Law. In these cases, a member of the Supervisory Committee elected by the Class&#160;A shareholder, after consulting with the shareholder, may elect a director of the same class. The members of the Supervisory Committee elected by the Class&#160;D shareholders may elect directors of that same class. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Directors are appointed to serve for an office term of 1 to 3 fiscal years, as determined by each shareholders&#8217; meeting. If elected by the Supervisory Committee, directors hold office until the election of directors at the following shareholders&#8217; meeting. The election of the members of the Board of Directors is not staggered. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under the Argentine General Corporations Law, a majority of our directors must be residents of Argentina. All directors must establish a legal domicile in Argentina for service of notices in connection with their duties. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Argentine General Corporations Law and our bylaws require the Board of Directors to meet at least once every quarter in person or remotely (by video conference), and an absolute majority of directors (including both those present or participating remotely) is required in order to constitute a quorum. If a quorum is not met one hour after the start time set for the meeting, the Chair or its substitute may invite alternates of the same class as that of the absent directors to join the meeting until the quorum is reached or call a meeting for another day. Resolutions must be adopted by a majority of the directors present or participating remotely, and the Chair or its substitute is entitled to cast the deciding vote in the event of a tie. </p>
