<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_34" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_35"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_35" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_36"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForImpairmentOfNonfinancialAssetsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-34367"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.5) Impairment of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;">right-of-use</div></div> assets </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">At the closing date of each period, the Group reviews if there is any indication that these assets may have suffered impairment loss or recovery of an impairment loss recognized in previous periods. If such an indication exists, the recoverable amount of the asset is estimated. To such effect, the Group compares their carrying amount with their recoverable amount. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Such assets are grouped into CGUs, the smallest identifiable group of assets generating cash inflows or cash flows independent from those generated by other assets or groups of assets, taking into account regulatory, economic, operational, and commercial conditions. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The assets of the Group&#8217;s main CGUs are grouped into: (i)&#160;CGUs separated by basins if they correspond to assets of fields with reserves primarily of gas; (ii)&#160;a single CGU if they correspond to assets of fields with reserves primarily of oil; and (iii)&#160;a single CGU if they correspond to assets affected to oil refining, production of petrochemical products and their commercialization. Changes in regulatory, economic, operating and commercial conditions may alter the grouping of assets into CGUs. A different grouping of assets may result in different estimates of the recoverable amounts of those assets, and, therefore, generate losses or recoveries of additional impairment losses. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">If the carrying amount exceeds the recoverable amount of a CGU, an impairment loss is recognized for such excess in value in operating profit or loss in the statement of comprehensive income. Impairment losses are distributed among the CGU&#8217;s assets pro rata to their carrying amounts, which are taken into account to calculate depreciation or amortization. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The reversal of an impairment loss is recognized in operating profit or loss in the statement of comprehensive income. To such effect, the carrying amount of the CGU is increased to the revised estimate of its recoverable amount, so that this new amount does not exceed the carrying amount without considering the impairment loss recognized in previous periods. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In compliance with IFRS 6, the recoverability of exploration rights recognized in the &#8220;Intangible assets&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position is assessed separately, if any events of circumstances suggest that the carrying amount of those assets may exceed their recoverable amount and/or prior to their reclassification to the &#8220;Mining property, wells and related equipment&#8221; account of the &#8220;Property, plant and equipment&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position when their technical reliability and commercial viability are demonstrable. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Measuring the recoverable amount </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The recoverable amount for each CGU is determined as the higher of (i)&#160;its fair value less costs of disposal, i.e. the price that would be received in an orderly transaction between market participants to sell the asset, less the costs of disposal of such assets, if such value is available, reasonably reliable and based on recent negotiations with potential buyers or similar transactions, and (ii)&#160;its value in use, i.e. the projections of cash flows generated by the exploitation of the assets, based on the best estimates of income and expenses available in relation to the economic conditions that will prevail during the remaining useful life of the assets, using past results and forecasts of business evolution and market development, discounted at a rate that reflects the weighted average cost of the capital employed. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In calculating value in use, the prices for the purchase and sale of hydrocarbons, refined products and petrochemical products, the current regulations and estimates of capital expenditure standout among the most sensitive aspects included in cash flow projections of the main CGUs. The assessment of the particular and variable circumstances used in cash flow projections requires the use of estimates (see Note 2.c)). </div></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForInvestmentInAssociatesAndJointVenturesExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136338248" id="ixv-34382"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.6) Investments in associates and joint ventures </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Associates and joint ventures are accounted for using the equity method (see Note 10). </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136338248" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338248_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_36" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_37"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; <td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_40" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_41"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_41" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_42"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338248_2"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">According to this method, the investment is initially recognized at cost in the &#8220;Investments in associates and joint ventures&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position, and its carrying amount increases or decreases to recognize the investor&#8217;s interest in the profit or loss of the associate or joint venture after the acquisition date, which is reflected in the &#8220;Income from equity interests in associates and joint ventures&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. Additionally, its carrying amount increases or decreases to recognize contributions and dividends which have affected the equity of the associate or joint venture. The investment includes, if applicable, the goodwill identified in the acquisition. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Joint arrangements under which the Group has contractually agreed to exercise the joint control with another party are classified either as joint ventures when the parties have rights over the net assets of the joint arrangement, or as joint operations (see Note 2.b.1) &#8220;Joint operations&#8221; section) when the parties have rights over the assets and obligations for the liabilities relating to the joint arrangement. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Investments in entities over which an investor may exert significant influence, but not control or joint control, are classified as associates. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Investments in associates and joint ventures have been valued based on the most recent financial statements available as of the end of each period, considering significant subsequent events and transactions and/or available management information and transactions between the Group and such related companies that could have produced changes in the equity of the latter. See Note 2.b.1) &#8220;Consolidation policies&#8221; section. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Interest in companies with negative equity are presented under the &#8220;Other liabilities&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">At the closing date of each period, the Group reviews if there is any indication that these investments may have suffered an impairment in value or recovery of an impairment loss recognized in previous periods. If such an indication exists, the recoverable amount of the investment is estimated. In the event of recognition of impairment in value or recovery of an impairment loss recognized in previous periods, it is recognized in the &#8220;Income from equity interests in associates and joint ventures&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136339467" id="ixv-34454"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.7) Financial instruments </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group&#8217;s classification of financial assets is determined by the business model for the management of such assets and the characteristics of contractual cash flows. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">A financial asset is measured at amortized cost if the following conditions are met: (i)&#160;the objective of the Group&#8217;s business model is to hold the asset to collect the contractual cash flows; and (ii)&#160;the contractual terms establish payments, on specific dates, solely of principal and interest. These financial assets are initially recognized at fair value plus costs of the transaction incurred and are subsequently measured at amortized cost using the effective interest rate method less any impairment losses. Profit or loss arising from derecognition, modifications, reclassifications at fair value through profit or loss, impairment in value, or from applying the effective interest rate are recognized in the &#8220;Net financial results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">If a financial asset fails to meet any of the above conditions to be measured at amortized cost, it is measured at fair value through profit or loss. These financial assets are initially recognized at fair value and the costs of the transaction incurred are recognized as expenses in net income in the statement of comprehensive income. Changes in the fair value and results from the sale of these assets are recognized in the &#8220;Net financial results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The purchase and sale of financial assets are recognized at the date in which the Group undertakes to purchase or sell those assets. The Group reclassifies financial assets only when the business model used to manage such assets changes. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial liabilities are initially recognized at fair value less costs of the transaction incurred and are subsequently measured at amortized cost using the effective interest rate method. Interest on debt instruments is recognized in the &#8220;Net financial results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income, except for interest that is capitalized. </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136339467" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339467_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_42" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_43"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_43" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_44"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_44" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_45"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339467_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339467_2"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_45" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_46"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_46" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_47"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_47" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_48"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339467_2"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In general, the Group uses the transaction price to determine the fair value of a financial instrument on initial recognition. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Impairment of financial assets </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group evaluates the impairment of its financial assets measured at amortized cost using the expected credit loss model, recognizing in profit or loss for the period the amount of change in the expected credit losses during the lifetime of the financial asset, as an impairment gain or loss in the &#8220;Provision for doubtful receivables&#8221; account in operating profit or loss in the statement of comprehensive income, and applying the simplified approach allowed under IFRS 9 &#8220;Financial instruments&#8221; for receivables. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under IFRS 9, expected credit losses are estimated by preparing a matrix based on maturity tranches, grouping the financial assets by type of customer: (i)&#160;related parties; (ii)&#160;public sector; and (iii)&#160;private sector. These groups are subsequently divided into <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">sub-groups</div> based on special characteristics indicative of the repayment capacity, such as: (i)&#160;payment defaults; (ii)&#160;existence of guarantees; and (iii)&#160;existence of a legal proceeding already initiated or in process of initiation for collection purposes, among others. Once each group is defined, an expected credit loss rate is assigned, which is calculated on the basis of the historical payment performance adjusted to current economic conditions and forecasts of future economic conditions. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Derecognition and offsetting </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial assets are derecognized when the rights to receive cash flows from such investments and the risks and benefits related to their ownership have expired or have been transferred. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial liabilities are derecognized when they have extinguished, i.e. when the obligation has been paid or cancelled, or has expired. In addition, the Group will account for an exchange of financial instruments with substantially different terms as an extinguishment of the original financial liability, recognizing a new financial liability. Similarly, the Group will account for a substantial modification in the current terms of a financial liability as an extinguishment of the financial liability and the recognition of a new financial liability. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial assets and liabilities offset each other when there is a legally enforceable right to set off such assets and liabilities and there is an intention to settle them on a net basis, or to realize the asset and settle the liability simultaneously. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForMeasuringInventories" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-34532"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.8) Inventories </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Inventories are valued at the lower of cost and net realizable value. Cost includes costs of purchase (less trade discounts, rebates and other similar items), costs of conversion, and other costs which have been incurred in bringing the inventories to their present location and condition for their sale according to the nature of the asset. The net realizable value is the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business less costs to sell. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the case of refined products, costs are allocated in proportion to the selling price of such products (isomargin method) due to the difficulty of recognizing the production costs for each product on an individual basis. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group assesses the net realizable value of inventories at the end of each period, charging the corresponding value adjustment to net income in the statement of comprehensive income when it exceeds their net realizable value, and reversing such adjustment when the circumstances that caused it change. </div></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForCashAndCashEquivalentsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-34538"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.9) Cash and cash equivalents </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the statement of cash flows, cash and cash equivalents include cash in hand, demand deposits with banks and other short-term highly liquid investments with original maturities of up to 3 months. They do not include account overdrafts, which are presented as loans. </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_48" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_49"><div></div></ix:continuation></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_49" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_50"><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></div></div></ix:continuation></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_50" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_51"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_52" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_53"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForIssuedCapitalExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-34603"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.10) Shareholder&#8217;s equity </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The &#8220;Capital&#8221; and &#8220;Treasury shares&#8221; accounts are made up of shares of common stock held at nominal value. The difference between the subscribed amount of capital increases and the nominal value of issued shares is presented in the &#8220;Issuance premiums&#8221; account. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">When the Company buys its own shares to comply with equity-settled share-based benefit plans, the cost incurred is presented in the &#8220;Acquisition cost of treasury shares&#8221; account. The difference between such cost incurred and the amount accrued from share-based benefit plans presented in the &#8220;Share-based benefit plans&#8221; account, is presented in the &#8220;Share trading premium&#8221; account (see Notes 31 and 38). </div></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForSharebasedPaymentTransactionsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-34608"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.11) Share-based benefit plans </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group maintains share-based benefit plans with the characteristics mentioned in Note 38. Such plans are recorded in accordance with the guidelines set out in IFRS 2 &#8220;Share-based payments&#8221;. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Equity-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service based on the Group&#8217;s estimate of the number of equity instruments that will eventually vest considering their fair value at the grant date, with an offsetting credit entry in the &#8220;Share-based benefit plans&#8221; account in the statement of changes in shareholders&#8217; equity. At the end of each period, the Group reviews its estimate according to the number of equity instruments it expects will vest based on the grant conditions specified under the respective share-based benefit plan. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Cash-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service based on the Group&#8217;s estimate of the number of equity instruments that will eventually vest with an offsetting entry in the &#8220;Salaries and social security&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position, measured at fair value. Changes in the fair value of the liability are recognized in net income in the statement of comprehensive income. At the end of each period, the Group reviews its estimate according to the number of equity instruments it expects will vest based on the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-market</div> vesting conditions. The impact of the revision of the original estimates, if applicable, is recognized in the statement of comprehensive income. </div></td></tr></table></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForRecognitionOfRevenue" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136338253" id="ixv-34627"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; <td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_57" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_58"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_58" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_59"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338253_2"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In contracts related to the sale of goods, revenue is recognized when control of the goods is transferred to the end customer, which occurs when the physical possession of the goods is transferred at the point of delivery based on the contractual terms of the agreements. When the performance obligation is satisfied at a given point in time, the Group recognizes as revenue the transaction price, which is the amount of consideration to which it expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods based on the selling price of each good. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Service contracts and construction contracts establish performance obligations that are satisfied over time. In the case of service contracts, revenue is recognized as the services are effectively provided and in accordance with the contractual terms of the agreements. In the case of construction contracts, revenue is recognized by measuring the degree of progress towards complete satisfaction, where such satisfaction may be reliably measured using the input method as the most appropriate method based on the contractual terms of the agreements and considering the final estimated margin of each project and its degree of progress by the end of the period. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, and in accordance with the requirements of IFRS 15, revenues are broken down into the following categories: (i)&#160;type of good or service; (ii)&#160;sales channels; and (iii)&#160;target market, according to the reported business segments (see Notes 5 and 25). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Income from National Government incentive programs </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under IAS 20 &#8220;Accounting for government grants and disclosure of government assistance&#8221;, grants awarded by the National Government are recognized at fair value when there is reasonable assurance that the grants will be received and that the conditions attached to the grant will be complied with. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Income from National Government grants are disclosed in the &#8220;National Government incentives&#8221; line under the &#8220;Revenues&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In accordance with the requirements set out in IAS 20, the nature and characteristics of National Government grants are described in Notes 36 and 37. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForAssetsOrDisposalGroupsAndRelatedLiabilitiesClassifiedAsHeldForSaleAndDiscontinuedOperationsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136338254" id="ixv-34700"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.13) <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Non-current</div> assets held for sale </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Non-current</div> assets (or disposal group) are classified as held for sale if their carrying amount will be recovered through a sale or disposal transaction rather than through continued use. This condition is considered fulfilled only when the sale or disposal transaction is highly probable and the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> asset (or disposal group) is available for immediate sale in its current condition. The liabilities of a disposal group classified as held for sale are presented separately from other liabilities in the statement of financial position. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As provided for in IFRS 5 <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#8220;Non-current</div> assets held for sale and discontinued operations&#8221;, for the sale transaction to be highly probable the appropriate level of the Company&#180;s Management must be committed to a plan to sell the asset (or disposal group) and an active program to find a buyer and complete such plan must have been actively initiated. Further, the asset (or disposal group) must be actively marketed for sale at a price that is reasonable in relation to its fair value less costs to sell. In addition, the sale transaction should also be expected to meet the conditions to be recognized as a completed sale within 1 year from the date of classification, with the exceptions permitted by IFRS 5, and the activities required to complete the sale plan should indicate that significant changes to the sale plan are unlikely to be made or that it will be cancelled. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">An extension of the period required to complete a sale does not prevent an asset (or disposal group) from being classified as held for sale, if the delay is caused by events or circumstances beyond the entity&#8217;s control and there is sufficient evidence that the entity remains committed to its plan to sell the asset (or disposal group). </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136338254" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338254_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_59" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_60"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; <td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_63" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_64"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_64" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_65"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338254_2"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Non-current</div> assets (or disposal group) classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of the carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Immediately prior to the classification of a <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> asset (or disposal group) as held for sale, the carrying amount of the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> asset (or disposal group) is measured in accordance with applicable IFRS, including IAS 36 &#8220;Impairment of assets&#8221;. The Group recognizes an impairment loss of the asset (or disposal group) up to fair value less costs to sell. The Group recognizes a gain for any subsequent increase arising from the measurement of fair value less costs to sell of an asset (or disposal group), but not in excess of any accumulated impairment loss previously recognized. A gain or loss not previously recognized on the date of sale of the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> asset (or disposal group) is recognized at the date of derecognition. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group shall not depreciate or amortize <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> assets (or disposal group) while classified as held for sale. However, interest and other expenses attributable to liabilities associated with <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> assets (or disposal group) classified as held for sale shall continue to be recognized in the statement of comprehensive income. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group considers that an impairment loss indicator exists under IAS 36 when a <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> asset (or disposal group) meets all the requirements of IFRS 5 to be classified as held for sale prior to the approval of the issuance of the financial statements (but not at the end of the reporting period), and the carrying amount of such <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> asset (or disposal group) exceeds its fair value less costs of disposal. In this case, the Group is required to perform an impairment review of such <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> asset (or disposal group) separately from its CGU and, if necessary, an impairment loss is recognized in accordance with IAS 36. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfChangesInAccountingPoliciesExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136338255" id="ixv-34784"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.14) New standards issued </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As required by IAS 8 &#8220;Accounting policies, changes in accounting estimates and errors&#8221;, below is a summary of the standards and interpretations issued by the IASB: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Standards and interpretations, the application of which is mandatory from January</div><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"></div><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#160;1, 2024 and which have been adopted by the Group, if applicable</div> </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 1 - Classification of liabilities </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In January 2020, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 1 &#8220;Presentation of financial statements&#8221; in relation to the classification of liabilities into current and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current,</div> which are applicable retroactively to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2024. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The amendments clarify that liabilities classification in current and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current:</div> </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Must be based on existing rights at the end of the reporting period to defer settlement by at least 12 months and make explicit that only rights in place at the end of the reporting period should affect the classification of a liability. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IFRS 16 - Leases </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In September 2022, the IASB issued amendments to IFRS 16 related to the measurement of leases in sale and leaseback transactions, as it failed to specify how to measure those leases after initial recognition, which are applicable retroactively to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2024. </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136338255" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338255_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_65" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_66"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; <td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">YPF SOCIEDAD ANONIMA</div></div></div></td>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_69" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_70"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_70" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_71"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Pursuant to this amendment to IFRS 16, a seller-lessee is required to measure lease liabilities arising from a sale and leaseback transaction without recognizing a gain or loss for the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;">right-of-use</div></div> it retains and is not prevented from recognizing a gain or loss for the total or partial termination of the lease. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The adoption of these amendments has not had any effects on the Group&#8217;s consolidated financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 1 - <div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;">Non-current</div> liabilities with covenants </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On October 2022, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 1 in relation to the classification of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> liabilities with covenants, which are applicable retroactively to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2024. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The amendments clarify that the classification of loans agreements with covenants as <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> liabilities may be affected when an entity is required to comply with such covenants on or before the date of the reporting period, even if the covenant is evaluated later. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, certain additional requirements are incorporated related to the disclosure of information in notes, as this will allow users of financial statements to understand the risk that <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> liabilities might fall due in the 12 months following the reporting period. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The adoption of these amendments has not had any effects on the Group&#8217;s consolidated financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 7 and IFRS 7 - Supplier finance arrangements </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In May 2023, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 7 &#8220;Statement of cash flows&#8221; and IFRS 7 &#8220;Financial instruments: Disclosures&#8221; related to supplier finance arrangements, which are applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2024. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">These amendments introduce new disclosure requirements of qualitative and quantitative information in the annual financial statements related to the mentioned supplier finance arrangements, such as contractual terms, carrying amounts of financial liabilities, settlements made and/or maturity dates, among others. The amendments do not require comparative information disclosure. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The adoption of these amendments has not had any effects on the Group&#8217;s consolidated financial statements. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Standards and interpretations, the application of which is not mandatory as of the closing date of these consolidated financial statements and which have not been adopted by the Group</div> </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;15, 2023, CNV General Resolution No.&#160;972/2023 was published in the BO, which provides that the earlier application of the IFRS and/or their amendments will not be allowed for issuers filing financial statements with the CNV, unless specifically allowed by such agency. In this sense, the Group did not apply these IFRS and/or its modifications in advance. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IFRS 10 and IAS 28 - Sale or contribution of assets between an investor and its associate or joint venture </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In September 2014, the IASB amended IFRS 10 and IAS 28 to clarify that in transactions involving a controlled entity, the extent of the profit or loss to be recognized in the financial statements depends on whether the sold or contributed controlled company is considered a business in accordance with IFRS 3 &#8220;Business combinations&#8221;. In December 2015, the IASB indefinitely postponed the application of such modifications. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 21 - Lack of exchangeability </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In August 2023, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 21 related to the methodology to be applied where there is a lack of exchangeability between two currencies, which are applicable for reporting periods beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2025. </div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338255_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338255_3"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_71" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_72"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; <td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_75" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_76"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_76" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_77"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">These amendments eliminate the applicable methodology described in IAS 21 where there was a temporary lack of exchangeability between two currencies, and introduce the definition of exchangeability between currencies and an analysis approach that requires each entity to identify whether a currency is exchangeable into another currency for each specific purpose for which such currency would be obtained following a series of parameters, such as an assessment of whether the currency is obtained within an ordinary administrative period, the ability to obtain said currency, among others. Once the absence of exchangeability between two currencies has been identified, the exchange rate should be estimated to represent that which would be obtained in an orderly transaction between market participants and which reflects economic conditions. These amendments do not specify a methodology for estimating the exchange rate to be used, which must be developed by each entity. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, these amendments incorporate disclosure requirements such as a description of the restrictions giving rise to the absence of exchangeability, a qualitative and quantitative description of the transactions involved, the types of exchange rates used and their estimation method, a description of the risks to which the entity is exposed due to the absence of exchangeability, among others. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Group is in the process of evaluating the effects of implementing these amendments. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">IFRS 18 &#8220;Presentation and disclosure in financial statements&#8221; </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In April 2024, the IASB issued IFRS 18, which replaces IAS 1, with the objective of providing better information on the financial performance of entities, improving their comparability, which is applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2027. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">IFRS 18 introduces the following information requirements that can be distinguished into 2 main groups: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">To group income and expenses into 3 defined categories: (i)&#160;operating; (ii) financing; and (iii)&#160;investing, and include certain defined subtotals, such as the operating result and the result before financing and income tax, with the aim of improving the comparability of the statement of comprehensive income. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">In the event of including performance measures defined by management, the entity must disclose the reason why said measures are useful to users of financial statements, their method of calculation, a reconciliation between to the most directly comparable subtotal from the statement of comprehensive income, among others. </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, IFRS 18 establishes more detailed guidance on how to organize information within the financial statements and whether it should be provided in the primary financial statements or in the notes, with the aim of improving the grouping of information in the financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Group is in the process of evaluating the effects of the application of IFRS 18, which it anticipates will be significant with respect to disclosures and changes of presentation in the financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IFRS 9 and IFRS 7 - Amendments to the classification and measurement of financial instruments </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In May 2024, the IASB issued amendments to IFRS 9 and IFRS 7 related to certain issues regarding the classification and measurement requirements of IFRS 9 and the disclosure requirements of IFRS 7, which are applicable for periods beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2026: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Introduce an accounting policy option for the derecognition of a financial liability when settlement is made through an electronic payment system and certain conditions are met. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Clarify on certain assessments that an entity must perform on its financial assets, for example to determine whether a financial instrument contains contractual cash flows that are solely payments of principal and interest, or whether it also contains covenants of a contingent nature that could significantly change the timing or amount of contractual cash flows. </div></td></tr></table></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338255_4" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338255_5"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_77" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_78"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_78" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_79"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_79" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_80"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338255_5" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338255_6"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_80" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_81"><ix:exclude>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Clarify the application of the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#8220;own-use&#8221;</div> requirements: The amendments allow an entity to apply the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#8220;own-use&#8221;</div> exemption in such contracts, usually long-term contracts, if the entity has been, and expects to be, a <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">net-purchaser</div> of electricity for the contract period. The <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#8220;own-use&#8221;</div> exemption relieves an entity from measuring such contracts at fair value through profit or loss. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_88" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_89"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfAccountingJudgementsAndEstimatesExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136339656" id="ixv-35250"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the fiscal year or period. Actual future profit or loss might differ from the estimates and assessments made at the date of preparation of these consolidated financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other key sources of uncertainty about the estimates made for the preparation of these consolidated financial statements are described below: </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Oil and gas reserves </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The process of estimating oil and gas reserves is complex and is an integral part of the Group&#8217;s decision-making process. It requires significant judgments and estimates based on available oil and gas reserves that are estimated using geological, geophysical, engineering and economic data, which implies a degree of uncertainty and depends on certain factors, assumptions and variables used in such estimation, some of which are beyond the control of the Group. The expected economically recoverable oil and gas reserves and resources have been estimated by qualified internal professionals based on accepted practices in the oil and gas industry. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group makes estimates and assumptions related to proved oil and gas reserves in accordance with the rules and regulations set out in Rule <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">4-10</div> (a) of Regulation <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">S-X</div> of the SEC for the oil and gas industry, which are used for the calculation of depreciations. These proved oil and gas reserves have been estimated by qualified internal professionals and audited by DeGolyer and MacNaughton. See Note 2.b.3) &#8220; Depreciation methods and useful lives &#8220; section. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, as of December&#160;31, 2024, the Group makes reserves and resources estimates within the framework of the Petroleum Resources Management System (&#8220;PRMS&#8221;). These estimates are consistent with the Company&#8217;s management plans with focus on activities and investments in unconventional fields, which considers that one of the drivers on which the YPF&#8217;s strategy is based. DeGolyer and MacNaughton Corp. (&#8220;DeGolyer and MacNaughton&#8221;), an independent international oil and gas consulting firm, has evaluated YPF&#8217;s estimated economically recoverable oil and gas reserves and resources under PRMS, and the results of this assessment do not differ significantly from YPF&#8217;s estimates. Such estimates incorporate several factors and assumptions including, but no limited to, expected reservoir performance based on geological, geophysical, and engineering assessments; future production volumes based on historical performance and expected future operating and investment activities; oil and gas future prices and quality differentials; and future development and operating costs. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company&#8217;s Management believes these factors and assumptions are reasonable based on the information available at the time of preparing our estimates. However, these estimates may change substantially as additional data from ongoing development activities and production performance becomes available and as economic conditions impacting oil and gas prices and costs change. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This estimated volume of oil and gas reserves and resources, which is directly associated with projects, investments and business plans, is used to assess the recoverability of Upstream assets and reflects the reserves and resources that the Group currently intends to develop based on the YPF management&#8217;s best estimates of future production volumes .See Notes 2.b.5) and 2.c) &#8220; Provision for Impairment of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;">right-of-use</div></div> assets&#8221; section. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Provisions </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group&#8217;s legal or assumed obligations are recognized, measured and disclosed in compliance with IAS 37 &#8220;Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets&#8221;. Provisions include both obligations whose occurrence do not depend on future events (as the provision for environmental liabilities and the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations), as well as obligations whose fulfillment depend on the occurrence of a future event that is beyond the Group&#8217;s control (as the provision for lawsuits and contingencies). </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136339656" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339656_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_89" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_90"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_90" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_91"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_91" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_92"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339656_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339656_2"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_92" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_93"><ix:exclude>
