<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_94" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_95"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Except for the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations and the provision for environmental liabilities whose disbursement dates are estimated on the basis of work plans, the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-current</div> provision for lawsuits and contingencies, given the nature of the items included, it is not possible to reasonably estimate a specific schedule for the respective disbursement dates. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the provision for lawsuits and contingencies, the final outcome of complaints, claims and litigation, as well as the category assigned by the Group to a given matter may differ, since estimates are based on the interpretation of rules, contracts, opinions and assessments of the amount of damages. Therefore, any change in the circumstances related to this type of contingencies and the strategy defined in each case might have a significant effect on the provision recognized for lawsuits and contingencies or the category assigned by the Group. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the provision for environmental liabilities, the Group is subject to several environmental protection laws and regulations imposing penalties for pollution cleanup costs and environmental damages resulting from its operations. The Company believes that the Group&#8217;s operations substantially comply with the laws and regulations currently in force relating to environmental protection, as they have been historically interpreted and applied. However, the Company regularly conducts studies in order to gain deeper knowledge of the environmental damage of certain geographic areas where the Group operates, in order to establish their status and any necessary remediation. Until such studies are completed and assessed, the Group cannot estimate the additional costs that will need to be incurred, if any. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations, considering the number of wells not yet abandoned, as well as the complexity with respect to several geographic areas where the wells are located, current costs incurred for hydrocarbon wells abandonment are used for estimating future costs, which constitute the best estimate for the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations. Changes in laws or regulations related to the abandonment of hydrocarbon wells, in costs, in the useful lives of hydrocarbon wells, in discount rates and/or in the applied technologies have an effect on the reassessment of these estimates. The accounting policies applied to the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations are described in Note 2.b.3). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group cannot anticipate the legislation or regulations that will be enacted in the future or how future regulations will be administered, which, like the studies in progress, could materially affect the results of operations in the long term. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to certain provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets, the Group, in accordance with the exemption contemplated under IAS 37, has decided not to disclose certain critical information that could seriously adversely affect the Group in third-party claims. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Income tax and deferred taxes </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The income tax expense for the fiscal year includes both current and deferred income tax expenses, which are determined and disclosed in compliance with IAS 12. The Group regularly assesses the positions taken in tax returns regarding situations in which tax regulations are subject to interpretations and makes provisions where appropriate based on the amounts expected to be paid to tax authorities. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Income tax expense is calculated based on the tax laws enacted or substantially enacted by the end of each period in the countries where the Group operates and generates taxable income. In addition, other factors are considered, such as the evaluation of the options established by such laws and their regulations, the interpretations associated with tax treatments for transactions and/or events not expressly provided for under current tax laws, analyzing if the tax authority might accept an uncertain tax treatment, and estimates related to the timing and realization of deferred taxes, such as the expected effective tax rate at such date. </div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339656_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339656_3"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_95" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_96"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_96" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_97"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_97" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_98"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339656_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339656_4"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_98" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_99"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_99" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_100"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_100" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_101"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339656_4"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The application of tax laws in Argentina requires interpretation and, consequently, involves the application of judgement and is open to challenge by the relevant tax authorities, creating uncertainty. Uncertainty about income tax treatments is established in accordance with IFRIC 23 &#8220;Uncertainty regarding income tax treatments&#8221; based on an assessment of the range of likely tax outcomes and reflecting the strength of technical arguments. In this regard, an assessment is made as to whether it is appropriate to consider the uncertain tax treatment separately or in conjunction with other uncertain tax treatments that may exist based on the approach that best predicts the resolution of the uncertainty and then assesses whether it is probable that the relevant tax authority will accept the tax treatment or succeed in the ultimate applicable legal instance. Otherwise, if the Group concludes it is not probable that the authority will accept an uncertain tax treatment it reflects the effect of the uncertainty by recording the uncertain tax treatment on the basis of the most likely amount or expected value method, depending on which method the Group expects to better predict the resolution of the uncertainty. In making this assessment, the Group utilizes tax knowledge and expertise from qualified internal professionals and takes into consideration tax advice from external advisors. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Deferred tax assets recognize tax loss carryforwards to the extent their offsetting through future taxable income is probable. In assessing the recognition of deferred tax assets, the Group considers the anticipated reversal of deferred tax liabilities, projections of future taxable income and tax planning strategies. Assumptions regarding the generation of future taxable income depend on the Group&#8217;s estimates of future cash flows. To the extent future cash flows and taxable income differ significantly from the estimates, the Group&#8217;s capacity to realize the recorded net deferred tax assets might be affected. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Also, changes in tax regulations and/or their interpretations may affect such estimates. See Note 18. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Provision for impairment of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and <div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;"><div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">right-of-use</div></div> assets </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The main guidelines used in estimating the recoverable amount of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="white-space:nowrap;display:inline;">right-of-use</div></div> assets are described in Note 2.b.5). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Measuring the recoverable amount of an asset involves the Group&#8217;s estimates on uncertain issues, such as inflation and deflation effects on costs, the discount rate, the volume of reserves, the distribution over time of production levels associated with such reserves and future prices of products, including the outlooks on supply and demand conditions in the local and international markets for oil, natural gas and refined products, which affect selling prices considered in cash flow projections. The Group&#8217;s estimates are subject to changes as new information becomes available. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As regards measurement of CGUs that group assets of fields with oil and gas reserves, cash flow projections are used covering the economically productive life of the fields, limited in most cases by the termination of exploitation concessions, agreements or investment contracts. Cash flow projections are determined using the Group&#8217;s best estimate of oil and natural gas future selling prices, volumes of reserves, the distribution over time of production levels associated with such reserves, future investments, production costs, field depletion rates, the supply and demand in local and international markets, the current legislation and contractual conditions, among other factors. The estimates of reserves and resources used in cash flow projections for the calculation of value in use reflect the reserves and resources that the Group expects to develop. In addition, the estimated future cash flow projections include a portion of unproved reserves and resources based on the specific risks of the CGUs. The recoverable amount of CGUs that group assets of fields with oil and gas reserves is determined using a combination of inputs including proved reserves, a certain volume of unproved reserves, a certain volume of contingent resources, and production volumes. See Note 2.c) &#8220;Oil and gas reserves&#8221; section. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Cash flow projections of CGUs that group assets other than those mentioned in the previous paragraph are estimated based, among other things, on the expected evolution of sales, unit contribution margins, fixed costs, variable costs and investment levels, in line with the outlooks contemplated in business plans and taking into account the current status of each group of assets. Likewise, cash flow projections until the end of an asset&#8217;s useful life are estimated by extrapolating cash flow projections based on budgets or forecasts, using the appropriate discount rates. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The prices considered in cash flow projections are based on a combination of projections available in the markets where the Group operates and taking into account the specific circumstances that could affect the different products commercialized by the Group. In general, the Group does not consider temporarily low (or high) prices or margins as an impairment indication (or reversal of an impairment loss). Impairment assessment mainly reflects long-term prices that are consistent with intermediate points between the maximum and minimum ranges observed in the market and that are within the range of price forecasts published by third-party experts of the oil and gas industry and government agencies. Natural gas prices correspond to the average weighted price per basin and sales channel, determined according to current contracts and regulations and the market supply and demand forecast. </div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_101" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_102"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_102" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_103"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_103" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_104"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_104" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_105"><ix:exclude>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337956_106"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForComparativeInformationExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-35470"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.d) Comparative Information </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Amounts and other information corresponding to the fiscal years ended December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022 presented in these financial statements for comparison purposes arise from the consolidated financial statements ended December&#160;31, 2023. Likewise, changes have been made to the comparative figures in Notes 5 and 25 as mentioned in Note 5. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, from this fiscal year, the Group has made a change in the presentation of the items in the &#8220;Financial results, net&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income (see Note 29). This change is intended to provide more relevant and detailed information on the origin of financial results and the effects of transactions or conditions that affect the financial situation, financial performance, and cash flows of the Group such as interests and exchange differences generated by loans, among others; and improve the comparability of the Group&#8217;s financial statements with its peers. This change had no effect on the Group&#8217;s statements of financial position, statements of changes in shareholders&#8217; equity, statements of cash flows, net financial results and net income. </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfBusinessCombinationsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136337934" id="ixv-35475"><div id="fin866694_9" style="margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">3. ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSALS </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The most relevant acquisitions and disposals of companies that took effect during the years ended December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 y 2022 are described below: </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Dissolution of the companies YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings, Inc. and YPF Services USA Corp. </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January&#160;5, 2024, the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware of United States approved, effective from December&#160;28, 2023, the dissolution of YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings, Inc. (subsidiary <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfOwnershipOfYPFHoldingsIncInThesubsidiary" contextRef="PAsOn01_05_2024_ApprovalByTheSecretaryOfStateOfTheStateOfDelawareForTheDissolutionOfSubsidiaryCompaniesMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis_YCLHHoldingsIncMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-116962">100</ix:nonFraction>% controlled by YPF Holdings) and YPF Services USA Corp. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Dissolution of the company YPF International </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May&#160;6, 2024, the Plurinational Service of Registry of Commerce (&#8220;SEPREC&#8221; by its acronym in Spanish) of Bolivia approved the dissolution and liquidation of YPF International. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Acquisition of Mobil Argentina S.A. </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; Pampa Energ&#237;a S.A., operator of such concession, owns the remaining working interest. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January&#160;29, 2025 (&#8220;acquisition date&#8221;), after the fulfillment of all the closing conditions, the sale and transfer by the Sellers to YPF of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ProportionOfOwnershipInterestInSubsidiary" contextRef="P01_29_2025To01_29_2025_MobilArgentinaSaMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-116965">100</ix:nonFraction>% of MASA&#8217;s shares and capital stock was completed. The sale price of the transaction agreed by the parties was US$ <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SalePriceConsiderationOfSharesTransferred" contextRef="PAsOn01_31_2025_YpfBrazilMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-116969">2.3</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million. Pursuant to the aforementioned, the Company recognized an impairment charge in the &#8220;Impairment of property, plant and equipment and inventories write-down&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income of 3 as of December&#160;31, 2024. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Based on the closing of the aforementioned share purchase and sale agreement and considering the fair value of the assets and liabilities of YPF Brasil, as of the closing date of the transaction, the result from the sale did not have significant effects. FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group&#8217;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk), liquidity risk and credit risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following provides a description of the principal risks that could have a material adverse effect on the Group&#8217;s strategy, performance, results of operations and financial condition. The risks facing the businesses, set out below, do not appear in any particular order of potential materiality or probability of occurrence. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The sensitivity analysis of market risks included below are based on a change in one factor while holding all other factors constant. In practice this is unlikely to occur, and changes in some of the factors may be correlated, for example, changes in interest rates and changes in foreign currency rates. </div></ix:nonNumeric></div></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136338269" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_1"><div></div></ix:continuation></div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_2"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_3"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_4"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_4" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_5"><ix:exclude>

Since YPF&#8217;s functional currency is the U.S. dollar, the currency that generates the greatest exposure is the peso (the Argentine legal currency). </div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfNatureAndExtentOfRisksArisingFromFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-35865"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following table provides a breakdown of the effect that a variation of 10% in the exchange rates corresponding to the peso against the U.S. dollar would have on the Group&#8217;s net income, mainly considering the exposure of financial assets and liabilities, excluding <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-monetary</div> items and financial instruments denominated in the functional currency of YPF and its subsidiaries, as of December&#160;31, 2024: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">4.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_18" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338269_19"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group&#8217;s pricing policy regarding the sale of fuels contemplates several factors such as international and local crude oil prices, international prices of refined products, processing and distribution costs, the prices of biofuels, the exchange rate fluctuations, local demand and supply, competition, inventories, export duties, local taxes, domestic margins for the products, among others. The Group&#8217;s expectation is to align, over time, local prices with those in international markets, seeking to maintain a reasonable relationship between the local prices of crude oil and fuels, without considering short-term fluctuations, however, the exposure to price risk will depend on other key factors that are also considered in the Group&#8217;s pricing policy (including, but not limited to, changes in the exchange rate or in international prices, or potential legal or regulatory limitations, or other limitations that affect the ability of the markets to face price changes), and which may therefore lead the Group to not be able to maintain such relationship, if volatility and uncertainty in international crude oil and their <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">by-products</div> prices and exchange rate fluctuations continue into the future. In 2024, crude oil deliveries were negotiated between producers and refiners or sellers. </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Liquidity risk management </div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Liquidity risk is associated with the possibility of a mismatch between the need of funds to meet short, medium or long-term obligations. The Group intends to align the maturity profile of its financial debt to be related to its ability to generate enough cash flows to finance the projected expenditures for each year. As of December&#160;31, 2024, the availability of liquidity reached <div style="display:inline;"><ix:nonFraction name="ypf:AmountAvailableForLiquidity" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_LiquidityRiskMemberifrsfullTypesOfRisksAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117012">1,118</ix:nonFraction></div>, considering cash of <div style="display:inline;"><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:Cash" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_LiquidityRiskMemberifrsfullTypesOfRisksAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117013">304</ix:nonFraction></div> and other liquid financial assets of <div style="display:inline;"><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:OtherCashAndCashEquivalents" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_LiquidityRiskMemberifrsfullTypesOfRisksAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117014">814</ix:nonFraction></div> included in the &#8220;Cash and cash equivalents&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position (see Note 16). Additionally, the Group has other investments freely available for <div style="display:inline;"><ix:nonFraction name="ypf:OtherInvestmentsFreelyAvailable" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_LiquidityRiskMemberifrsfullTypesOfRisksAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117015">390</ix:nonFraction></div> included in &#8220;Investments in financial assets&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position (see Note 15). Uncommitted bank credit lines together with local and international capital markets constitute an important source of funding. Likewise, YPF has the capacity to issue debt under the Frequent Issuer Regime. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Based on the requirements for access to the Foreign Exchange Market established by BCRA to maturities of principal amounts of offshore debts and the issuance of debt securities denominated in foreign currency scheduled until December&#160;31, 2024, all the provisions issued were fulfilled by the Group. See Note 36.h). </div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:MaturityAnalysisForNonderivativeFinancialLiabilities" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-36214"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following table sets forth the maturity dates of the Group&#8217;s financial liabilities as of December&#160;31, 2024: </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Credit risk management </div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Credit risk is defined as the possibility of a third party not complying with its contractual obligations, thus negatively affecting results of operations of the Group. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Credit risk in the Group is measured and controlled on an individual customer basis. The Group has its own systems to conduct a permanent evaluation of credit performance and the determination of risk limits of all of its customers and to third parties, in line with best practices using for such end internal customer records and external data sources. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial instruments that potentially expose the Group to a credit concentration risk consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents, investments in financial assets, trade receivables and other receivables. The Group invests temporary excess cash primarily in high liquid investments with financial institutions with a strong credit rating both in Argentina and abroad. In the normal course of business and based on ongoing credit evaluations to its customers, the Group provides credit to its customers and certain related parties. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Likewise, the charge for doubtful receivables is charged to net income in the statement of comprehensive income, based on specific information regarding its clients. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Provisions for doubtful receivables are measured by the criteria mentioned in Note 2.b.7) &#8220;Impairment of financial assets&#8221; section. </div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfCreditRiskExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-36668"> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The maximum exposure to credit risk of the Group of December&#160;31, 2024 based on the type of its financial instruments and without excluding the amounts covered by several types of guarantees is set forth below: </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

These provisions represent the Group&#8217;s best estimate of the credit losses incurred in relation with accounts receivables. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Guarantee policy </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As collateral of the credit limits granted to customers, the Group receives several types of guarantees from its customers. In the gas stations and distributors segment, where generally long-term relationships with customers are established, mortgages prevail. For foreign customers, joint and several bonds from their parent companies prevail. In the industrial and transport segment, bank guarantees prevail. To a lesser extent, the Group has also obtained other guarantees such as credit insurances and guarantee customer-supplier, among others. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group has effective guarantees granted by third parties for <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:GuaranteesGrantedByThirdParties" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117066">1,013</ix:nonFraction>, <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:GuaranteesGrantedByThirdParties" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117067">945</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:GuaranteesGrantedByThirdParties" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117068">873</ix:nonFraction> as of December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During the fiscal years ended December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, the Group did not execute significant guarantees. </div> </ix:continuation></div></div><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/> <div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div> <div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

<td id="fin866694_11" style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">5.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION </div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The different business segments in which the Group&#8217;s organization is structured consider the different activities from which the Group can obtain revenues and incur expenses. Such organizational structure is based on the way in which the chief decision maker analyzes the main operating and financial magnitudes for making decisions about resource allocation and performance assessment, also considering the business strategy of the Group. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Business segment information is presented consistently with the manner of reporting the information used by the chief decision maker to allocate resources and assess business segment performance. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The business segment structure is organized as follows: </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Upstream </div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation of hydrocarbon fields and production of crude oil and natural gas. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from: (i)&#160;the sale of the crude oil produced to the Downstream business segment; and (ii)&#160;the sale of the natural gas produced and the natural gas retained in plant to the Gas and Power business segment. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On July&#160;1, 2024, certain assets related to the production of frac sand for well drilling/fracking purposes, which were formerly included in Upstream business segment, were assigned to Central Administration and Others. In addition, the comparative information for fiscal years ended December&#160;31, 2023 and 2022 has been restated. </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Downstream </div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Downstream business segment performs activities related to: (i)&#160;crude oil refining and the production of petrochemical products; (ii)&#160;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to the refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&#160;commercialization of refined and petrochemical products obtained from such processes; (iv)&#160;commercialization of crude oil; and (v)&#160;commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">by-products.</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Its revenues are mainly derived from the sale of crude oil, refined and petrochemical products, specialties for the agribusiness industry and grains and their <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">by-products.</div> These operations are performed through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Industries, Transportation, Aviation, Agro, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade and Transportation and Sales to Companies. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">It incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of: (i)&#160;crude oil from the Upstream business segment and third parties; (ii)&#160;gasoline and natural gas to be consumed in the refinery and petrochemical industrial complexes from the Gas and Power business segment; and (iii)&#160;propane and butane to be commercialized from the Gas and Power business segment. </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

Also, through our investments in associates and joint ventures, the Gas and Power business segment undertakes activities related to: (i)&#160;separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and gasoline; (ii)&#160;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&#160;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </div> </ix:nonNumeric></div></div> <ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136338015" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338015_1"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338015_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338015_2"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338015_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338015_3"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> </div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338015_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338015_4"><ix:exclude>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:6pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(1)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 6pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">See Note 36.h). </div></td></tr></table>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:6pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(2)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 6pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">See Note 29. </div></td></tr></table></ix:continuation><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fair value measurement </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">IFRS 13 &#8220;Fair value measurement&#8221; defines the fair value of a financial instrument as the amount for which an asset could be exchanged, or a financial liability settled, between knowledgeable, independent parties in an arm&#8217;s length transaction. All financial instruments measured at fair value are assigned to one of the valuation hierarchy levels specified under IFRS 13 (as well as loans measured at amortized cost whose fair value is disclosed in &#8220;Fair value of financial assets and financial liabilities measured at amortized cost&#8221; section below). This valuation hierarchy comprises 3 levels. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(i)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Level&#160;1: The valuation is based on unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical financial assets or liabilities that the Group can refer to at the end of the reporting period. A market is deemed active if transactions take place with sufficient frequency and in sufficient quantity for price information to be available on an ongoing basis. A quoted price in an active market provides the most reliable evidence of fair value and shall be used without adjustment to measure fair value whenever available. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(ii)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Level&#160;2: The fair value is determined by using valuation methods based on inputs directly or indirectly observable in the market. If the financial instrument concerned has a fixed contract period, the inputs used for valuation must be observable for the whole of this period. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">(iii)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Level&#160;3: The Group uses valuation techniques not based on inputs observable in the market. This is only permissible insofar as no market data is available. The inputs reflect the Group&#8217;s assumptions regarding the factors, which market players would consider in their pricing. The Group uses the best available information, including internal data. </div></td></tr></table></ix:continuation></div></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338017_11" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338017_12"><div></div></ix:continuation></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338017_12" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338017_13"><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></div></div></ix:continuation></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338017_13" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338017_14"><ix:exclude>

The Company considered this to be an impairment loss indicator under IAS 36. Accordingly, the Company performed an impairment review separately from its CGU and recognized an impairment charge of property, plant and equipment of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLossPropertyPlantAndEquipment" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_CguOilCguGasAustralBasinAndCguGasNeuquinaBasinMemberifrsfullIndividualAssetsOrCashgeneratingUnitsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118136">1,782</ix:nonFraction> (<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLossPropertyPlantAndEquipmentNetOfTax" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_CguOilCguGasAustralBasinAndCguGasNeuquinaBasinMemberifrsfullIndividualAssetsOrCashgeneratingUnitsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118137">1,158</ix:nonFraction> net of the income tax effect) as of December&#160;31, 2023, considering the net assets and recoverable amount of each disposal group. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Considering, most of the transactions of oil and gas assets in Argentina during recent years are related to fields where the main targeted reservoirs are unconventional formations (specifically, the Vaca Muerta formation), and for the transactions that could be considered comparable to the assets evaluated in each disposal group, the publicly available information was insufficient to derive conclusions for a fair value in active markets for identical assets to those of each disposal group (Level 1), or inputs other than quoted prices included within Level&#160;1 that are observable for the assets, either directly or indirectly (Level 2), the recoverable amount for each disposal group was determined applying an asset valuation technique commonly used in the oil and gas industry which is the discounted cash flow analysis technique. This valuation technique is considered to be Level&#160;3 in the fair value hierarchy due to unobservable inputs used in the valuation, representing the fair value less costs of disposal measurement. In estimating the discounted cash flows of the disposal groups, the Company worked closely with a third-party qualified independent valuer not related to the Group, with appropriate qualifications, to establish the appropriate valuation techniques and inputs to the model. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_22" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_23"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_23" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_24"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_24" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_25"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_25" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_26"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">8.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">PROPERTY, PLANT AND EQUIPMENT (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338295_27"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This valuation technique required projections of production, operating expenses, capital expenditures, hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs, royalties and taxes and the date of the termination of the concessions. The key assumptions to which the disposal groups recoverable amounts are most sensitive are production, crude oil and natural gas prices, discount rate and macroeconomic variables. Values for reserves were expressed in terms of future gross revenues, future net revenues, present value and considering a <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">ten-year</div> extension of the termination of certain concessions expiring in the near term. Future net revenues were calculated by deducting from future gross revenues royalties paid in cash, operating expenses, capital expenditures and hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs, production taxes, and income tax. Operating expenses include fields operating expenses, transportation and processing expenses, and an allocation of overhead that directly relates to production activities. Capital expenditures include drilling and completion costs, facilities costs, and maintenance costs. Hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs are those costs associated with the removal of facilities, plugging of wells and reclamation and restoration associated with the abandonment of hydrocarbon wells. The recoverable amount was defined as future net revenues discounted at a discount rate after income tax, which as of December&#160;31, 2023 was <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfDiscountRatesUsedInCurrentEstimateOfValueInUse" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118138">15</ix:nonFraction>%. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, the Group recognized an impairment charge of property, plant and equipment for the <div style="display:inline;">CGU Gas - Northwest Basin</div> of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLossPropertyPlantAndEquipment" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_CguGasNorthwestBasinMemberifrsfullIndividualAssetsOrCashgeneratingUnitsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118139">58</ix:nonFraction> (<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLossPropertyPlantAndEquipmentNetOfTax" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_CguGasNorthwestBasinMemberifrsfullIndividualAssetsOrCashgeneratingUnitsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118140">37</ix:nonFraction> net of income tax effect), generated by a combination of variables, but mainly due to production costs increases. The discount rate after income tax used as of December&#160;31, 2024 was <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfDiscountRatesUsedInCurrentEstimateOfValueInUse" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118141">14.80</ix:nonFraction>%, and the recoverable amount after income tax as of such date of the CGU Gas - Northwest Basin was <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:RecoverableValueAfterTaxes" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_CguGasNorthwestBasinMemberifrsfullIndividualAssetsOrCashgeneratingUnitsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118142">28</ix:nonFraction>. In addition, as of December&#160;31, 2024, the carrying amount of the net assets of the CGU Gas - Neuquina Basin amounts to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RecoverableAmountOfAssetOrCashgeneratingUnit" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_CguGasNeuquinaBasinMemberifrsfullIndividualAssetsOrCashgeneratingUnitsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118143">2,769</ix:nonFraction> and approximates its recoverable amount. The Group will continue analyzing the prospects for the variables mentioned above to further estimate their impact on expected cash flows. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, the Group has no significant exploratory well costs under evaluation for a period longer than 1 year. </div><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DisclosureInTabularFormOfDistributionOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentByGeographicAreaExplanatoryTextBlock" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-51275"><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Likewise, in accordance with IFRS 8, the distribution of property, plant and equipment by geographic area is broken down below: </div><div style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

In the context of this transaction, YPF received <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:AcquisitiondateFairValueOfTotalConsiderationTransferred" contextRef="PAsOn01_31_2025_CampamentoCentralCanadonPerdidoMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118529">28</ix:nonFraction>. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">At the closing date of the aforementioned assignment agreements for the &#8220;Estaci&#243;n Fern&#225;ndez Oro&#8221; and &#8220;Campamento Central - Ca&#241;ad&#243;n Perdido&#8221; exploitation concessions and considering the fair value less costs to sell of such groups of assets, the result from the sale of such assets does not have significant effects. Additionally, the derecognition of the carrying amount of net assets held for sale and liabilities directly associated with assets held for sale related to such exploitation concessions is <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:AssetsAndLiabilitiesClassifiedAsHeldForSale" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_CampamentoCentralCanadonPerdidoMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118530">45</ix:nonFraction>. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, as mentioned above, the Company has signed assignment agreements for certain groups of assets that are subject to closing conditions mainly related to regulatory and provincial approvals, for which the Company is taking the necessary steps to close; and it is highly probable that these assets will be disposed. In addition, the Company maintains groups of assets as held for sale for which agreements have not yet been signed but continuous in negotiations with third parties for their disposal or reversal. The delay in the fulfillment of the plan for the disposal of mature fields is due to the complexity of the negotiations, which is beyond the Company&#8217;s control. However, YPF remains committed to its plan for the disposal of such assets, with active negotiations with third parties including, among others, the operational optimization plan executed in the Province of Santa Cruz mentioned below; as well as compliance with the closing conditions of the signed assignment agreements. As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Company considers that the disposal of such assets continues to be highly probable during 2025. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_6" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_7"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_7" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_8"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_8" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_9"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_9" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_10"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_10" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_11"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">11. ASSETS HELD FOR SALE AND ASSOCIATED LIABILITIES (cont.) </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136339583_11">
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Accounting matters </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2023, considering the aforementioned YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors&#8217; decision, impairment indicators under IAS 36 were evaluated for each group of assets. Accordingly, the Company performed an impairment review separately from its CGU and recognized an impairment charge of property, plant and equipment (see Note 8). The disposal of these groups of assets did not meet the requirements of IFRS 5 to be classified as held for sale as of December&#160;31, 2023, therefore these groups of assets were not classified as held for sale as of that date. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In February 2024, after the fulfillment of all the requirements of IFRS 5, the assets were reclassified from the &#8220;Property, plant and equipment&#8221; line item to the &#8220;Assets held for sale&#8221; line item and the related provisions for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations and for environmental liabilities and liabilities for concessions to the &#8220;Liabilities directly associated with assets held for sale&#8221; line item as current items in the statement of financial position. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Considering that, after their classification, the assets classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell (&#8220;fair value&#8221;), the Company evaluates the changes in fair value, recognizing, for such changes, a profit up to the limit of the impairment loss previously recognized or an impairment loss in addition to that previously recognized (see Note 2.b.13)). Considering, most of the transactions of oil and gas assets in Argentina during recent years are related to fields where the main targeted reservoirs are unconventional formations (specifically, the Vaca Muerta formation), and for the transactions that could be considered comparable to the assets evaluated in each disposal group, the publicly available information was insufficient to derive conclusions for a fair value in active markets for identical assets to those of each disposal group (Level 1), or inputs other than quoted prices included within Level&#160;1 that are observable for the assets, either directly or indirectly (Level 2), the recoverable amount for each disposal group was determined in accordance with the offers received and the sales agreements for the groups of assets with signed assignment agreements (Level 3) and/or by applying an asset valuation technique commonly used in the oil and gas industry, which is the discounted cash flow analysis technique. This valuation technique is considered Level&#160;3 in the fair value hierarchy due to the unobservable inputs used in the valuation and represents the fair value for the groups of assets to be reversed or under negotiation for disposal. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This valuation technique required projections of production, operating expenses, capital expenditures, hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs, royalties and taxes, and the date of the termination of the concessions. The key assumptions to which the disposal groups recoverable amounts are most sensitive are production, crude oil and natural gas prices, discount rate and macroeconomic variables. Values for reserves were expressed in terms of future gross revenues, future net revenues, present value and considering a <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">ten-year</div> extension of the termination of certain concessions expiring before 2030. Future net revenues were calculated by deducting from future gross revenues royalties paid in cash, operating expenses, capital expenditures and hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs, production taxes, and income tax. Operating expenses include fields operating expenses, transportation and processing expenses, and an allocation of overhead that directly relates to production activities. Capital expenditures include drilling and completion costs, facilities costs, and maintenance costs. Hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs are those costs associated with the removal of facilities, plugging of wells and reclamation and restoration associated with abandonment of hydrocarbon wells. Severance indemnities and operating optimizations expenditures were not considered. The recoverable amount was defined as future net revenues discounted at a discount rate after income tax, which as of December&#160;31, 2024 was <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfDiscountRatesUsedInCurrentEstimateOfValueInUse" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118531">15</ix:nonFraction>%. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, based on the aforementioned evaluation of the changes in the fair value, the Company recognized a loss due to changes in the fair value of assets held for sale by <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:GainLossOnChangeInFairValueOfAssetHeldForSale" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" sign="-" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118532">260</ix:nonFraction> in the &#8220;Other net operating results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income, mainly generated by the more pronounced decline of the fields and the lower production than expected due to its performance. The carrying amount of the assets held for sale may be adjusted in future periods depending on the results of the disposal process carry out by YPF and the economic consideration to be agreed with third parties for such assets. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, and in relation to the Mature Fields Project, in December 2024, the Company has committed to an optimization plan that involves operating efficiency measures related to the reduction of third party employees directly or indirectly affected to the operation of areas in the Province of Santa Cruz related to certain groups of assets held for disposal. For such concept, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2024, the Company recognized a charge for <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ProvisionForOperatingOptimizations" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118533">266</ix:nonFraction> in the &#8220;Provision for operating optimizations&#8221; line under &#8220;Other operating results, net&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the Company&#8217;s own personnel and for the assignment agreements signed for 8 groups of assets (24 areas) mentioned above, the Company, for the year ended December&#160;31, 2024, recognized a charge for severance indemnities of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ProvisionForSeveranceIndemnities" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118534">63</ix:nonFraction> in the &#8220;Provision for severance indemnities&#8221; line under &#8220;Other operating results, net&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

In certain lawsuits related to events or acts that took place before December&#160;31, 1990, YPF has been required to make advance payments in compliance with certain judicial decisions. YPF has the right to be reimbursed for these payments by the Argentine Government based on the indemnity mentioned above. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In pending lawsuits, YPF has claimed its right to be indemnified by the Argentine Government for events and contingencies prior to January&#160;1, 1991 under Law No.&#160;24,145 (YPF&#8217;s Privatization Law) and Decree No.&#160;546/1993. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17.a.2) Claims arising from restrictions in the natural gas market </div></div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
