<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_15" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_16"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17. PROVISIONS (cont.) </div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_16" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_17"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17.a.3) Users and Consumers Association </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Users and Consumers Association claims (originally against Repsol YPF S.A. before extending its claim to YPF) the reimbursement of the overprice allegedly charged to bottled LPG consumers from periods between years 1993 to 1997 and from 1997 to 2001. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;28, 2015, the Lower Court rendered judgment admitting the claim for compensation from period between years 1993-1997 filed by the Users and Consumers Association against YPF and ordered the Company to transfer the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ProceedsFromTransferActivity" contextRef="P12_28_2015To12_28_2015_ComisionNacionalDeLaDefensaLaCompetenciaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118894">98</ix:nonFraction> plus interest (to be estimated by the accounting expert in the settlement period) to the SE, to be allocated to the trust fund created under Law No.&#160;26,020. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The judgment rejects the claim for the items corresponding to the period 1997-2001, considering that YPF&#8217;s position in the domestic bulk LPG market had not been sufficiently proved. Furthermore, the judgment dismissed the complaint against Repsol S.A., as Repsol YPF S.A. had no equity interest in YPF, nor any other kind of relation with YPF from 1993 to 1997, period in which the plaintiffs claim YPF abused its dominant position. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Both parties filed an appeal against that judgment, which was admitted with suspensive effect. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;7, 2017, the Company was notified about the Court of Second Appeals&#8217; judgment, which: (i)&#160;confirmed the claims for compensation for the 1993-1997 period; (ii)&#160;extends the Users and Consumers Association claim from period between years 1997 to 1999 under the item &#8220;equity transfer of consumers to producers for the higher cost of LPG&#8221;, deferring the settlement related to this item to the execution stage of the judgment; and (iii)&#160;partially grants the appeal filed by the defendant with respect to the item &#8220;damage caused by lower or different energy consumption due to the higher cost of LPG&#8221;. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">It should be noted that the judgment confirmed by the Court of Second Appeals does not order YPF to pay the claimant the ultimately settled amount, but rather to transfer such funds to the SE for the funds to be allocated to a trust fund created by Law No.&#160;26,020, in order to expand the natural gas network in areas with lower resources according to the criteria established by the enforcement authority. The enforcement authority, within 6 months from the settlement of the judgment amount becomes final, must present the corresponding feasibility studies (Decree No.&#160;470/2015) together with a work plan beginning within 6 months from the presentation of the feasibility studies. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Finally, the Company filed an extraordinary appeal against the Court of Second Appeals&#8217; judgment, which was sustained and the court file was submitted to the CSJN, being the enforcement of the Court of Second Appeals&#8217; judgment still suspended as of the date of issuance of the consolidated financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;2, 2021, the CSJN forwarded the file to the National Attorney General&#8217;s Office for its opinion on the legal merits of the extraordinary appeal. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;13, 2023, the National Attorney General&#8217;s Office issued an opinion recommending the CSJN to grant the extraordinary appeal lodged by YPF and to reverse the Court of Second Appeals&#8217; judgment. As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the extraordinary appeal is pending resolution. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17.a.4) Environmental claims </div></div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">La Plata </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the operation of the refinery owned by YPF in La Plata city, Province of Buenos Aires, there are certain judicial claims, mostly filed by neighbors of the area seeking (i)&#160;compensation for damages arising from the alleged environmental contamination caused by the operation of the La Plata Refinery and (ii)&#160;the environmental remediation of the waterways adjacent to the mentioned refinery. Should these claims be sustained, they could demand additional investments related to the operation of La Plata Refinery. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2006 YPF submitted a presentation before the Environmental Policy Secretariat of the Province of Buenos Aires, whereby it suggested the performance of a study for the characterization of risks associated with the aforementioned contamination. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_17" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_18"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_18" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_19"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_19" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_20"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_20" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_21"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_21" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_22"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17. PROVISIONS (cont.) </div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_22" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_23"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfRiskInEnvironmentalClaims" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" id="ixv-118895">On January&#160;25, 2011, YPF executed an agreement with the Provincial Agency for Sustainable Development (&#8220;OPDS&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) of the Province of Buenos Aires, under the Remediation, Liability and Environmental Risk Control Program, created under Resolution No.&#160;88/2010 of the OPDS.</ix:nonNumeric> Under this agreement, the parties agreed to jointly perform a work program in the channels adjacent to La Plata Refinery over a term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:RefineryTermPeriod" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-118896">8</ix:nonNumeric> years, and which involved the characterization and risk assessment studies of channel sediments. The agreement provides that should corrective actions be detected as a result of the risk assessment studies, the different alternatives and available techniques will be considered, as well as the steps needed for their implementation. Dating studies of deposited material will also be performed under the agreement, in order to determine the responsibilities of the Argentine Government in view of its obligation to hold YPF harmless in accordance with the article 9 of YPF&#8217;s Privatization Law. This study proved between <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfHydrocarbons" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118897">88</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfHydrocarbons" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118898">91</ix:nonFraction>% of the hydrocarbons present in the channels were deposited prior to 1991. In this context, YPF, with the agreement of the OPDS, carried out several studies and characterizations through specialized consultants whose progress was notified to the provincial agency. The agreement was replaced by Resolution No.&#160;380/2019 issued by the OPDS, which approves the remediation modality suggested by YPF (monitored natural recovery) over a term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ExtendedPeriodCoveredByFinancialStatements" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" id="ixv-118899">24 months</ix:nonNumeric>. YPF has answered all points required by the OPDS and requested the extension of the resolution. On June&#160;26, 2023, through Resolution No.&#160;2,775/2023 issued by the Ministry of Environment of the Province of Buenos Aires, YPF obtained a <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">two-year</div> extension to continue with the remediation and monitoring works through the suggested remediation modality (monitored natural recovery). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding the judicial claims mentioned above, on February&#160;7, 2022, the Company was notified of the first instance judgment which considered the environmental damage had been proved, and therefore ordered that activities should cease and the environmental damage affecting the waterways adjacent to La Plata Refinery be remedied. <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:LossContingentDamagesSought" contextRef="P02_07_2022To02_07_2022_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" id="ixv-60196">This decision determined the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">co-defendants&#8217;</div> joint liability for the damages in the following proportions: YPF 90% (the Argentine Government 80% and YPF 20%) and the 2 <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">co-defendant</div> companies 10%. The decision was appealed by the Company.</ix:nonNumeric> On August&#160;29, 2024 the Court of Appeals confirmed the obligation to cease and remedy the environmental damage determined in the first instance. The <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">co-defendants</div> filed an extraordinary appeal to the CSJN and, as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, such appeal is pending resolution. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

These processes are at the discovery stage. Fuel would have emerged and become perceptible in November 2002, which resulted in remediation works conducted by the Company since then in the affected area, supervised by the environmental authority of the Province of Buenos Aires. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Argentine Government denied any responsibility to indemnify YPF in this case, wherefore the Company sued the Argentine Government to obtain a judicial decision declaring the invalidity of such decision. As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, this lawsuit is pending resolution. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_27" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_28"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17. PROVISIONS (cont.) </div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_28" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_29"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17.a.5) Tax claims </div></div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Dispute over the cost deduction for hydrocarbon well abandonment </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company has recorded the hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs in accordance with the criteria detailed in Note 2.b.3) and, in the absence of a specific treatment of this matter in the Income Tax Law and its Regulatory Decree, has deducted the charge for hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs in the calculation of income tax, based on the general criteria of the tax standard for deduction of expenses (accrual criteria). Nevertheless, this interpretation has been objected to by the AFIP, which would allow for deductions once the expense has been incurred. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The AFIP understands that the deduction of hydrocarbon well abandonment costs should be deferred until the taxpayer has the opportunity to actually proceed to well abandonment, once the wells have been depleted, as it considers the abandonment of the well is the event triggering the accrual of hydrocarbon well abandonment costs. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On the other hand, the Company, as well as other companies in the oil and gas industry, understand that the substantial event generating costs in connection with well abandonment is, in fact, the act of drilling, as drilling causes environmental impact and, consequently, the obligation to repair such impact (abandonment). This obligation is not subject to any condition since there is no uncertainty as to whether well depletion will inevitably occur. The Company has learned that similar disputes have been raised by the AFIP with other companies in the oil and gas industry. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In this respect, in June 2016, the SRH of MINEM, the body in charge of clarifying the origin of the legal obligation in this respect, and in response to a consultation of the Chamber of Oil Exploration and Production, ruled in favor of the position of the oil and gas companies and concluded that drilling is the substantial event generating the charge for well abandonment costs. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This response of the Chamber of Oil Exploration and Production has been informed to the AFIP by both the SRH and by YPF but, with different arguments the AFIP rejected this position. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On November&#160;7, 2018, the Company was notified by AFIP of the commencement of a determination procedure with respect to the projected adjustment for fiscal years 2011 to 2016. The Company filed its defense with the AFIP on December&#160;21, 2018. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;3, 2020, the Company was notified by AFIP of the commencement of a determination procedure with respect to the projected adjustment for fiscal years 2017. The Company filed its defense with the AFIP on March&#160;17, 2020. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;26, 2020, Law No.&#160;27,562 was published in the BO, expanding the regime for the regularization of taxes, social security contributions and customs duties originally established under Law No.&#160;27,541, which was regulated by AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;4,816/2020. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;9, 2021, YPF waived the statute of limitations for fiscal year 2014 to allow the AFIP to analyze the legal grounds for the defense filed by the Company on December&#160;21, 2018, in the context of the administrative proceeding. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company, based on the opinion of its external advisors, and notwithstanding the technical merits for defending its position, evaluated the regularization regimes provided for under Laws No.&#160;27,562 and No.&#160;27,653 for the income tax and the compensations made in due course with the credit balances generated by such tax, and on November&#160;30, 2020 and March&#160;30, 2022, adhered to the aforementioned regimes, thus putting an end to the dispute over the cost deduction for hydrocarbon well abandonment corresponding to fiscal periods 2011 to 2013 and fiscal periods 2014 to 2017, respectively. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding fiscal years following and including 2018, it should be noted that since the enactment of Law No.&#160;27,430 (&#8220;Tax Reform&#8220;) in December 2017, the deduction of the well abandonment costs at the time of the drilling phase was admitted, considering them as part of the investment cost, regardless of the period in which the effective disbursement is made. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_29" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_30"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_30" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_31"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_31" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_32"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_32" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_33"><ix:exclude>

PROVISIONS (cont.) </div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338242_34"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17.a.6) Other pending litigation </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During the normal course of business, the Group has been sued in numerous legal proceedings at labor, civil and commercial courts. The Company, in consultation with its external counsel, has established a provision considering to such end the best estimate based on information available as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, including legal fees and court costs. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">17.b) Provision for environmental liabilities and Provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Based on the Group&#8217;s current remediation and hydrocarbon well abandonment plans, the Group has set up a provision for environmental liabilities, where assessments and/or remedial actions are probable and can reasonably be estimated, and for hydrocarbon well abandonment obligations, considering the number of wells not yet abandoned, the costs and schedule for the timing of disbursements. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfIncomeTaxExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136338288" id="ixv-60353"><div id="fin866694_24" style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">18. INCOME TAX </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The income tax expense contemplates the application of the integral inflation adjustment mechanism applicable to property, plant and equipment, and the indexation of the accumulated tax losses carryforward until the concurrence of the tax result of the fiscal year 2024, all considering that the assumption of confiscation is verified, in the Company&#8217;s opinion, in accordance with the jurisprudence of the CSJN in force as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company, based on the opinion of its external advisors, considers that the position adopted is in line with the criteria, in accordance with the jurisprudence of the CSJN and a possible controversy with the tax authorities in the ultimate applicable legal instance would have a final and definitive resolution favorable to the Company, in accordance with the guidelines of IFRIC 23 (see Note 2.c) &#8220;Income tax and deferred taxes&#8221; section). For the year ended December&#160;31, 2024, the assumed tax criteria generated a profit of 981. </div><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DisclosureOfDetailedInformationAboutIncomeTaxExpenseExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-60358"><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The calculation of the income tax expense accrued for the years ended December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022 is as follows: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">YPF SOCIEDAD ANONIMA</div></div></div></td>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfShareCapitalReservesAndOtherEquityInterestExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" id="ixv-75732"><div id="fin866694_37" style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">31. SHAREHOLDERS&#8217; EQUITY </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, the Company&#8217;s capital amounts to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SubscribedCapital" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120234">3,922</ix:nonFraction> and treasury shares amount to 11 represented by <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:NumberOfSharesSubscribed" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_OrdinarySharesMemberifrsfullClassesOfShareCapitalAxis" unitRef="Unit_shares" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120235">393,312,793</ix:nonFraction> book-entry shares of common stock and divided into <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfClassesOfShares" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" id="ixv-120236">four classes of shares (A, B, C and D)</ix:nonNumeric>, with a par value of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ParValuePerShare" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_ARS_per_Share" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120237">10</ix:nonFraction> pesos and <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfVotingRights" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" id="ixv-120238">1 vote per share</ix:nonNumeric>. These shares are fully subscribed, <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">paid-in</div> and authorized for stock exchange listing. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2024, there are <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:NumberOfSharesOutstanding" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_ClassASharesMemberifrsfullClassesOfShareCapitalAxis" unitRef="Unit_shares" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120239">3,764</ix:nonFraction> Class&#160;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&#160;A share remains outstanding, <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfGrantBasedOnSharesOutstanding" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" id="ixv-120240">the affirmative vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&#160;mergers; (ii) acquisitions of more than <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:PercentageOfVotingEquityInterestsAcquired" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_ClassASharesMemberifrsfullClassesOfShareCapitalAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120241">50</ix:nonFraction>% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&#160;transfers of all the YPF&#8217;s exploitation and exploration rights; (iv)&#160;the voluntary dissolution of YPF; (v)&#160;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina; or (vi)&#160;make an acquisition that would result in the purchaser holding <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:PercentageOfVotingEquityInterestsAcquired" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_CapitalStockMemberifrsfullClassesOfShareCapitalAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120242">15</ix:nonFraction>% or more of the Company&#8217;s capital stock, or <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:PercentageOfVotingEquityInterestsAcquired" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024_ClassDSharesMemberifrsfullClassesOfShareCapitalAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120243">20</ix:nonFraction>% or more of the outstanding Class&#160;D shares. Items (iii)&#160;and (iv) also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress.</ix:nonNumeric> </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;26, 2024, the General Shareholders&#8217; Meeting was held, which approved the statutory financial statements of YPF (see Note 2.b.1)) corresponding to the year ended on December&#160;31, 2023 and, additionally, approved the following in relation to the retained earnings: (i)&#160;completely disaffect the reserve for future dividends, the reserve for purchase of treasury shares and the reserve for investments; (ii)&#160;absorb accumulated losses in unappropriated retained earnings and losses up to the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RetainedEarnings" contextRef="PAsOn04_26_2024_UnappropriatedRetainedEarningsAndLossesMemberifrsfullComponentsOfEquityAxis" unitRef="Unit_MXN" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120244">1,003,419</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of pesos (US$ <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RetainedEarnings" contextRef="PAsOn04_26_2024_UnappropriatedRetainedEarningsAndLossesMemberifrsfullComponentsOfEquityAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120245">1,244</ix:nonFraction> million); (iii) allocate the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RetainedEarnings" contextRef="PAsOn04_26_2024_ReservesForPurchaseOfTreasuryShareMemberifrsfullComponentsOfEquityAxis" unitRef="Unit_MXN" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120246">28,745</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of pesos (US$ <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RetainedEarnings" contextRef="PAsOn04_26_2024_ReservesForPurchaseOfTreasuryShareMemberifrsfullComponentsOfEquityAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120247">36</ix:nonFraction> million) to constitute a reserve for purchase of treasury shares; and (iv)&#160;allocate the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RetainedEarnings" contextRef="PAsOn04_26_2024_ReserveOfGainsAndLossesFromInvestmentsInEquityInstrumentsMemberifrsfullComponentsOfEquityAxis" unitRef="Unit_MXN" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120248">3,418,972</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million of pesos (US$ <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:RetainedEarnings" contextRef="PAsOn04_26_2024_ReserveOfGainsAndLossesFromInvestmentsInEquityInstrumentsMemberifrsfullComponentsOfEquityAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120249">4,236</ix:nonFraction> million) to constitute a reserve for investments. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Until the enactment of Law No.&#160;26,741 described below, Repsol S.A. (&#8220;Repsol&#8221;) had a participation in the Company, directly and indirectly, of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ProportionOfOwnershipInterestInEquity" contextRef="P05_04_2012To05_04_2012_RepsolSAMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120250">57.43</ix:nonFraction>% shareholding while Petersen Energ&#237;a S.A.U. and its affiliates exercised significant influence through a <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ProportionOfOwnershipInterestInSharesByRelatedParty" contextRef="P05_04_2012To05_04_2012_PetersenEnergiaSauAndAffiliatesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120251">25.46</ix:nonFraction>% shareholding of YPF&#8217;s capital stock. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Law No.&#160;26,741 enacted on May&#160;4, 2012, changed YPF&#8217;s shareholding structure declared the Class&#160;D shares of YPF owned by Repsol as national public interest and subject to expropriation representing 51% of YPF&#8217;s equity. In addition, Law No.&#160;26,741 declared that achieving self-sufficiency in the supply of hydrocarbons as well as in the exploration, exploitation, industrialization, transportation and sale of hydrocarbons, shall be considered of national public interest and a priority for Argentina, with the goal of guaranteeing socially equitable economic development, job creation, the increase of the competitiveness of various economic sectors and the equitable and sustainable growth of the provinces and regions. The shares subject to expropriation were distributed as follows: <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfSharesSubjectToExpropriation" contextRef="P05_04_2012To05_04_2012_FederalGovernmentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120252">51</ix:nonFraction>% for the Argentine National Government and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfSharesSubjectToExpropriation" contextRef="P05_04_2012To05_04_2012_StateOrProvinceMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120253">49</ix:nonFraction>% for certain provinces. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During the fiscal years ended December&#160;31, 2024 and 2023, the Company has not repurchased its own shares. During the fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2022, the Company has repurchased <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:TreasuryStockSharesAcquired1" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_shares" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120254">1,888,798</ix:nonFraction> of its own shares issued for an amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:PurchaseOfTreasuryShares" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120255">28</ix:nonFraction>, for purposes of compliance with the share-based benefit plans (see Note 38). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In accordance with the provisions of the LGS and the CNV rules, the Company must set aside a legal reserve of not less than <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:LegalReservesAsAPercentageOfNetProfitPriorYearAdjustmentsAndTransferFromOtherComprehensiveIncomeMinimum" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120256">5</ix:nonFraction>% of the positive result resulting from the algebraic sum of net profit or loss for the year, prior-year adjustments, transfers from other comprehensive income to unappropriated retained earnings and losses from previous years, until such reserve reaches <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:MaximumPercentageOfLegalReserve" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120257">20</ix:nonFraction>% of the sum of the &#8220;Capital&#8221; and &#8220;Adjustment of capital&#8221; accounts and the translation differences related to such accounts according to the CNV rules. As of December&#160;31, 2024, the legal reserve has been fully integrated, amounting to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:StatutoryReserve" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120258">787</ix:nonFraction>. Likewise, the Company&#8217;s Shareholders&#8217; Meeting has defined voluntary reserves for future dividends, for investments and for purchase of treasury shares. In relation to the reserve for future dividends and in compliance with the LGS, we declare dividends in the currency of legal tender in Argentina, which is the peso. The dividends are declared and distributed based on the last annual audited financial statements in pesos submitted to the CNV. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Considering Article 3, item 11, sections c) and e), Chapter III, Title IV of CNV rules, the balances of the accounts &#8220;Acquisition cost of treasury shares&#8221; and &#8220;Share trading premiums&#8221; in the currency of legal tender in Argentina, which is the peso, restricts the distribution of retained earnings. According to the Company&#8217;s shareholders&#8217; equity in its functional currency, the restricted balance of retained earnings amounts to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:RestrictedDistributionOfRetainedEarnings" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120259">70</ix:nonFraction>, 70 and 68 as of December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively, of which <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:DistributableRetainedEarningsSubjectToRestrictionAcquisitionCostOfTreasuryShares" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120260">28</ix:nonFraction>, 30 and 30 correspond to the balance of &#8220;Acquisition cost of treasury shares&#8221; account and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:DistributableRetainedEarningsSubjectToRestrictionBalanceOfSharePremiumAccount" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120261">42</ix:nonFraction>, 40 and 38 to the balance of &#8220;Share trading premiums&#8221; account, as of December&#160;31, 2024, 2023 and 2022, respectively. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">When the net balance of retained earnings at the end of a fiscal year is positive, it can be distributed upon the decision of the Shareholders&#8217; meeting, while not subject to legal restrictions. Additionally, pursuant to the CNV rules, when the net balance of &#8220;Other comprehensive income&#8221; account in the currency of legal tender in Argentina, which is the peso, is positive, it will not be distributed nor capitalized nor used to compensate accumulated losses, but will be computed as part of retained earnings in order to make comparisons to determine the situation of the Company in relation to Articles 31, 32 and 206 of the LGS, or other legal or regulatory rules making reference to limits or ratios with capital and reserves, not specifically and expressly provided for under the CNV rules. When the net balance of &#8220;Other comprehensive income&#8221; account at the end of a fiscal year is negative, a restriction on the distribution of retained earnings for the same amount will be imposed. </div></ix:nonNumeric></div></div><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES </div></div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.a) Legal proceedings </div></div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.a.1) Introduction </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">At the time of its acquisition by YPF in 1995, Maxus Energy Corporation (&#8220;Maxus&#8221;) and certain of its subsidiaries (including Tierra Solutions, Inc. (&#8220;TS&#8221;), Maxus International Energy Company (&#8220;MIEC&#8221;), Maxus (US) Exploration Company (&#8220;MUSE&#8221;) and Gateway Coal Company (&#8220;Gateway&#8221;) and together with Maxus, TS, MIEC and MUSE, the &#8220;Maxus Entities&#8221;), would have certain liabilities related to former operations of a previous Maxus subsidiary, Diamond Shamrock Chemicals Company (&#8220;Chemicals&#8221;). In 1986, Maxus sold Chemicals to Occidental Chemical Corporation (&#8220;Occidental&#8221;), and in connection with that sale agreed to indemnify Chemicals and Occidental from and against certain liabilities relating to the business or activities of Chemicals prior to September&#160;4, 1986, including environmental liabilities relating to chemical plants and waste disposal sites used by Chemicals prior to that date. Mainly as a result of such indemnity obligation, the Maxus Entities have been involved in various administrative and judicial proceedings of an environmental and contractual nature in the United States, as described in Note 33.a.2). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In June 2016, each of the Maxus Entities filed a voluntary petition under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code of the United States (&#8220;United States Bankruptcy Code&#8221;) with the United States Bankruptcy Court of the District of Delaware (&#8220;Bankruptcy Court&#8221;), which had the effect of staying the cross-claims described in Note 33.a.2.ii). In December 2016, as part of their reorganization process, the Maxus Entities, in their capacity as debtors, filed their proposed plan of liquidation (&#8220;Liquidation Plan&#8221;) in accordance with the United States Bankruptcy Code. In March 2017, the Maxus Entities and the creditors committee of the Maxus Entities (&#8220;Creditors Committee&#8221;) filed their alternative proposed plan of liquidation (&#8220;Alternative Plan&#8221;) under the United States Bankruptcy Code, which contemplated, among other matters, the creation of a liquidating trust (&#8220;Liquidating Trust&#8221;) and the cancellation of the equity participations of YPF Holdings and YCLH Holdings, Inc (&#8220;YCLH Holdings&#8221;, formerly CLH Holdings, Inc.) in the Maxus Entities. The Bankruptcy Court approved the Alternative Plan in May 2017, which was confirmed and became effective in July 2017. </div></ix:nonNumeric></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136337959" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_1"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_2"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_3"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_4"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_4" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_5"><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><ix:exclude>(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated)</ix:exclude> </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>33. ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In June 2018, the Liquidating Trust filed a lawsuit with the Bankruptcy Court against YPF, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings and YPF International (collectively, the &#8220;YPF Defendants&#8221;), as well as other entities not related to the YPF Defendants, claiming alleged damages in an amount up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:LossContingencyEstimateOfClaimingAllegedDamagesAmount" contextRef="PAsOn06_30_2018" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120276">14,000</ix:nonFraction>, on the basis of allegations of fraudulent transfers and alter ego liability of the YPF Defendants in connection with corporate restructuring transactions of the Maxus Entities. Throughout the 1990s and 2000s decades, certain restructuring transactions were carried out in respect of the international operations of the Group, including certain operations by the companies that made up the Maxus Entities&#8217; group, which were carried out in the ordinary course of business with the legitimate objective of achieving greater efficiencies in the management of such international operations. For its part, the Liquidating Trust alleged that (i)&#160;these restructuring transactions constitute fraudulent transfers for which the YPF Defendants are liable, and (ii)&#160;the YPF Defendants are an alter ego of the Maxus Entities and are responsible for all of their liabilities, including the environmental liabilities described in Note 33.a.2.i). The YPF Defendants rejected these allegations made by the Liquidating Trust for considering them without merit and obtained a partial summary judgment decision from the Bankruptcy Court in their favor, rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory (liability for all liabilities and contingencies of the Maxus Entities) proposed by the Liquidating Trust related to the alleged alter ego damages, as described in Note 33.a.4). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;6, 2023, the YPF Defendants, the Liquidating Trust and other companies not related to the YPF Defendants (Repsol, S.A., Repsol Exploraci&#243;n, S.A., Repsol USA Holdings LLC, Repsol E&amp;P USA LLC, Repsol Offshore E&amp;P USA, Inc., Perenco Trinidad&#160;&amp; Tobago (Holdings) ETVE SLU (f/k/a Repsol E&amp;P T&amp;T Limited), and Repsol Services Co. (collectively, the &#8220;Repsol Defendants&#8221;) signed, among other documents, a settlement and release agreement (&#8220;Trust Settlement Agreement&#8221;) providing for a full release and discharge of all claims in exchange for payment of a settlement amount, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain conditions, including court approvals and other procedural events, as described in Note 33.a.4). </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.a.2) Background to the Reorganization Process of the Maxus Entities under the United States Bankruptcy Code </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Following the petition filed by the Maxus Entities with the Bankruptcy Court under the United States Bankruptcy Code in June 2016, the Company only has access to information regarding administrative and judicial proceedings against the Maxus Entities that is published by the competent authorities and/or that is publicly filed by the parties involved in such proceedings, including information published by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (&#8220;EPA&#8221;). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The development of these administrative and judicial proceedings was relevant to the Company in light of the Liquidating Trust&#8217;s request to the Bankruptcy Court that the YPF Defendants be found liable for all liabilities and contingencies of the Maxus Entities, including those that might eventually arise in the future as a result of such proceedings (&#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory). However, as described in Note 33.a.4), on June&#160;22, 2022, the Bankruptcy Court granted partial summary judgment in favor of the YPF Defendants, rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory (liability for all liabilities and contingencies of the Maxus Entities) proposed by the Liquidating Trust relating to the alleged alter ego damages. In rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory, the Bankruptcy Court agreed with the YPF Defendants that the alleged alter ego damages required evidence of causation and, therefore, the Liquidating Trust would have to prove that the claimed damages were caused by the alleged alter ego conduct. Moreover, as described in Note 33.a.4), the case brought by the Liquidating Trust has been dismissed. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_5" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_6"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_6" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_7"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_7" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_8"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_8" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_9"><ix:exclude>

ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.a.2.i) Environmental administrative matters </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 1986 at the time of the sale of Chemicals to Occidental, TS (formerly Chemical Land Holdings, Inc.) owned a chemical plant located on Lister Avenue in Newark, New Jersey, on the banks of the Passaic River. The plant allegedly discharged chemicals that contaminated the area surrounding the plant (&#8220;Lister Site&#8221;), the Passaic River and Newark Bay. After the sale and up to the date the Maxus Entities filed the petition for reorganization with the Bankruptcy Court in June 2016, the plant in the Lister Site continued to be owned by TS. Occidental alleged that under the sale agreement, Maxus made itself liable to indemnify Occidental for all environmental liabilities related to the Lister Site, the Passaic River and the Newark Bay that may be Chemicals&#180; or Occidental&#180;s responsibility. Throughout the 1990s and subsequently, the EPA, the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (&#8220;Department of Environmental Protection&#8221; or &#8220;DEP&#8221;), and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (&#8220;NOAA&#8221;) initiated several administrative proceedings against Occidental, the Maxus Entities, and various other entities in connection with the study and remediation of environmental liabilities located at the Lister Site, the Passaic River, and Newark Bay, which gave rise to, among others, those mentioned below: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

The defendants made responsive pleadings and filings. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2008, Occidental filed cross-claims before the New Jersey Court alleging that under Chemicals&#8217; sale agreement, Maxus would be liable to indemnify Occidental for the damages that the DEP claimed from Occidental, and that YPF, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings and Repsol (later adding YPF International) were also liable for such damages as they had received fraudulent transfers from Maxus and/or were Maxus&#8217; alter ego. The defendants rejected these allegations and asserted appropriate defenses. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2013, the DEP entered into a proposed settlement agreement with YPF, YPF Holdings, YPF International, YCLH Holdings, Maxus and TS (&#8220;Settlement Agreement&#8221;). The Settlement Agreement, which did not imply endorsement of facts or rights and presented only for conciliatory purposes, was subject to an approval process, publication, comment period and approval by the New Jersey Court. According to the terms of the Settlement Agreement, the DEP would agree to release certain claims related to environmental liabilities within a geographic area of the Passaic River initiated against YPF, YPF International, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings, Maxus and TS, recognizing a limited liability of up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:MaximumLitigationALimitedLiability" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2013_SettllementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120279">400</ix:nonFraction> collectively, for these and other participants in the litigation if they were found responsible. margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Simultaneously, Repsol reached a settlement agreement with the DEP, agreeing to pay <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PaymentOfLitigationSettlement" contextRef="P02_10_2014To02_10_2014_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis_NewJerseyCourtApprovedTheSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120281">65</ix:nonFraction> (subject to the same <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PaymentOfLitigationSettlement" contextRef="P12_31_2013To12_31_2013_NewJerseyCourtApprovedTheSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120282">400</ix:nonFraction> limitation described above). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, on December&#160;16, 2014, the New Jersey Court approved a settlement agreement whereby the DEP agreed to settle all claims against Occidental related to the environmental liabilities within a specific geographical area of the Passaic River, in consideration for the payment of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:LitigationSettlementClaimAmount" contextRef="P12_16_2014To12_16_2014_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis_SettllementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120286">190</ix:nonFraction> and a sum amounting up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PaymentAndSettlementOfEnvironmentalLiabilities" contextRef="P12_16_2014To12_16_2014_SettllementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120287">400</ix:nonFraction> to reimburse the State of New Jersey in the event it is required to pay a percentage of the costs for future remedial actions in accordance with the United States Federal Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Following the signing of the aforementioned settlement agreements, the cross-claims between the defendants (Occidental, Maxus, TS, YPF, YPF International, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings and Repsol) remained pending resolution by the New Jersey Court. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">However, such cross-claims were stayed as of June&#160;17, 2016, when Maxus, TS, and other affiliated companies each filed a voluntary petition under Chapter 11 with the Bankruptcy Court, as described in Note 33.a.3). On June&#160;28, 2016, at Occidental&#8217;s request, the New Jersey Court transferred all remaining claims in the Passaic River litigation from the New Jersey Court to the Bankruptcy Court. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;2, 2023, a stipulation of dismissal of all claims was filed in the New Jersey Court, effectuating the immediate dismissal with prejudice of the action as of that same date. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.a.3) Reorganization Process under Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;17, 2016, each of the Maxus Entities filed a voluntary petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code with the United States Bankruptcy Court. In this context, the Maxus Entities entered into an agreement (&#8220;2016 Agreement&#8221;) with YPF, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings, YPF International and YPF Services USA Corp (&#8220;YPF Services&#8221;) (together, the &#8220;YPF Entities&#8221;), to settle all of the Maxus Entities&#8217; claims against the YPF Entities, including any alter ego claims, all of which, in the YPF Entities&#8217; opinion, had no merit. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The 2016 Agreement provided for: (i)&#160;the granting of a year-long loan by YPF Holdings for an amount of up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:LoanPayableToRelatedPartiesFaceValue" contextRef="PAsOn06_17_2016_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis_YPFHoldingsMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120288">63.1</ix:nonFraction> (&#8220;DIP Loan&#8221;) to finance the Maxus Entities&#8217; activities during a bankruptcy case; and (ii)&#160;a payment of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SettlementPayment" contextRef="P06_17_2016To06_17_2016_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120289">130</ix:nonFraction> to the Maxus Entities (&#8220;Settlement Payment&#8221;) for a release of all claims that the Maxus Entities might have against the YPF Entities. </div><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfSettlementPaymentSubjectToDebtorsAgreement" contextRef="P12_29_2016To12_29_2016_ChapterElevenPlanOfLiquidationMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" id="ixv-76112"><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;29, 2016, the Maxus Entities filed with the Bankruptcy Court their proposed Liquidation Plan under the United States Bankruptcy Code. The Liquidation Plan foresaw a <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SettlementPayment" contextRef="P12_29_2016To12_29_2016_ChapterElevenPlanOfLiquidationMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120290">130</ix:nonFraction> Settlement Payment under the 2016 Agreement and provided that, if the 2016 Agreement was approved, portions of the <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SettlementPayment" contextRef="P12_29_2016To12_29_2016_ChapterElevenPlanOfLiquidationMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120291">130</ix:nonFraction> Settlement Payment would be deposited into (i)&#160;a liquidating trust for distribution to creditors and (ii)&#160;an environmental response trust for use in remediation. Moreover, if the Liquidation Plan were approved, the 2016 Agreement with the Maxus Entities would likely be confirmed and the claims against the YPF Entities, including the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">alter-ego</div> claims, would be settled and released in exchange for the <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SettlementPayment" contextRef="P12_29_2016To12_29_2016_ChapterElevenPlanOfLiquidationMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120292">130</ix:nonFraction> Settlement Payment. </div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Liquidation Plan, however, provided for certain contingencies should the Bankruptcy Court not approve the 2016 Agreement. In that scenario, the Maxus Entities&#8217; claims against YPF Entities, including the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">alter-ego</div> claims, would be transferred into a liquidating trust. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;28, 2017, the Maxus Entities and the Creditors Committee submitted the Alternative Plan, which did not include the 2016 Agreement with the YPF Entities. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under the Alternative Plan, the Liquidating Trust could pursue alter ego claims and any other claim belonging to the insolvent&#8217;s estate against the YPF Entities. The Liquidating Trust would be financed by Occidental in its capacity as creditor of the Maxus Entities. As such, the Alternative Plan did not contemplate the implementation of the originally submitted 2016 Agreement, and on April&#160;10, 2017, YPF Holdings gave notice that this situation constituted an event of default under the DIP Loan. By the approval of the financing offered by Occidental under the Alternative Plan, the Bankruptcy Court ordered the return of the outstanding amounts (<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ReturnOfOutstandingAmounts" contextRef="P06_17_2016To06_17_2016_DebtorInPossessionLoanMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis_YPFHoldingsMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120293">12</ix:nonFraction>)&#160;under the terms of the DIP Loan, which were subsequently returned to YPF Holdings. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_15" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_16"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_16" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_17"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_17" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_18"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_18" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_19"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_19" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_20"><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><ix:exclude>(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated)</ix:exclude> </div></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_20" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_21"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33. ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.) </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_21" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_22"><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May&#160;22, 2017, the Bankruptcy Court issued an order confirming the Alternative Plan submitted by the Creditors Committee and the Maxus Entities, which became effective as of July&#160;14, 2017. Through the Alternative Plan the Liquidating Trust was created, which brought in 2018 the complaint referred to in Note 33.a.4) hereafter. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.a.4) Claim of the Liquidating Trust </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;14, 2018, the Liquidating Trust filed a lawsuit against the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants before the Bankruptcy Court, claiming alleged damages of up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ClaimAllegedDamages" contextRef="PAsOn06_14_2018_MaxusEnergyCorporationLiquidatingTrustMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120295">14,000</ix:nonFraction>, on the basis of allegations of fraudulent transfers and liability as the Maxus Entities&#8217; alter ego (&#8220;Liquidating Trust&#8217;s Claim&#8221;). As described above, throughout the 1990s and 2000s decades, several restructuring operations were carried out in respect of the international operations of the Group, including operations of companies that made up the Maxus Entities&#8217; group, which were carried out in the ordinary course of business with the legitimate objective of achieving greater efficiencies in the management of the Group&#8217;s international operations. For its part, as against the YPF Defendants, the Liquidating Trust alleged that (i)&#160;these restructuring transactions constituted fraudulent transfers for which the YPF Defendants were liable and (ii)&#160;the YPF Defendants were an alter ego of the Maxus Entities and were responsible for all of the Maxus Entities&#8217; liabilities, including the environmental liabilities described in Note 33.a.2.i). The YPF Defendants rejected such allegations and filed a motion to dismiss the Liquidating Trust&#8217;s Claim (&#8220;Motion to Dismiss&#8221;). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Between October&#160;19, 2018 and January&#160;22, 2019, several procedural actions were completed in connection with the Motion to Dismiss. Similarly, during that period, the Repsol Defendants also filed a motion requesting that the Bankruptcy Court dismiss the Liquidating Trust&#8217;s Claim. On February&#160;15, 2019, the Bankruptcy Court denied both motions. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;1, 2019, the YPF Defendants sought leave to appeal the order dated February&#160;15, 2019, rejecting the Motion to Dismiss. The appeal was denied by the Delaware District Court on September&#160;12, 2019, and the parties proceeded to the discovery process. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">While the aforementioned appeal was still being considered, on April&#160;1, 2019, the YPF Defendants on one hand, and the Repsol Defendants, on the other hand, answered the complaint initiated by the Liquidating Trust. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Within the framework of the Liquidating Trust&#8217;s Claim, during 2019 and 2020 court activity focused on (i)&#160;the filing of motions to withdraw the reference, the purpose of which was to have a matter transferred to district court of the respective district rather than a bankruptcy court, (ii)&#160;the discovery process, (iii)&#160;the filing of a motion to disqualify against the attorneys of the Liquidating Trust, and (iv)&#160;the definition of procedural stages. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;23, 2020, the District Court for the District of Delaware rejected the motions to withdraw the reference raised by the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants as premature. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With regard to the discovery process, the judicial activity mainly included proceedings related to the definition of the documentary and testimonial evidence to be produced in the process. The fact discovery process substantially concluded on October&#160;21, 2021, and the expert discovery process concluded on April&#160;8, 2022. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With regard to the motion to disqualify the attorneys of the Liquidating Trust, on December&#160;19, 2020, the YPF Defendants filed a Motion to Disqualify White&#160;&amp; Case LLP as legal representatives of the Liquidating Trust based on the Company&#8217;s understanding that such law firm might be prevented from acting in such capacity by virtue of conflicts of interest arising from the incorporation to the firm of <div style="white-space: nowrap;
