ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;16, 2022, the Liquidating Trust filed a motion for partial summary judgment on certain of its claims against the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants. That motion did not request the entry of a monetary judgment at that time, acknowledging that certain issues should be resolved at trial. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;27, 2022, the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants filed their motions for summary judgment as well as their respective oppositions to the motion for summary judgment filed by the Liquidating Trust. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;13, 2022, a hearing was held before the Bankruptcy Court for the presentation of the oral arguments related to motions for summary judgment. On June&#160;22, 2022, the Bankruptcy Court rejected the motion for summary judgment filed by the Liquidating Trust stating, among other considerations, that there were relevant matters of fact in dispute that had to be settled at the trial stage. The Bankruptcy Court also partially granted summary judgment in favor of the YPF Defendants rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory (responsibility for all Maxus Entities&#8217; liabilities and contingencies) proposed by the Liquidating Trust in relation to the claimed alter ego damages. In rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory proposed by the Liquidating Trust, the Bankruptcy Court concurred with the YPF Defendants that the damages claimed by alter ego require evidence of causality, and, therefore, the Liquidating Trust would have to prove that the damages claimed were caused by the purported alter ego behavior. The Bankruptcy Court also stated that the liability for the alleged alter ego behavior of the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants is an issue that would have to be first settled at the trial stage before the amount of damages, if any, can be analyzed. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On September&#160;30, 2022, the Bankruptcy Court confirmed the dates proposed by the parties for trial during the months of March and April 2023. On January&#160;3, 2023, the parties jointly requested a stay of all deadlines and suspension of trial dates, with new trial dates to be held for the period between June&#160;19, 2023, and July&#160;31, 2023. The Bankruptcy Court granted the request that same day. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As mentioned in Note 33.a.1), on April&#160;6, 2023, the YPF Defendants, the Repsol Defendants and the Liquidating Trust signed the Trust Settlement Agreement. Pursuant to the Trust Settlement Agreement, the Liquidating Trust agreed to dismiss with prejudice all of the actions brought against the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants and to provide a full release and discharge of all claims, in exchange for the payment of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:AggregateClaims" contextRef="PAsOn04_06_2023_TrustSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_YPFAndRepsolDefendandsMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120298">575</ix:nonFraction>, of which the YPF Defendants agreed to pay <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ShorttermLegalProceedingsProvision" contextRef="PAsOn05_01_2023_TrustSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_YPFAndRepsolDefendandsMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120299">287.5</ix:nonFraction> (less certain deductions), plus interest accruing from May&#160;1, 2023 until the date of payment. The civil action pending before the New Jersey state court against the YPF Defendants (see Note 33.a.2.ii)) was also included in the dismissals and releases described above. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition to the Trust Settlement Agreement, the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants signed a settlement and release agreement (&#8220;Oxy Settlement Agreement&#8221;) with Occidental and various other Occidental entities, including Occidental Petroleum Corporation and Occidental Chemical Holding Corporation (together, the &#8220;Oxy Parties&#8221;). Pursuant to the Oxy Settlement Agreement, which did not require any payment in addition to the amounts covered by the Trust Settlement Agreement given the benefits to the Oxy Parties under that agreement, the Oxy Parties agreed to release all claims they may possess against the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants relating to the Maxus Entities, the Passaic River and other areas subject to environmental remediation. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants also entered into a settlement and covenant not to sue agreement (&#8220;Government Agreement&#8221;) with various U.S. governmental entities, including the U.S. Department of Justice (on behalf of the EPA, the Department of Interior, and the NOAA) and the States of Ohio and Wisconsin (&#8220;Governmental Parties&#8221;). The Governmental Parties have covenanted not to sue the YPF Defendants or the Repsol Defendants with respect to claims similar to those the Liquidating Trust has asserted, as well as certain claims under the U.S. Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (&#8220;CERCLA&#8221;). Given the benefits to the Governmental Parties under the Trust Settlement Agreement, the Government Agreement also did not require any payment in addition to the amounts covered by the Trust Settlement Agreement. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_27" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_28"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_28" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_29"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_29" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_30"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_30" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_31"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337959_31"><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL"><ix:exclude>(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated)</ix:exclude> </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>33. ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As noted above, the YPF Defendants&#8217; payment to the Liquidating Trust, and the dismissal and release of actions and claims against the YPF Defendants under the aforementioned agreements, were subject to a number of conditions and procedural steps, including obtaining a final court order approving the Trust Settlement Agreement and a final court order approving the Government Agreement. On August&#160;2, 2023, following satisfaction of all conditions and procedural steps, the YPF Defendants made payment under the Trust Settlement Agreement and the dismissals and releases described above became effective as to the YPF Defendants, including dismissal of all relevant state and federal actions against the YPF Defendants. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.b) Accounting matters </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In connection with the petition filed with the Bankruptcy Court under the United States Bankruptcy Code by the Maxus Entities on June&#160;17, 2016, as described in Note 33.a.2), the Company considered this an event that required reconsideration of whether the consolidation of the Maxus Entities remained appropriate. In order to carry out this analysis, the Company followed the guidelines established in IFRS 10 to reassess whether it maintained control over the activities of the Maxus Entities. This analysis, in accordance with IAS 8, was complemented by the criteria set forth in the United States Standard ASC 810 published by the FASB, the principles of which are consistent with IFRS 10, but addresses in more detail the issues related to the consolidation of entities that file a reorganization proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Generally, when an entity files a reorganization petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code, shareholders do not maintain the ability to exercise the power to make decisions that have a significant impact on the economic performance of the business of entities because that power is usually subject to Bankruptcy Court approval. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The petition filed by the Maxus Entities under the United States Bankruptcy Code had relevant effects on the rights of YPF Holdings as a shareholder of these entities, because creditors of the bankruptcy process (the &#8220;Creditors&#8221;) replaced the shareholders in their legal capacity to file derivative suits against the directors on behalf of the Maxus Entities for breach of the Debtors&#8217; fiduciary obligations, since the Creditors would be the main beneficiaries in any increase in value of these entities. However, at the time of the voluntary filing of the reorganization petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code, it should be noted that YPF Holdings retained its right to designate directors of the Maxus Entities through shareholders&#8217; meetings, unless the Bankruptcy Court ordered otherwise. In addition, the bankruptcy cases filed with the Bankruptcy Court also affected the responsibilities and functions of the board of directors and management of each of the respective Maxus Entities. Each of the Maxus Entities had become a &#8220;debtor in possession&#8221; and, in accordance with the United States Bankruptcy Code, remained in possession of its property and, subject to certain limitations, was authorized to carry out its normal operations, unless the Bankruptcy Court ordered otherwise. Even so, during the United States Bankruptcy Code&#8217;s cases, the directors of the Maxus Entities do not have absolute discretion, since any decision outside the ordinary course of business of the Maxus Entities will be subject to the approval of the Bankruptcy Court. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Likewise, on November&#160;8, 2016, the Maxus Entities amended their <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">by-laws</div> in order to give greater discretion to the independent directors. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, the Alternative Plan approved by the Bankruptcy Court was confirmed and became effective in July 2017, pursuant to which the equity participations of YPF Holdings and YCLH Holdings in the Maxus Entities were cancelled, and, accordingly, these companies ceased having any participation in the Maxus Entities. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In view of the foregoing, the Company understands that it is no longer able to influence the Maxus Entities&#8217; operations and results, a necessary condition established by IFRS 10 to establish the existence of an effective financial control and therefore, on June&#160;17, 2016, it proceeded to deconsolidate the investments of the Maxus Entities. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group has the following contingencies and claims, individually significant, which in the opinion of the Company and its external counsels, have a possible outcome. In this sense, and based on the information available to the Group, including the amount of time remaining before conclusion of pending lawsuits, the results of evidence discovery and the assessment of internal and external advisors, the Group is unable to estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of loss in relation to certain matters described in Note 34.b). </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">34.a) Contingent assets </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group has no significant contingent assets. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">34.b) Contingent liabilities </div></div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">34.b.1) Environmental claims </div></div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Asociaci&#243;n Superficiarios de la Patagonia (&#8220;ASSUPA&#8221;) </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">ASSUPA sued the companies operating exploitation concessions and exploration permits in the different basins (Neuquina basin in 2003, Northwest basin in 2010, and Austral basin in 2012), YPF among them, claiming the remediation of the general environmental damage purportedly caused by hydrocarbon activities. In addition, it requested the establishment of an environmental restoration fund, and the implementation of measures to prevent environmental damages in the future. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Concessionary companies in the Neuquina basin areas </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The claim was answered by YPF and the rest of the sued parties. Following several proceedings, on December&#160;30, 2014, the CSJN issued <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:NumberOfInterlocutoryJudgments" contextRef="P12_30_2014To12_30_2014_AsociacionSuperficiariosDeLaPatagoniaMemberYPFLegalEntitiesAxis_CsjnMemberifrsfullClassesOfProvisionsAxis" unitRef="Unit_Judgment" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120302">2</ix:nonFraction> interlocutory judgments. The first judgment declared that all environmental damages related to local and provincial situations were outside the scope of its original competence, and that only inter-jurisdictional situations (such as the Colorado River basin) would fall under its venue. In the second judgment, the CSJN rejected the petition filed by ASSUPA to incorporate Repsol S.A. and the directors who carried their activities in YPF until April 2012 as a necessary third party. The CSJN also rejected precautionary measures and other proceedings related to such request. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As a result of such decision, an individual filed a preventive damage action to reduce presumed damages and prevent future damages (action for repair of damages) consisting of the comprehensive remediation of collective damages allegedly caused by the hydrocarbon activity undertaken by YPF in the Province of Neuqu&#233;n. In such action, YPF answered the claim and requested that the National Government, the Provincial Government and other oil companies in the area be summoned to appear. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Concessionary companies in the Northwest basin areas </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;1, 2014, YPF was notified of the complaint and moved for the suspension of procedural deadlines due to notification defects, which motion was granted by the court. On April&#160;19, 2017, YPF was notified of the court order resuming procedural deadlines and timely filed a challenge for legal defect, together with other the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">co-defendants.</div> The court ordered those terms to answer the complaint be stayed until a final order is rendered on the defense based on a legal defect. As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the procedural deadlines are suspended until the digitization of the proceedings. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Concessionary companies in the Austral basin areas </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On November&#160;2, 2015, YPF was notified of the claim and requested the suspension of procedural deadlines due to notification defects. This suspension was granted by the court and following several incidents with different codefendants and parties summoned to appear. On June&#160;23, 2020, the judge ordered a new notification with the transfer of the case. The decision was appealed by the plaintiff. </div></ix:nonNumeric></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136337029" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_1"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_2"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_3"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_4"><ix:exclude>

CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May&#160;12, 2021, the case was submitted to the Federal Contentious Administrative Court of Appeals to decide on the plaintiff&#8217;s appeal on the interlocutory judgment, in which the judge decided to sustain the claim filed by YPF, among other <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">co-defendants,</div> ordering the transfer of the case. <td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Dock Sud, R&#237;o Matanza, Riachuelo, Quilmes and Refiner&#237;a Luj&#225;n de Cuyo </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2006, a group of neighbors of Dock Sud, Province of Buenos Aires, sued 44 companies, including YPF, the Argentine Government, the Province of Buenos Aires, the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires and 14 municipalities, before the CSJN, seeking remediation and indemnification for environmental collective damages to the Matanza and Riachuelo rivers. Additionally, another group of neighbors of the Dock Sud area, filed 2 additional environmental claims, one of which was desisted in relation to YPF, while the other claim seeks remediation and indemnification for collective environmental damages to the Dock Sud area and individual property damages allegedly suffered by several companies located in that area, including YPF, the Province of Buenos Aires and several municipalities. Currently, it is not possible to reasonably estimate the outcome of these complaints, nor is it possible to estimate the resulting associated legal fees and expenses. YPF has the right to be indemnified and held harmless by the Argentine Government for events and claims prior to January&#160;1, 1991, in accordance with YPF Privatization Law. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Through its judgment dated July&#160;8, 2008, the CSJN: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Determined that the Authority of the Matanza Riachuelo Basin (&#8220;ACUMAR&#8221;) (Law No.&#160;26,168) should be in charge of executing the program for environmental remediation of the basin, being the Argentine Government, the Province of Buenos Aires and the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires responsible for its performance; delegated to the Federal Lower Court of Quilmes the knowledge of all the matters concerning the execution of the remediation and sanitation; declared that all the litigations related to the execution of the remediation plan will be accumulated and be processed by this court and that this process produces lis pendens relating to the other collective actions seeking the environmental remediation of the basin, which should be archived. YPF was notified of certain resolutions issued by ACUMAR, whereby the Company was required to present an industrial reconversion plan in connection with certain YPF installations. Despite the appeal by the Company of the aforementioned resolutions, the plan was still presented. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Decided that the proceedings to determine liabilities arising from past behaviors to repair the collective environmental damage would continue being heard by CSJN. </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On October&#160;22, 2024, the CSJN issued a final judgement whereby: (i)&#160;it terminated the CSJN&#8217;s supervision of compliance with the judgement of July&#160;8, 2008; (ii) it terminated the case for the remediation of the collective environmental damage without sentencing any of the 44 defendant companies; (iii)&#160;it imposed the costs in the order incurred; and (iv)&#160;it decided that the litigation related to the execution of the remediation plan will continue to be processed before the corresponding court. YPF is not a party to such litigation. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition to the aforementioned in Note 17.a.4) related to environmental claims in Quilmes, the Company has other judicial and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-judicial</div> claims against it, based on similar arguments. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On the other hand, the monitoring activities carried out routinely by YPF have allowed to detect a certain degree of environmental impact on the subsoil within the vicinity of the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery, which led to the implementation of a program for the survey, assessment and remediation of environmental damages, agreed by the Company with the enforcement agencies of the Province of Mendoza, which costs have been recognized in the &#8220;Provision for environmental liabilities&#8221; account of the &#8220;Provisions&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding the environmental damage to the aquifer surrounding the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery, a detailed research plan was conducted in order to define, analyze risks and implement mitigating actions. Thereafter, a remediation engineering plan was developed which is currently being implemented. Remediation <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">follow-up</div> is carried out under the supervision and with the assistance of Instituto Nacional del Agua (&#8220;INA&#8221;) and local authorities. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_5" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_6"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_6" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_7"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_7" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_8"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_8" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_9"><ix:exclude>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Petersen Energ&#237;a Inversora, S.A.U. and Petersen Energ&#237;a, S.A.U. (collectively, &#8220;Petersen&#8221;) - Eton Park Capital Management, L.P., Eton Park Master Fund, LTD. and Eton Park Fund, L.P. (collectively, &#8220;Eton Park&#8221;, and together with Petersen, the &#8220;Plaintiffs&#8221;) </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Plaintiffs in these proceedings are Petersen and Eton Park, both of which previously held American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) evidencing American Depositary Shares (ADSs) representing YPF Class&#160;D shares. Petersen filed its complaint on April&#160;8, 2015 and Eton Park filed its complaint on November&#160;3, 2016. Both complaints were filed before the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York (&#8220;District Court&#8221;), and against the Republic of Argentina (&#8220;Republic&#8221;) and YPF. The complaints make allegations related to the Republic&#8217;s intervention in YPF in 2012 and the Republic&#8217;s subsequent expropriation of a controlling interest in YPF held by Repsol (see Note 31). Petersen and Eton Park allege that the Republic and YPF breached purported obligations contained in the Company&#8217;s bylaws. The Petersen case and the Eton Park case were deemed to be related cases, are being conducted jointly and were assigned to the same District Court. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On September&#160;8, 2015, before Eton Park had filed its complaint, the Republic and YPF filed motions to dismiss Petersen&#8217;s claims. On October&#160;19, 2015 and October&#160;23, 2015, Petersen filed oppositions to the Republic&#8217;s and YPF&#8217;s motions to dismiss, respectively. On September&#160;9, 2016, the District Court issued a decision partially denying the motions to dismiss. The Company and the Republic appealed this decision, requesting a complete dismissal of the complaint. The Company and the Republic argued that the case should proceed in Argentina, if at all (forum non conveniens). The United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit (&#8220;Court of Appeals&#8221;) held that the District Court had jurisdiction over this matter. On October&#160;31, 2018, the Company and the Republic appealed this decision to the United States Supreme Court (&#8220;Supreme Court&#8221;). On June&#160;24, 2019, the Supreme Court declined to hear the appeal. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;30, 2019, the Republic and YPF filed motions to dismiss both the Petersen and the Eton Park cases, once again arguing that the cases should proceed in Argentina (forum non conveniens). On June&#160;5, 2020, the District Court denied these motions to dismiss. The Republic and YPF filed their answers to the Petersen complaint on July&#160;8, 2019 and to the Eton Park complaint on July&#160;10, 2020. On July&#160;13, 2020, the District Court issued an order requiring the parties to proceed with fact and expert discovery. Given the overlap between the Petersen and Eton Park cases, they moved forward jointly and the parties proceeded with consolidated discovery in both cases. Fact discovery concluded on August&#160;27, 2021. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Expert discovery concluded on April&#160;6, 2022. On April&#160;14, 2022, Petersen and Eton Park (&#8220;Plaintiffs&#8221;) and YPF and the Republic (&#8220;Defendants&#8221;) filed opening briefs in support of cross-motions for summary judgment in the Petersen and Eton Park actions. Plaintiffs argued that the District Court should grant summary judgment in their favor on liability and damages as to both YPF and the Republic. In their opening briefs, YPF and the Republic each argued that it has no liability and owes no damages to Plaintiffs, and that the District Court should, therefore, grant summary judgment in its favor and dismiss all remaining claims against it. The parties filed opposition and reply briefs on May&#160;26, 2022 and June&#160;23, 2022, respectively. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;30, 2023, the District Court granted YPF&#8217;s motion for summary judgment and denied Plaintiffs&#8217; motion for summary judgment as to YPF in its entirety. The District Court found that YPF has <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ContractualLiabilityPayableValue" contextRef="PAsOn03_30_2023_PetersonAndEtonParkAndYpfAndTheRepublicMemberYPFCaseDetailsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" id="ixv-120307">no</ix:nonFraction> contractual liability and owes <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:DirectDamagesPayableForBreachOfContract" contextRef="PAsOn03_30_2023_PetersonAndEtonParkAndYpfAndTheRepublicMemberYPFCaseDetailsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" id="ixv-120308">no</ix:nonFraction> damages for breach of contract to Plaintiffs and accordingly dismissed Plaintiffs&#8217; claims against YPF. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In line with the decision issued on March&#160;30, 2023, in the final judgment issued on September&#160;15, 2023 the District Court ordered, adjudged and decreed that all of Plaintiffs&#8217; claims against YPF were dismissed, decreeing that YPF has <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ContractualLiabilityPayableValue" contextRef="PAsOn03_30_2023_PetersonAndEtonParkAndYpfAndTheRepublicMemberYPFCaseDetailsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" id="ixv-120309">no</ix:nonFraction> contractual liability and owes <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:DirectDamagesPayableForBreachOfContract" contextRef="PAsOn03_30_2023_PetersonAndEtonParkAndYpfAndTheRepublicMemberYPFCaseDetailsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" id="ixv-120310">no</ix:nonFraction> damages for breach of contract to Plaintiffs. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_10" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136337029_11"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On October&#160;18, 2023, Plaintiffs appealed the District Court&#8217;s final judgment as to YPF and those orders that, for purposes of appeal, merge into the designated final judgment. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On October&#160;23, 2023, YPF filed a notice of conditional cross-cross-appeal. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The appeals filed by the parties in these proceedings were fully briefed as of September&#160;6, 2024. The Second Circuit Court of Appeals will set a date for oral argument. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;1, 2024, Plaintiffs filed a turnover motion, which became public (and accessible to YPF) on April&#160;22, 2024. This motion requests that the District Court order the Republic to turn over the YPF Class&#160;D shares held by the Republic to Plaintiffs in partial satisfaction of the District Court&#8217;s judgment against the Republic in this proceeding. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Plaintiffs and the Republic completed their briefing on the turnover motion on July&#160;8, 2024. The District Court may, but is not required to, hold oral argument prior to rendering a decision on the turnover motion. Furthermore, the District Court&#8217;s decision on the turnover motion may be appealed by Plaintiffs or the Republic in accordance with applicable procedural rules. YPF is not a party to the turnover motion. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Plaintiffs are also seeking discovery of documents from YPF related to their theory that YPF could be an alter ego of the Republic. YPF denies that it is an alter ego and objected to Plaintiffs&#8217; document requests. On May&#160;28, 2024, the District Court ordered YPF to produce documents in response to Plaintiffs&#8217; discovery requests. As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, Plaintiffs have not requested that the District Court find that YPF is an alter ego of the Republic, and the District Court&#8217;s order on discovery is not a ruling accepting Plaintiffs&#8217; alter ego theory. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;12, 2024, YPF filed a brief requesting that the District Court permanently enjoin Plaintiffs from pursuing recovery from YPF in connection with their September&#160;15, 2023 final judgment against the Republic, arguing that Plaintiffs&#8217; alter ego theory is barred under the doctrine of res judicata. Plaintiffs filed their opposition and YPF filed its reply. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On November&#160;15, 2024, the District Court stayed alter ego discovery from YPF, pending the Court&#8217;s consideration of supplemental briefing by YPF, the Republic and Plaintiffs on certain issues currently before the Court. The supplemental briefing was completed on January&#160;24, 2025. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF will continue to defend itself in accordance with the applicable legal procedures and available defenses. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company will continue to reassess the status of the litigation and its possible impact on the results and financial situation of the Group, as needed. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">34.b.3) Claims before the CNDC </div></div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div> <div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DisclosureOfMainRegulationsAndOtherRegulationsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_136338105" id="ixv-76714"> <div id="fin866694_42" style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36. MAIN REGULATIONS </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The main regulatory framework under which the Group carries on its business activities is described below. However, the purpose of this section is not to provide an exhaustive description of all the regulations governing the Group&#8217;s business. </div> <div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.a) Regulations applicable to the hydrocarbon industry </div></div> <div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.a.1) Hydrocarbons Law </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Law No.&#160;17,319 was enacted on June&#160;23, 1967, and along its effective term, it received numerous amendments, one of them was introduced in 2014 by Law No.&#160;27,007 (&#8220;Hydrocarbons Law&#8221;). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Hydrocarbons Law lays down the principles governing the exploration, exploitation, industrialization, transportation and commercialization of hydrocarbon resources in Argentina. Also, the Bases Law (see Note 36.j)) incorporated amendments to the Hydrocarbons Law. The most relevant aspects are as follows: </div> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Liquid and gaseous hydrocarbon reservoirs located in Argentine territory and its continental shelf belong to the Argentine Government or the provinces, depending on their territorial location. Activities related to hydrocarbon exploration, exploitation, industrialization, transportation and commercialization shall be undertaken by state-owned, private or mixed ownership companies, under the provisions of the Hydrocarbons Law and the regulations issued by the PEN. Also, these companies shall be registered with the Registry of Oil Companies created under SE Resolution No.&#160;407/2007, under which a technical and financial analysis of those companies is conducted on an annual basis. Companies not registered are not authorized to undertake activities in oilfields located in Argentine territory. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">The terms for exploration permits are set at each call for bids by the enforcement authority, according to the exploration objective: (i)&#160;permit for conventional exploration concessions, the term is divided into 2 periods of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfConventionalExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120330">3</ix:nonNumeric> years each, plus an optional extension of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfExtensionOfConventionalExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120331">5</ix:nonNumeric> years; (ii)&#160;permit for unconventional exploration, the term is divided into 2 periods of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfUnconventionalExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120332">4</ix:nonNumeric> years each, plus an optional extension of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfExtensionOfUnconventionalExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120333">5</ix:nonNumeric> years; and (iii)&#160;permit for exploration in continental shelf and territorial waters, the term is divided into 2 periods of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfContinentalShelfAndTerritorialWatersExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120334">3</ix:nonNumeric> years each, which may be extended for <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfExtensionOfContinentalShelfAndTerritorialWatersExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120335">1</ix:nonNumeric> year each. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">The terms for exploitation concessions, which shall run from the date the concession is awarded under the respective regulation, shall be as follows: (i)&#160;conventional exploitation concession: <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ConventionalExploitationConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120336">25</ix:nonNumeric> years; (ii)&#160;unconventional exploitation concession: <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:UnconventionalExploitationConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120337">35</ix:nonNumeric> years; and (iii)&#160;exploitation concession in continental shelf and territorial waters: <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ContinentalShelfAndTerritorialWaterConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120338">30</ix:nonNumeric> years. Additionally, holders of transportation concessions granted from the effective date of such decree and expansions of facility capacity in transportation concessions granted prior to such date and carried out thereafter, may ensure firm service capacity to shippers through capacity reservation contracts. These contracts may be freely negotiated regarding their allocation modality, prices and volumes. The uncontracted capacity and the unused contracted capacity shall be subject to the tariff to be approved by the enforcement authority. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

Also, it establishes that exploitation concessions and transportation concessions granted prior to the enactment of the Bases Law will continue under the legal figure of &#8220;concession&#8221; and governed until their expiration by the legal framework existing at the date of approval of the Bases Law. </div></td></tr></table> </ix:nonNumeric></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_136338105" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_1"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_2"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_3"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_4"><ix:exclude>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Decree No.&#160;1,057/2024 established the following distinction: (i)&#160;transportation concessions for holders of exploitation concessions; (ii)&#160;transportation concessions for <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-holders</div> of exploitation concessions; (iii)&#160;transportation authorizations for holders of exploitation concessions; (iv)&#160;transportation authorizations for <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-holders</div> of exploitation concessions; (v)&#160;transportation authorizations that are part of refining complexes and their related storage facilities; and (vi)&#160;transportation authorizations for owners of projects and/or facilities for the conditioning, separation, fractionation, liquefaction, and/or any other process of hydrocarbon industrialization. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Holders of exploration permits and exploitation concessions shall pay: (i)&#160;annually in advance, a fee per each square kilometer or fraction, according to the scale specified by the PEN; and (ii)&#160;a percentage between <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfAdvanceFee" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120346">12</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfAdvanceFee" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120347">18</ix:nonFraction>% of wellhead production of the liquid hydrocarbons extracted by way of royalty, allowing the national or provincial Executive Branch, as appropriate, and as grantors of such concessions, to reduce this rate up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageReductionInTheConcessionFee" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120348">5</ix:nonFraction>% considering the productivity, conditions and location of the wells. In addition, they are subject to federal, provincial and municipal taxes, customs duties on imports and exports, and, during the effective term of the exploration permit, to the tax regime established under the Hydrocarbons Law. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Decree No.&#160;1,057/2024 established that the free exercise of the right to export hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives may not be interrupted, nor be reviewed again once certain deadlines have passed, during the entire period or program of shipments or deliveries not objected to by the SE, and the requirements established in said decree must be complied with for this purpose, except in the event of exceptional circumstances which objectively compromise the security of supply in the domestic market. For those exports of hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives whose period or program of shipments or deliveries exceeds <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ProgramOfShipmentsOrDeliveriesTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2024To12_31_2024_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120350">1</ix:nonNumeric> year, the interested party must prove the right to dispose of the export volumes and in the deadlines committed. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">&#8201;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Likewise, it provided that the SE may object in whole or in part to the export of hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives, only based on the technical and/or economic reasons that affect the security of supply in the domestic market. Additionally, it establishes that the SE may object totally or partially to exports due to significant and unforeseen variations in the prices of hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives in the domestic market, on a temporary basis and until this situation has ended. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Through the Bases Law, hydrocarbon processing and natural gas storage activities are incorporated, for which the national or provincial Executive Branch, as applicable, may grant storage and/or processing authorizations. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Owners of projects and/or facilities for the conditioning, separation, fractionation, liquefaction and/or any other hydrocarbon industrialization process may request an authorization to transport hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives to their industrialization facilities and from them to subsequent industrialization or commercialization process centers and/or facilities. </div></td></tr></table> <div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

Under this amendment, the provinces were granted the primary control of natural resources within their territories. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">In 2007, Law No.&#160;26,197 recognized that hydrocarbon reservoirs, in compliance with Article 124 of the Argentine National Constitution (including reservoirs for which concessions were awarded prior to 1994) were owned by the provinces and granted them right to administer such reservoirs. </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.a.2) YPF Privatization Law </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 1992, Law No.&#160;24,145 (&#8220;Privatization Law&#8221;) privatized Yacimientos Petrol&#237;feros Fiscales Sociedad del Estado, YPF&#8217;s predecessor company, and decided the transfer of hydrocarbon fields from the Argentine Government to the provinces, subject to the existing rights of the holders of exploration permits and exploitation concessions. Under the Privatization Law, the Company was awarded exploration permits and exploitation concessions which are the original titles to numerous concessions that are currently operated by YPF. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.a.3) Hydrocarbon Unconventional Exploitation Concessions (&#8220;CENCH&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) in the Province of Neuqu&#233;n. </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;16, 2021, the Province of Nequ&#233;n published Decree No.&#160;2,183/2021 whereby approved Resolution No.&#160;53/2020, as amended by Resolution No.&#160;142/2021, which regulate the award of a CENCH in the province. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The aforementioned resolutions: (i)&#160;established the parameters applicable to the pilot plan to be submitted in order to apply for a CENCH and the technical criteria to define the territorial area of the CENCH; (ii)&#160;created the Area Extension Bonus for the area exceeding the pilot plan area; (iii)&#160;required the presentation of an annual update of a Continuous Development Plan during the mass production stage, and (iv)&#160;specified that commitments undertaken for the year following each presentation and update of the Continuous Development Plan should be firm commitments. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.b) Regulations applicable to the Downstream business segment </div></div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.b.1) Regulation related to liquid hydrocarbon exports </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Exports of crude oil, gasoline and diesel, among other goods, are subject to the registration provided for under Decree No.&#160;645/2002 and SRH Resolution No. <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">E-241/2017,</div> as amended by SSHyC Resolution No.&#160;329/2019. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In order to obtain an export permit, companies interested in exporting these products should enter export transactions in a register and ensure they have given the possibility of acquiring the products to interested potential domestic market agents. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;28, 2023, SE Resolution No.&#160;175/2023 was published in the BO, creating a special regime for the registration of crude petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals through cross-border crude oil pipelines. In order to obtain the export permit, entities will be required to prove to the SSHyC that the respective export does not affect domestic market supply. The permit shall indicate the export volume authorized for a minimum term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:MinimumTermForWhichTheExportVolumeShallBeAuthorized" contextRef="P03_28_2023To03_28_2023_LiquidHydrocarbonExportsMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120352">1</ix:nonNumeric> year from the date the permit was granted. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_12" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_13"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_13" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_14"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_14" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_15"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_15" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_16"><ix:exclude>

<td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">YPF SOCIEDAD ANONIMA</div></div></div></td>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_16" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_17"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_17" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_18"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Decree No.&#160;1,057/2024 (see Note 36.j)) provided that the SE shall keep a record of the export operations that were notified, those that were objected to, and those that were actually carried out. This decree establishes that, until its repeal or modification is ordered, exclusively with regard to the registration of such operations, Decree No.&#160;645/2002, SRH Resolution No. <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">E-241/2017</div> and its amendment Disposition No.&#160;329/2019 of the SSHyC, and Resolution SE No.&#160;175/2023 will continue to be applicable. In addition, it determines that the SE must make the corresponding regulatory adjustments for these and all other regulations referring to exports of hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives in order to comply with the objectives established in the Bases Law (see Note 36.j)) and the Hydrocarbons Law (see Note 36.a.1)). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, the provisions regulating the export of hydrocarbons and/or their derivatives are described in the Hydrocarbons Law (see Note 36.a.1)). </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.b.2) Refined products </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Resolution No.&#160;5/2016 issued by the former SRH, which replaced Annex II to SE Resolution No.&#160;1,283/2006, established specifications for grades 2 and 3 of diesel and gasoline, which include changes in the content of lead, manganese, oxygen and ethanol, and, more significantly, in relation to sulphur, demanding oil and gas companies to implement a plan to reduce sulphur limits to 50 mg/kg for gasoline grade 2, to 10 mg/kg for gasoline grade 3 and up to 350 mg/kg for diesel grade 2. In order to meet the new specifications, oil and gas companies had to submit to the enforcement authority a detailed schedule of the investment program for the following years. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Through SE Resolution No.&#160;576/2019, which modified former SRH Resolution No.&#160;5/2016, new specifications were established for gasoline grade 2 and diesel grade 2, and the deadline to meet these requirements regarding sulphur content in gasoline grade 2 was extended since January&#160;1, 2024. As of that date, the specifications that apply to gasoline grade 2 establish a maximum sulphur content of 50 mg/kg. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">However, through SE Resolution No.&#160;492/2023 a specific mechanism was established to defer the effective date of the specifications of SE Resolution No.&#160;576/2019 in accordance with the schedules detailed by each oil and gas company to reach the required specifications. In this sense, in relation to the detailed schedule of the investment program submitted by the Company, the enforcement authority decided to extend the deadline to comply with the specifications for gasoline grade 2 produced at the La Plata Industrial Complex until June&#160;30, 2024, and for diesel grade 2 produced at the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Industrial Complex until December&#160;31, 2025. Therefore, the Company is currently executing the last activities in compliance with the applicable resolution, having completed those related to the La Plata Industrial Complex. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.c) Regulations applicable to activities of the Gas and Power business segment </div></div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.c.1) Transportation, processing, storage, distribution and commercialization of natural gas </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Law No.&#160;24,076 (&#8220;Gas Law&#8221;), which was enacted in 1992, together with its Regulatory Decree No.&#160;1,738/1992, regulate natural gas public transportation and distribution services. Likewise, the Bases Law (see Note 36.j)) incorporated amendments to the Gas Law. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Gas Law also created the ENARGAS to administer and enforce the legal framework adopted for the transportation, distribution and commercialization of natural gas. The Bases Law created the &#8220;Ente Nacional Regulador del Gas y la Electricidad&#8221;, which will replace and assume the ENARGAS functions. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Natural gas transmission and distribution systems are divided into 2 main natural gas pipelines, the Northern and Southern systems, operated by transportation companies and 9 regional distribution companies. These systems operate under the open access principle, whereby natural gas suppliers have access to the available capacity without discrimination. Also, under the Gas Law, transportation companies are not allowed to buy or sell natural gas (with certain exceptions) and certain forms of cross-ownership among producers, transporters, distributors and sellers is forbidden. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The domestic wholesale demand of natural gas is divided into 4 segments: (i)&#160;priority demand supplied by distribution companies (residential demand and other <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">non-industrial</div> users, hereinafter the &#8220;Distribution&#8221;); (ii) thermoelectric generation; (iii)&#160;industrial demand; and (iv)&#160;compressed natural gas (&#8220;CNG&#8221;). </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_18" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_19"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_19" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_20"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_20" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_21"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_21" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_22"><ix:exclude>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="text-align:start; BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt;width:100%;border:0;margin:0 auto">

<td style="width:34%"/>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2024, 2023 AND 2022</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_22" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_23"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:ARIAL">(Amounts expressed in millions of United States dollars, except shares and per shares amounts expressed in United States dollars, and as otherwise indicated) </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">36.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_23" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_24"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding commercialization, the Gas Law provides that prices shall result from the free interaction of supply and demand and established the right to transfer the acquisition cost of natural gas to users of the distribution system. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">However, regulations applicable to natural gas commercialization were affected by the declaration of public emergency under Law No.&#160;25,561 enacted on January&#160;6, 2002 (&#8220;Public Emergency Law&#8221; of 2002), the financial crisis of 2001, the end of the convertibility regime and the freezing of transportation and distribution tariffs. Thus, a series of provisional decisions modified the pricing system and the volumes tendered, among which the following stand out: regulations seeking to establish agreements between producers and the SE to ensure offer volumes and an interim process for price reconversion; rules regulating natural gas dispatch to redirect injected natural gas and other mechanisms to ensure the supply of the priority demand (Distribution segment). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2017, after the Public Emergency Law of 2002 ceased to be effective, a transition process began for the supply of the Distribution segment, which comprised: calling upon producers and ENARSA to reach an agreement on the basic conditions (&#8220;Framework Agreement&#8221;) for the supply of natural gas effective from January&#160;1, 2018 to December&#160;31, 2019; establishing a mechanism for competitive bidding for the term April 2019 - March 2020 and the subsequent renewal (instructed by the SE) of the contracts resulting from the bidding process until the expiration of the term established in Article 5 of Law No.&#160;27,541 (the Solidarity Law declaring the public emergency of the energy sector). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">From January&#160;1, 2021, since the approval of the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 by Decree No.&#160;892/2020 (see Note 36.d.1)), the demand from the Distribution segment and most of the demand from the thermoelectric generation segment are duly supplied, and therefore, the prices received by producers supplying these segments are established through the bidding process provided for thereunder. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The sale of natural gas to the thermoelectric generation segment is regulated by former SE Resolution No.&#160;95/2013, Article 8, whose effectiveness was reestablished by Resolution No.&#160;12/2019 issued by Ministry of Productive Development, under which CAMMESA has provisionally been assigned the role to acquire and supply fuels without cost to generators which do not have natural gas supply contracts currently in force. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Also, sales to the industrial segment, as well as to the CNG segment (modified by Decree No.&#160;892/2020 and SE Resolution No.&#160;447/2020) are based on the free negotiation between producers or sellers and clients. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2024, through the Bases Law, regulated by Decree No.&#160;1,057/2024 (see Note 36.j)), the figure of &#8220;underground natural gas storage authorizations in depleted natural hydrocarbon reservoirs&#8221; was incorporated. Additionally, the possibility for holders of an underground natural gas storage permit to apply for a hydrocarbon transportation authorization was established. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Likewise, Decree No.&#160;1,057/2024 regulated the distinction of types of concessions, authorizations and transportation licenses, identifying natural gas transportation licenses and/or their extensions granted under the Gas Law. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, through the Bases Law (see Note 36.j)), the Hydrocarbons Law was amended incorporating the activities of processing and storage of natural gas, as described in Note 36.a.1). Likewise, the possibility to request authorization to transport hydrocarbons for owners of projects and/or facilities for the conditioning, separation, fractionation, liquefaction and/or any other hydrocarbon industrialization process. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_24" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_25"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_25" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_26"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%;clear:both"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_26" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_27"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_27" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_136338105_28"><ix:exclude>
